mobile-framework.summary: Verdict: React Native + Expo (SDK 57 now, SDK 58 when stable in ~Oct 2026), with Continuous Native Generation and hand-written Swift/Kotlin for the OS-surface targets. The deciding fact is that neither Flutter nor Kotlin Multiplatform removes the native work for the features that define this product: Flutter's live_activities (2.6.0) and home_widget (0.10.0) both require you to write the SwiftUI widget extension and Kotlin widget yourself, and Compose Multiplatform 1.11 (May 2026) has no WidgetKit/ActivityKit story at all, so Live Activities, Dynamic Island, WidgetKit, Glance, Wear OS tiles and watchOS complications are Swift/Kotlin regardless of framework. Expo is the only option that (a) keeps TypeScript end to end with the Cloudflare Workers backend and packages/shared, (b) has an officially stable path for iOS widgets + Live Activities (expo-widgets, stable since SDK 56, Android widgets in SDK 58 beta), (c) has a mature config-plugin route for arbitrary Apple targets including watch apps (@bacons/apple-targets 5.0.0, expo>=52) without ejecting, and (d) ships a web target for free via Expo Router. Legacy architecture is gone since SDK 55 (Feb 2026); Hermes v1 is default since SDK 56, and its reanimated memory regression was fixed in expo@57.0.9. Offline store: expo-sqlite + drizzle-orm useLiveQuery (change listener based) with a server-authoritative pull/cursor sync plus an outbox table; WatermelonDB (0.28.0) is broken on bridgeless RN and PowerSync is unnecessary machinery (and $49/mo Pro, FSL-licensed) for a server-is-truth model. Maps: @maplibre/maplibre-react-native 11.4.0 (New Architecture only, RN>=0.80) with OpenFreeMap tiles (free, unlimited, commercial OK) as Phase 0 default and Protomaps PMTiles on R2 (planet ~120 GB, ~$1.80/mo storage) as the owned fallback; MapLibre Native handles pmtiles:// natively. Push: raw APNs/FCM tokens from expo-notifications getDevicePushTokenAsync plus Live Activity tokens from the ActivityKit bridge, sent from Workers directly (APNs HTTP/2 + ES256 JWT via WebCrypto works in production Workers); Expo Push Service cannot drive Live Activities and is optional for plain notifications. Observability: @sentry/react-native with Expo plugin; product analytics Aptabase (AGPL server, MIT SDK, no device IDs, free 20k events, EU region) with Workers Analytics Engine for backend metrics. Web: Expo Router static output for the app shell in Phase 0, share pages stay Workers-served HTML.

findings.topic: Expo SDK / React Native current versions and cadence
findings.detail: Latest stable: expo@57.0.24 (SDK 57, released 2026-06-30) on React Native 0.86, React 19.2. SDK 56 (2026-05-21) RN 0.85; SDK 55 (2026-02-25) RN 0.83 and REMOVED Legacy Architecture ('you will not be able to use the Legacy Architecture in SDK 55 projects and later'). SDK 58 beta published 2026-09-15 on RN 0.88 RC; stable expected 3-4 weeks after RN 0.88 ships (likely Oct 2026). Cadence is ~3 majors/year (Feb, May/Jun, ~Oct). Hermes v1 is the default engine since SDK 56; it had a large memory regression when importing react-native-reanimated/worklets, fixed in expo@57.0.9 (RN 0.86.2); dev startup regression fixed in 57.0.17 (RN 0.86.3). SDK 55 required Xcode 26; SDK 57.0.23+ adds opt-in scene-based lifecycle (ios.enableSceneSupport) which iOS 27 SDK builds require; SDK 58 makes it required. Min deployment target: SDK 55 iOS 15.1 with bump to 16.4 planned for SDK 56; expo-widgets requires iOS 16.4+. SDK 58 beta also: Expo Router SSR/data loaders/middleware/native tabs stable; expo-sqlite libSQL sync REMOVED; expo-notifications foreground display default, threadIdentifier grouping, Android setAlarmClock delivery; RN Strict TypeScript API default; File.write() async.

findings.topic: EAS Build / Submit / Update pricing (expo.dev/pricing, Sept 2026)
findings.detail: Free: $0, 15 Android + 15 iOS builds/month, low priority, 1 concurrency, 45-min timeout, EAS Update 1,000 MAU, 100 GiB bandwidth, no overage possible. Starter: $19/mo + usage, $45 build credit, high priority, 1 concurrency (+$50 each, up to 5), 2-hour timeout, 3,000 MAU. Production: $199/mo + usage, $225 build credit, 2 concurrency, 50,000 MAU, 1 TiB bandwidth. Enterprise: custom, $1,000+ credit, 5 concurrency, 1M+ MAU. Per-build overage on paid plans: Android medium $1, Android large $2, iOS medium $2, iOS large $4. EAS Update MAU overage $0.005 tiered down to $0.00085; bandwidth $0.10/GiB. EAS Submit included on all plans; seats unlimited. Practical read: Starter covers Phase 0 (~22 iOS-medium builds/month on the $45 credit) and the 2-hour timeout matters once MapLibre + Swift targets are compiled; Free plan's 45-min limit is a real risk with native targets.

findings.topic: expo-widgets (official) for iOS WidgetKit + Live Activities
findings.detail: expo-widgets 57.0.20 (MIT). Alpha in SDK 55 (2026-03-04 blog), promoted to STABLE for iOS in SDK 56 (2026-06-18 blog). Widgets/Live Activities are React components marked with a 'widget' directive that compile to a separate JS bundle executed by a JSC runtime inside the Widget Extension and mapped onto SwiftUI via @expo/ui/swift-ui primitives only (no hooks, no app state, no async inside 'widget' functions). CNG config plugin generates the Widget Extension target, App Group (groupIdentifier), entitlements, and SwiftUI scaffolding; requires dev builds (not Expo Go). Live Activity API: start(props, url?), update(props), end(dismissalPolicy, props?, contentDate?), getInstances(), getPushToken(), addPushTokenListener(), addPushToStartTokenListener() (iOS 17.2+); config enablePushNotifications: true; staleDate + stable ActivityKit identifiers added in 57.x/58; frequent updates need NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates. Widget families: systemSmall/Medium/Large/ExtraLarge, accessoryCircular/Rectangular/Inline. Images via shared widgetsDirectory in the App Group; ChartView added in SDK 57. Android: 'initial Android package and config plugin' appears in the sdk-57 changelog; SDK 58 beta: Android widgets run their own JS bundle on a dedicated Hermes runtime with interactions and Material colors (i.e. Android is beta-new as of Sept 2026). Min iOS 16.4. Software Mansion's expo-live-activity was ARCHIVED 2026-06-01 with a pointer to expo-widgets.

findings.topic: @bacons/apple-targets (Evan Bacon) for arbitrary Apple targets incl. watchOS
findings.detail: @bacons/apple-targets 5.0.0, MIT, peer expo>=52, 1.4k stars. Config plugin that generates native Xcode targets during `npx expo prebuild --clean` from a top-level targets/ directory (virtual expo:targets folder in Xcode), so the /ios directory stays uncommitted (no eject). 30+ target types: widget, watch, watch-widget (complications), clip, app-intent, share, notification-service, notification-content, intent, spotlight, action, safari, keyboard, etc. Unsupported: TV Top Shelf, Finder Sync, Mail. App Groups + entitlements declared in expo-target.config.js; ships an ExtensionStorage native module for App Group NSUserDefaults. You write the SwiftUI yourself (full ActivityKit/WidgetKit fidelity, no runtime in the extension). Requirements: Expo SDK 53+, CocoaPods 1.16.2+, Xcode 16+, macOS 15. Known limitations: App Clip signing automation incomplete; expo-updates breaks App Clip builds. Used by the Expo blog's own widget tutorial as the predecessor path. Coexistence of apple-targets-generated targets with the expo-widgets-generated extension in one project is NOT verified.

findings.topic: Other widget/extension plugins evaluated
findings.detail: expo-targets (csark0812) 1.9.2, MIT: Apple targets (share, action, App Clips, iMessage, widgets, notification extensions) AND Android widgets as first-class Glance/Compose in a target folder, data sharing via App Groups (iOS) / SharedPreferences (Android); 'tested on Expo SDK 57'; younger and single-maintainer; Android share/action carry stability caveats. react-native-android-widget 0.22.1 (MIT, optional peer expo>=54, New Architecture supported): JSX rendered to RemoteViews (not Glance), Expo config plugin, configurable widgets. expo-android-glance-widget (akshayjadhav4): experimental. react-native-widget-extension and @bittingz/expo-widgets: not evaluated in depth; superseded by expo-widgets. Verdict: for Android, write Glance in Kotlin inside a local Expo Module (or expo-targets), since the ongoing notification and Wear OS work are Kotlin anyway.

findings.topic: Live Activities via APNs push (start/update/end, push-to-start)
findings.detail: Headers: apns-push-type: liveactivity; apns-topic: <bundleId>.push-type.liveactivity; apns-priority: 10 (or 5). Payload aps.event ∈ {start, update, end}; start requires attributes-type + attributes + content-state (optional alert); update carries content-state; end carries dismissal-date; stale-date supported; timestamp required. Push-to-start tokens come from Activity.pushToStartTokenUpdates (iOS 17.2+) and require token-based (p8/ES256) APNs auth; per-activity update tokens from activity.pushTokenUpdates. iOS 18+ supports broadcast channels ('channel' field) so many devices tracking one flight can be updated with one push, which maps directly onto the one-FlightTracker-DO-per-flight design. Apple applies an update budget; frequent-updates entitlement flag is Info.plist NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates. Cloudflare Workers can call APNs directly: Workers fetch speaks HTTP/2 to origin (workerd issue #4841 confirms APNs works in production Workers even though local macOS dev failed), ES256 JWT via WebCrypto, and a Workers-friendly client exists (@fivesheepco/cloudflare-apns2).

findings.topic: Data sharing between RN app and extensions
findings.detail: iOS: App Groups (group.<bundleId>) with shared NSUserDefaults (expo-widgets configures groupIdentifier automatically; apple-targets exposes ExtensionStorage) and a shared container directory for images (expo-widgets widgetsDirectory). A shared SQLite file in the App Group container is possible but neither official package documents it; recommend a small JSON snapshot ('next flight' + activity content-state) written by the app and read by the extension, never a shared DB, because widget extensions run under tight memory/time budgets. Android: SharedPreferences / a small file for Glance state (expo-targets uses SharedPreferences) plus WorkManager for refresh; Wear OS via the Data Layer API (DataClient/MessageClient).

findings.topic: Wear OS and watchOS with Expo
findings.detail: React Native does not run on Wear OS or watchOS; both companions must be native. watchOS: @bacons/apple-targets 'watch' + 'watch-widget' target types generate the Watch App and complication targets from targets/ (SwiftUI); communication via WatchConnectivity (react-native-watch-connectivity or a small local Expo Module); 2026 guides exist for Expo + Apple Watch. Wear OS: add a Kotlin/Compose-for-Wear-OS + Tiles Gradle module to the Android project via a config plugin (withSettingsGradle include + withAppBuildGradle wearApp dependency); this pattern is from memory and not verified against an official Expo doc; communication via react-native-wear-connectivity 0.1.17 (MIT, DataLayer/MessageClient bridge) or a local Expo Module. No Expo 'wearOS target' abstraction exists. Wear OS minimum target API 34 since 2025-08-31.

findings.topic: Flutter comparison
findings.detail: Flutter 3.41 (Feb 2026); Impeller default, Skia opt-out deprecated in 3.38. live_activities 2.6.0 (verified publisher, 654 likes, 150 pub points): iOS 16.1+, push tokens and push-to-start (17.2+), Android RemoteViews beta; but 'it's not currently possible to only use Flutter': you must author the Widget Extension + ActivityAttributes struct in Swift and Kotlin RemoteViews XML. home_widget 0.10.0 (2.2k likes, 193k downloads): data bridge only, 'does not allow writing Widgets with Flutter itself'. Wear OS apps possible via wear_plus; watchOS is an explicit Flutter non-goal. Net: same native surface area as Expo, minus TypeScript sharing with the Workers backend, minus an equivalent to expo-widgets, and a Dart web build that is not suitable for the SEO-relevant web surface.

findings.topic: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform comparison
findings.detail: Compose Multiplatform for iOS stable since 1.8.0 (May 2025); 1.10.0 (Jan 2026) common @Preview, Navigation 3, Compose Hot Reload; 1.11.0 (May 2026) experimental native UIView text input, concurrent rendering default. No WidgetKit/ActivityKit/watchOS story in any release; widgets and Live Activities are SwiftUI written in Xcode, with shared Kotlin models exported via SKIE (Swift Export still alpha). Requires a Kotlin/Gradle toolchain, a second language for the backend boundary, and web via Wasm that is not production-grade for an SEO-facing site. Verdict: strongest of the three for shared business logic, weakest fit for a TypeScript-everywhere monorepo with a Workers backend and a small team.

findings.topic: Offline-first store options
findings.detail: expo-sqlite (SDK 57): sync+async APIs, prepared statements, tagged-template sql, withExclusiveTransactionAsync, enableChangeListener:true + addDatabaseChangeListener(), createSessionAsync() changesets (SQLite session extension), SQLCipher via useSQLCipher, FTS toggle, kv-store (AsyncStorage-compatible), web support alpha (WASM + COOP/COEP); libSQL sync removed in SDK 58. drizzle-orm has native expo-sqlite driver with useLiveQuery since v0.31.1 (re-runs on change listener; requires enableChangeListener). op-sqlite 18.2.4 (MIT, JSI, Expo plugin, sqlcipher/libsql options, fastest raw throughput) is a drop-in alternative if expo-sqlite performance is insufficient. WatermelonDB 0.28.0 (MIT, 11.8k stars) devDeps pin RN 0.74.6; its native layer grabs RCTCxxBridge internals that do not exist in bridgeless mode and RN 0.82+ removed the bridge, so it is a dead end for SDK 55+. PowerSync: Free 2 GB synced/mo, 500 MB hosted, 50 concurrent clients, projects deactivate after 1 idle week; Pro from $49/mo with 30 GB synced, 1,000 peak concurrent clients then $30 per 1,000; self-host Open Edition is FSL (source-available), Enterprise self-host for write checkpoints. For a server-authoritative model PowerSync's sync-rules engine and 1,000-concurrent-client pricing unit are cost and complexity without benefit.

findings.topic: MapLibre React Native status
findings.detail: @maplibre/maplibre-react-native 11.4.0 (2026-09-19, MIT), peer react-native >=0.80.0, New Architecture ONLY from v11 (v11.0.0 announced in the April 2026 MapLibre newsletter; API overhauled to match MapLibre GL JS with style-spec paint/layout props on a unified Layer). v11.4.0 bumps MapLibre Native to 13.6.1 Android / 6.31.0 iOS; Android minSdk 23; Expo config plugin (dev build required). Patch cadence is high (11.3.8 to 11.4.0 in 19 days) which signals both activity and churn. MapLibre Native handles pmtiles://https://... sources natively on Android (11.7.0+) and iOS with no extra code, but PMTiles sources do not participate in offline packs. Web: use maplibre-gl directly behind a platform-split component.

findings.topic: Tile providers and costs
findings.detail: OpenFreeMap: public instance free, no request limits, no API key, commercial use explicitly allowed, styles Positron/Bright/Liberty/Dark/Fiord3D, weekly planet builds for self-host, funded by GitHub Sponsors (single maintainer). Protomaps self-hosted: planet basemap ~120 GB PMTiles (z0-15, daily/weekly builds), served from R2 via the official Worker; R2 $0.015/GB-month (=~$1.80/mo for the planet), Class B $0.36/M, egress free; Workers Paid $5/mo incl. 10M requests then $0.30/M; R2 latency on cache miss 500 ms+ (put a custom domain in front for cache). MapTiler: Free 5k sessions/100k requests non-commercial with logo; Flex $30/mo 25k sessions, overage $2.50/1k sessions. Stadia: Free 200k credits non-commercial; Starter $20/mo 1M credits, +3c/1k. Cheapest viable: OpenFreeMap now, Protomaps-on-R2 as the owned fallback (~$7/mo all-in) when uptime or attribution control matters; expect to switch the style URL only.

findings.topic: State and data libraries
findings.detail: @tanstack/react-query 5.102.8 (Sept 2026, active weekly releases) for server state with persistence to expo-sqlite/kv-store; zustand 5.0.15 (~1 KB) for client/UI state (prefs, units, quiet hours). No Redux, no MobX, no Jotai needed. Pattern: TanStack Query owns network cache + retries + focus refetch; drizzle useLiveQuery owns the durable local flight/trip tables; zustand owns ephemeral UI state.

findings.topic: Push notifications architecture
findings.detail: expo-notifications: getDevicePushTokenAsync() returns the raw APNs (iOS) / FCM (Android) token ('can be used with another push notification service'); getExpoPushTokenAsync() returns an ExponentPushToken for Expo Push Service (600 notifications/s/project, 100 per request, 4,096-byte payload, ttl/priority/channelId/interruptionLevel; no Live Activity support). Background data handling via expo-task-manager with _contentAvailable. @react-native-firebase/messaging 26.4.0 (Apache-2.0, New Architecture required from v26, Expo config plugin, optional peer expo>=47) gives getAPNSToken() and setBackgroundMessageHandler but requires the Firebase SDK in the binary and conflicts with other handlers. Recommendation: expo-notifications for permissions/display/channels, store BOTH device token (APNs/FCM) and, optionally, the Expo token per device row; Workers backend sends via a PushSender interface with adapters {apns-direct (ES256 JWT, WebCrypto), fcm-v1 (service-account OAuth JWT), expo-push}; Live Activity start/update/end MUST go apns-direct with liveactivity push type. Do not add react-native-firebase unless FCM analytics/other Firebase products are wanted (privacy-first argues against).

findings.topic: Sentry and product analytics
findings.detail: Sentry: @sentry/react-native with the @sentry/react-native/expo config plugin (Expo SDK 50+), getSentryExpoConfig for Debug IDs, source maps auto-uploaded during EAS builds, mobileReplayIntegration, Expo Router navigation tracing; sendDefaultPii opt-in. Pricing: Developer free 5k errors/50 replays/5M spans, Team $26/mo (annual) 50k errors. Aptabase: free 20k events/mo, $10/mo 200k up to $450/mo 50M, no overage (pauses), server AGPL-3.0 / SDKs MIT, @aptabase/react-native, never collects device/advertising IDs, EU region eu.aptabase.com, 5-year retention. PostHog: 1M events free/mo, EU cloud, but self-hosting is 'officially unsupported' and recommended only under ~300k events/mo. Workers Analytics Engine: Workers Paid includes 10M data points/mo (+$0.25/M) and 1M queries (+$1/M), Free 100k points/day; limits 250 points per invocation, 20 blobs + 20 doubles + 1 index (<=96 B) per point, 16 KB blobs per point, 3-month retention, currently not billed. Umami is web-pageview oriented; not verified for RN. Recommendation: Sentry (both mobile + Workers), Aptabase for app product events (own-able, anonymous, cheap), Analytics Engine for backend/provider-cost metrics.

findings.topic: Web target
findings.detail: Expo Router web supports output single | static | server. static pre-renders routes to HTML (generateStaticParams for dynamic routes, <Head/> for SEO) and deploys to any static host including Cloudflare; API routes (+api.ts) are stable but need server output and are CommonJS-only/no dynamic imports; EAS Hosting runs on Cloudflare Workers (custom domain on paid plans). SDK 58 promotes SSR, data loaders and middleware to stable and enables async route chunks on web by default. expo-sqlite on web is alpha (WASM, needs COOP/COEP). Recommendation for Phase 0: one Expo Router codebase with web output 'static', deployed as Workers static assets under app.<domain>; no API routes (the Hono Worker is the API); share pages remain Workers-served HTML in apps/api; on web replace the SQLite layer with TanStack Query persistence (no offline requirement on web).

mobile-framework.recommendation:
FRAMEWORK: React Native + Expo SDK 57 (upgrade to SDK 58 as soon as stable, before any App Store submission, because iOS 27 SDK builds require the scene-based lifecycle that SDK 58 makes default). Why: the hard, differentiating surfaces (Live Activity/Dynamic Island, WidgetKit, Glance, Wear tile, watch complication) are Swift/Kotlin in ALL three frameworks; Flutter's live_activities/home_widget and KMP/Compose 1.11 give you nothing there, whereas Expo gives you CNG (targets generated at prebuild, /ios and /android never committed), an official stable expo-widgets path, apple-targets for the watch target, TypeScript shared with the Workers backend (zod schemas for API, Live Activity content-state, sync envelopes in packages/shared), and a free web target. New Architecture is not a decision any more (legacy removed in SDK 55).

iOS LIVE ACTIVITY + WIDGETS: Default to hand-written SwiftUI in a targets/widget target generated by @bacons/apple-targets 5.0.0, plus a ~150-line local Expo Module (modules/activitykit, Swift) exposing start/update/end, activity.pushTokenUpdates, Activity.pushToStartTokenUpdates and App Group snapshot writes. Rationale: this matches the mandate ('native modules required regardless: Swift'), keeps the extension free of a JS runtime under WidgetKit's memory budget, gives Flighty-grade Dynamic Island fidelity, and apple-targets is 3 years old at v5 vs expo-widgets stable for 3 months. Run a 2-day spike on expo-widgets in Phase 1; if it renders the Live Activity design acceptably, it can replace the hand-written extension since the push contract (APNs content-state) is identical either way. Do not mix both in Phase 0 (coexistence unverified).

ANDROID: local Expo Module (Kotlin) modules/android-surfaces with a Glance widget, the ongoing notification, and a WorkManager refresh; Wear OS as a separate Gradle module (Compose for Wear OS + Tiles) included by a config plugin, talking Data Layer to the phone app. Skip react-native-android-widget (RemoteViews, not Glance) and expo-widgets Android (beta in SDK 58).

OFFLINE STORE: expo-sqlite + drizzle-orm (useLiveQuery with enableChangeListener) in apps/mobile, schema in packages/shared alongside the Neon/Drizzle server schema so types line up. Sync: server-authoritative pull with a per-user cursor (GET /sync?since=<cursor> returning upserts+tombstones for trips, flights, flight_states, prefs), applied in one exclusive transaction; a client outbox table (id, op, payload, attempts, created_at) drained by a TanStack mutation with idempotency keys; server wins on conflict, client keeps last-known state for display. No PowerSync, no WatermelonDB. op-sqlite is the swap-in if profiling shows expo-sqlite too slow (unlikely at this data volume).

MAPS: @maplibre/maplibre-react-native 11.4.0 with OpenFreeMap 'liberty'/'dark' style URLs behind a single MAP_STYLE_URL config; Protomaps PMTiles on R2 (~$7/mo) ready as fallback; MapLibre GL JS on web via platform-split component. No Google Maps SDK anywhere.

STATE: @tanstack/react-query 5.x + zustand 5.x; persist query cache to expo-sqlite/kv-store.

PUSH: expo-notifications for permission/channels/display; store raw APNs/FCM device tokens plus Live Activity update and push-to-start tokens in Postgres (device_push_tokens with kind ∈ {apns, fcm, expo, la_update, la_push_to_start}); Workers PushSender interface with apns-direct (ES256 via WebCrypto, HTTP/2 fetch), fcm-v1 and expo-push adapters; Live Activities always apns-direct; use iOS 18 broadcast channels later for one-push-per-flight fan-out.

OBSERVABILITY: @sentry/react-native + Expo plugin on mobile, Sentry on Workers; Aptabase for product analytics (anonymous, AGPL server if self-host later); Workers Analytics Engine for provider-cost and refresh metrics.

WEB: Expo Router web output static in the same app, deployed to Workers static assets; share pages stay Workers HTML.

PHASE 0 SCAFFOLD (empty shells, compile in CI): apps/mobile (Expo SDK 57, TypeScript, expo-router, CNG, app.config.ts with bundle ids, App Group group.<bundleId>, aps-environment, NSSupportsLiveActivities + FrequentUpdates, UIBackgroundModes remote-notification); apps/mobile/targets/widget (apple-targets 'widget': placeholder WidgetKit widget + ActivityAttributes with the shared content-state schema); apps/mobile/targets/watch + targets/watch-widget (apple-targets: empty SwiftUI watch app + complication); apps/mobile/modules/activitykit (local Expo Module, Swift); apps/mobile/modules/android-surfaces (local Expo Module, Kotlin: Glance widget + ongoing notification stub); apps/mobile/wear (Kotlin Compose for Wear OS + Tiles module, wired by plugins/withWearApp.ts config plugin); apps/mobile/plugins/ (config plugins under test); expo-sqlite + drizzle schema + migration runner; eas.json with development/preview/production profiles and EAS Starter plan; packages/shared with zod contracts including LiveActivityContentState and SyncEnvelope; apps/api push/ module with the PushSender interface and an APNs adapter test using a fake HTTP/2 endpoint. CI: typecheck + vitest on packages/shared and apps/api (vitest-pool-workers), Expo `expo prebuild --clean` + `xcodebuild`/`gradle assembleDebug` smoke on a nightly EAS build to prove the native targets still generate.
risks: Expo ships ~3 majors/year and dropped legacy arch in SDK 55; every third-party native lib (MapLibre v11 NA-only, RNFirebase v26 NA-only) must track it. Budget one upgrade sprint per SDK; pin exact versions and use `npx expo install --check` in CI.

iOS 27 SDK builds require scene-based lifecycle (SDK 57.0.23+ opt-in, SDK 58 default); Apple will eventually require the iOS 27 SDK for submissions, forcing the SDK 58 upgrade on Apple's timeline, not yours.
Hermes v1 (default since SDK 56) had a serious memory regression with reanimated until expo@57.0.9; expect further engine-level regressions in 58.

expo-widgets has been 'stable' on iOS only since June 2026 and Android is beta in SDK 58; the hand-written SwiftUI/apple-targets path avoids that risk but apple-targets is a single-maintainer project (Evan Bacon, Expo employee) and coexistence with expo-widgets in the same project is unverified.

WidgetKit/ActivityKit extensions have tight memory budgets and Apple applies an undocumented Live Activity update budget; a 2-minute refresh cadence boarding-to-landing must use apns-priority 5 for non-urgent updates and reserve priority 10 for gate/delay changes, or activities will be throttled.

Wear OS and watchOS are 100% native Kotlin/Swift with no Expo abstraction; the Gradle-module-via-config-plugin pattern for Wear is community practice, not an Expo-documented feature (unverified from memory), and will need a maintained config plugin in-repo.

OpenFreeMap is a donation-funded single-maintainer public instance with no SLA; keep the Protomaps-on-R2 fallback deployable (R2 cache-miss latency 500 ms+; PMTiles sources cannot be bundled into MapLibre offline packs).
maplibre-react-native v11 was a full API rewrite in April 2026 with frequent patch releases; expect breaking patch behaviour and thin Stack Overflow coverage.
WatermelonDB is effectively dead on bridgeless RN; any 'boring' advice recommending it is stale. expo-sqlite web is alpha, so web must not depend on the SQLite layer.
EAS Free plan's 45-minute build timeout and 15 iOS builds/month will be exceeded once Swift targets + MapLibre are compiled; Starter ($19 + usage) is the realistic floor.

Direct APNs from Workers depends on Workers' HTTP/2 origin support which is confirmed in production but fails in local workerd on macOS; Live Activity push tests must run against a fake endpoint in Miniflare and a real device in staging.

Expo Push Service cannot start or update Live Activities, so a pure-Expo-push design is impossible for this product; the APNs adapter is mandatory from Phase 0 even if plain notifications go through Expo Push.
Workers Analytics Engine is 3-month retention and not yet billed; long-lived provider-cost history needs periodic export to R2/Postgres.
open_decisions_for_owner: Live Activity UI implementation: hand-written SwiftUI via @bacons/apple-targets + local ActivityKit Expo Module (recommended default) vs official expo-widgets (JS-defined, @expo/ui primitives, JSC runtime in the extension). Decide after a Phase 1 spike; Phase 0 scaffolds the apple-targets path.
Whether to adopt Expo SDK 58 during Phase 0 (RN 0.88 RC today; stable expected ~Oct 2026) or freeze on 57.0.x until Phase 1. Recommendation: start on 57, upgrade in the first week 58 is stable.

Expo Push Service as an additional notification transport (simplifies FCM credential handling, adds an Expo dependency and a data processor) vs apns-direct + fcm-v1 only (privacy-first, one less vendor). Live Activities are apns-direct either way.

Product analytics vendor: Aptabase cloud ($10/mo at 200k events, EU region) vs self-hosting Aptabase (AGPL) vs PostHog cloud (1M free events but heavier SDK and identity model). Privacy posture argues for Aptabase.
Tile strategy: OpenFreeMap public instance (free, no SLA) vs owning Protomaps PMTiles on R2 (~$7/mo, 120 GB weekly refresh job) from day one.

Whether to scaffold the Wear OS module and watchOS target in Phase 0 as empty shells (recommended, so App Group ids, bundle ids, provisioning profiles and CI build matrix account for them) or defer until Phase 5-6 and accept a later re-provisioning cost.
EAS plan: Starter ($19 + usage) for Phase 0-1 vs Production ($199) once two developers are producing daily builds; and whether to keep macOS runners for a self-hosted CI fallback.

Android widget authoring path: Kotlin Glance in a local Expo Module (recommended, aligns with Wear/ongoing-notification Kotlin work) vs expo-targets Glance target vs waiting for expo-widgets Android (SDK 58 beta).
SQLCipher for the on-device DB (expo-sqlite useSQLCipher) given email-derived itinerary data on device: cost is ~1-2 MB binary and key management; recommend yes for Pro-tier email sync data.
alternatives_rejected: Flutter: identical native workload for Live Activities/widgets (live_activities 2.6.0 and home_widget 0.10.0 both require hand-written Swift/Kotlin), no watchOS (explicit non-goal), Dart breaks TypeScript-everywhere and shared zod contracts with the Workers backend, weaker SEO web story.

Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform 1.11: strong shared-logic story but zero WidgetKit/ActivityKit/watch abstraction, Swift Export still alpha (SKIE needed), Gradle/Kotlin toolchain for a TS backend team, Wasm web not production-appropriate for an SEO surface.
Bare React Native without Expo: loses CNG, config plugins, EAS, Expo Router web, expo-widgets/apple-targets; every native target becomes committed Xcode/Gradle state to maintain by hand.
WatermelonDB: native layer depends on RCTCxxBridge/bridge internals removed in RN 0.82+, devDeps pinned to RN 0.74.6; unusable on SDK 55+.

PowerSync: designed for client-authoritative/bidirectional sync with sync rules; adds a service ($49/mo Pro, FSL-licensed self-host) and a 1,000-concurrent-client pricing unit for a model where the server is the source of truth and client writes are a small outbox.
react-native-android-widget: renders JSX to RemoteViews, not Glance; the brief requires Glance and the Kotlin surface is needed anyway for ongoing notification + Wear tile.
software-mansion-labs/expo-live-activity: archived 2026-06-01, fixed-layout config model, points users to expo-widgets.

@react-native-firebase/messaging as the push layer: requires the Firebase SDK in the binary, conflicts with other notification handlers, and expo-notifications already exposes raw APNs/FCM device tokens; FCM v1 HTTP can be called from Workers without the client SDK.
Google Maps SDK / Mapbox: SDK billing and per-MAU pricing; MapLibre + OpenFreeMap/Protomaps is free-to-cheap and fully swappable by style URL.
PostHog self-hosted: officially unsupported and recommended only under ~300k events/month; Umami is web-pageview oriented (unverified for RN).

Separate web framework (Next.js etc.) for the logged-in web app in Phase 0: Expo Router static output already yields the same screens; share pages are Workers HTML regardless, so a second frontend is pure duplication at this stage.

cloudflare-backend.summary: Verified as of 2026-09-19 against Cloudflare, Neon, Sentry, Hono and npm primary sources. The Cloudflare stack proposed in the brief is viable on a single Workers Paid account ($5/mo minimum) with Durable Objects, Hyperdrive, Queues, Workflows, KV, R2, Analytics Engine, Cron, rate-limit binding, Email Routing and Access all available; only Email Service sending is still beta. Durable Objects: SQLite-backed, 10 GB per object on Paid, ~1,000 req/s soft cap per object, one alarm per object with at-least-once execution and up to 6 exponential-backoff retries, RPC methods on stubs, deterministic idFromName/getByName, and no production enumeration API (a Postgres registry is mandatory). The DO lifecycle declaration has moved from the `migrations` array to a new `exports` field; a greenfield repo should adopt `exports` from day one. The vitest integration has been renamed from @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers to @cloudflare/vitest-plugin (v1.1.13, requires Vitest 4.1) and exposes runDurableObjectAlarm, runInDurableObject, listDurableObjectIds, getQueueResult and per-file isolated storage; Vitest fake timers do not drive DO alarms or KV expiry, so FlightTracker needs an injectable clock. Hyperdrive is included at no charge (unlimited queries on Paid), pools in transaction mode near the origin, caches SELECTs for 60 s by default with no write invalidation, and works with Neon's direct connection string; Neon Launch is pure usage pricing ($0.106/CU-hr, $0.35/GB-mo, 10 branches included then $1.50/branch-mo). Verdict: Neon over D1; D1's 10 GB hard cap, SQLite dialect lock-in (schema and query rewrite under Drizzle), export that blocks the DB, and read replication still in public beta make a later migration materially expensive. Two notable gotchas for Phase 0: Workers Builds does not generate preview URLs for Workers that export Durable Objects, and Email Service sending starts new accounts on an undisclosed conservative daily quota, which threatens magic-link delivery at launch.

findings.topic: Durable Objects: pricing
findings.detail: Workers Paid: 1M requests/mo included then $0.15/M; duration 400,000 GB-s/mo included then $12.50/M GB-s; SQLite rows read 25B/mo included then $0.001/M; rows written 50M/mo included then $1.00/M; stored data 5 GB-mo included then $0.20/GB-mo. Free plan: 100k req/day, 13,000 GB-s/day, 5M row reads/day, 100k row writes/day, 5 GB total. Alarm invocations count as requests; each setAlarm() is billed as one row write. Hibernation-eligible objects do not accrue duration. Worked estimate (derived, not vendor-verified): a flight tracked from 30 days out on the mandated cadence fires roughly 200-210 alarms (23 daily + 5 daily 7d..48h + 45 hourly + 15 at 10-min + ~105 at 2-min for a 3.5h flight + ~12 post-arrival), i.e. ~205 DO requests, ~600 row writes and ~5 GB-s per flight; at 100k tracked flights/month that is ~20.5M requests (~$3), ~60M row writes (~$10 over included), ~0.5M GB-s (~$1.25 over included).

findings.topic: Durable Objects: limits
findings.detail: SQLite storage 10 GB per object (Paid) / 1 GB (Free); unlimited objects and unlimited per-account SQLite storage on Paid; 500 DO classes per account (Paid); soft throughput ~1,000 req/s per object before overloaded errors (best-practice page says plan for 500-1,000 rps); key+value 2 MB in SQLite storage; CPU 30 s default per request, configurable to 5 min via cpu_ms; alarm handler wall time 15 min; 6 simultaneous outgoing connections per request. RPC serialized payload limit 32 MiB (use ReadableStream beyond). blockConcurrencyWhile has a 30 s timeout and throttles to ~200 rps, so reserve it for constructor schema init.

findings.topic: Durable Objects: alarms semantics
findings.detail: Exactly one alarm per object; setAlarm(scheduledTimeMs) overrides any existing alarm; getAlarm() returns null while the alarm handler is running unless setAlarm was called inside it; deleteAlarm() unsets. Guaranteed at-least-once; if alarm() throws it is retried with exponential backoff starting at 2 s, up to 6 retries; alarm(alarmInfo) receives {retryCount, isRetry}. ctx.abort({retryAlarm}) controls whether an interrupted alarm retries. Docs mandate idempotent alarm handlers. Known issue: alarms may fail after a hot reload in wrangler dev (restart dev server). Objects hibernate after ~10 s idle and are evicted after 70-140 s idle; alarms wake them; no shutdown hook, persist incrementally. Alarm precision / minimum interval: not documented (unverified, from memory: alarms are not sub-second precise; 2-min cadence is safe).

findings.topic: Durable Objects: RPC, naming, enumeration, DO-to-DO
findings.detail: With compatibility_date >= 2024-04-03 public methods on a DurableObject subclass are callable as RPC on the stub (async, serializable args/returns, exceptions propagate without stack traces); docs prefer RPC over fetch(). Namespace API: idFromName(name) deterministic, newUniqueId() random (lower first-use latency), idFromString, getByName(name, {locationHint}), get(id, {locationHint}), jurisdiction(). There is NO API to list or enumerate objects in production (listDurableObjectIds exists only in the vitest plugin and respects per-file isolation), so a registry table in Postgres keyed by the DO name is required. DO-to-DO calls: a DO receives env bindings and can call other DO stubs via env (invoke-methods page returned 404 during this run; behaviour confirmed by rules page guidance to always await RPC calls and by the base-class docs exposing this.env). Rules page: one object per coordination atom, avoid global singletons, persist state before non-storage I/O, use optimistic locking around fetch() interleaving, make alarms idempotent, call an explicit init() because objects do not know their own name. Code rollouts are gradual: a new Worker may call an old DO version for seconds to minutes, keep DO RPC APIs backward compatible across deploys.

findings.topic: Durable Objects: SQLite storage API
findings.detail: ctx.storage.sql.exec(query, ...bindings) returns SqlStorageCursor with next/toArray/one/raw, columnNames, rowsRead, rowsWritten (billing counters usable for cost logging). Consume cursors synchronously before the next await for snapshot isolation. ctx.storage.transactionSync(cb) for atomic sync work. Both sync KV (ctx.storage.kv.*) and async KV APIs exist on SQLite objects (hidden __cf_kv table). Point-in-time recovery: getCurrentBookmark/getBookmarkForTime (30 days)/onNextSessionRestoreBookmark. Indexes, ALTER, FTS5, JSON supported; databaseSize property. int64 loses precision past 2^53. Best practice: create tables in constructor inside blockConcurrencyWhile, call deleteAll()+deleteAlarm() when decommissioning an object to stop storage billing.

findings.topic: Durable Objects: lifecycle declaration (migrations vs exports)
findings.detail: Wrangler now has a first-class `exports` field: {"exports": {"FlightTracker": {"type": "durable-object", "storage": "sqlite"}, "Old": {"type":"durable-object","state":"deleted"}, "OldName": {"type":"durable-object","state":"renamed","renamed_to":"NewName"}}}. Legacy `migrations` array ({tag, new_sqlite_classes, renamed_classes, deleted_classes}) is deprecated; a config containing both is rejected at validation; once deployed with `exports` you cannot return to `migrations`; lifecycle changes are atomic at the control plane (no gradual rollout) and you cannot roll back to a version deployed before an exports-driven change; deletes are permanent (no trash); storage backend cannot change after provisioning. Greenfield: use `exports` with storage sqlite from the first deploy.

findings.topic: Testing DOs: @cloudflare/vitest-plugin (formerly vitest-pool-workers)
findings.detail: Current package is @cloudflare/vitest-plugin v1.1.13 (peer vitest ^4.1.0); @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers v0.22.0 is legacy with an official migration guide. Config: defineConfig({plugins:[cloudflareTest({wrangler:{configPath:'./wrangler.jsonc'}, miniflare:{...overrides}})]}). Imports: env and exports from 'cloudflare:workers'; createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, runInDurableObject(stub, cb), runDurableObjectAlarm(stub) (runs and removes the scheduled alarm, returns true/false), listDurableObjectIds(ns), getQueueResult(batch, ctx) from 'cloudflare:test'. Storage isolation is per test file (writes undone at file end); test files run in parallel by default; --max-workers=1 --no-isolate for shared state. Known issues: Vitest fake timers do NOT apply to KV/R2/cache simulators (cannot expire KV keys); DO alarms are exercised by calling runDurableObjectAlarm, not by advancing time, so the FlightTracker cadence logic should take an injectable now() so a test can step through daily→hourly→10-min→2-min tiers deterministically; always await storage promises; use `using` for RPC methods returning non-primitives; dynamic import() fails inside handlers; WebSockets in DOs need --no-isolate; V8 coverage unsupported (use Istanbul). Recipes exist for DOs with direct access, Queue producers/consumers, Hyperdrive with a Vitest-managed TCP server (inject() a port from globalSetup), and Workflows. Custom Vitest environments/runners are not supported.

findings.topic: Hyperdrive
findings.detail: Included in Workers Free and Paid at no extra charge; Free: 100k queries/day (fail beyond), Paid: unlimited queries; no egress fees. Limits: 10 configs (Free) / 25 (Paid); ~20 (Free) / ~100 (Paid) origin connections per config; 15 s connect timeout; 10 min idle timeout; 60 s max query; 50 MB max cached response. Pool sits in region(s) closest to the origin DB; transaction-mode pooling; named prepared statements supported for postgres.js and node-postgres. Query cache defaults: max_age 60 s (max 1 h), stale_while_revalidate 15 s; only parameterized immutable SELECTs are cached; cache is NOT invalidated by writes, so create a second config with --caching-disabled for user-facing reads (docs recommend this for auth/sessions/read-after-write). Local dev: CLOUDFLARE_HYPERDRIVE_LOCAL_CONNECTION_STRING_<BINDING> env var or localConnectionString in config; wrangler dev --remote uses the real config. Latency with Placement: 1-3 ms per sequential query when near origin vs 20-30 ms from distant regions. nodejs_compat is required for pg/postgres.js and is enabled by default for compatibility_date >= 2026-08-04.

findings.topic: Neon pricing and Hyperdrive fit
findings.detail: Free: $0, 100 CU-hours/project/month, 0.5 GB storage/project (writes fail beyond), 10 branches, 100 projects, autoscale to 2 CU, mandatory scale-to-zero after 5 min, 6 h restore window. Launch: no minimum, $0.106/CU-hour, $0.35/GB-month, 10 branches included then $1.50/branch-month (prorated hourly), autoscale to 16 CU, scale-to-zero configurable/disableable, up to 7 days PITR at $0.20/GB-month. Scale: $0.222/CU-hour, $0.35/GB-month, 25 branches included, fixed sizes to 56 CU, scale-to-zero 1 min to always-on, up to 30 days PITR. 500 GB egress included then $0.10/GB. Always-on 0.25 CU on Launch ≈ 0.25 × 730 × $0.106 ≈ $19/mo; 1 CU always-on ≈ $77/mo. Neon's Hyperdrive guide uses the DIRECT (non-pooled) connection string with sslmode=require and either pg or postgres.js; Hyperdrive's local connection string shows sslmode=disable but the upstream leg is TLS. Practical warning: Hyperdrive keeps idle origin connections up to 10 min and Neon treats connection activity as resetting the scale-to-zero timer, so expect production compute to stay warm; budget for always-on rather than assuming scale-to-zero savings. Neon GitHub Actions exist for create/delete/reset branch and schema diff; branches support expiration dates for ephemeral PR branches.

findings.topic: Drizzle ORM on Workers
findings.detail: Versions on npm: drizzle-orm 0.45.2, drizzle-kit 0.31.10, postgres (postgres.js) 3.4.9. Cloudflare's official Drizzle+Hyperdrive example uses pg (node-postgres) with drizzle-orm/node-postgres and a new Client per request on env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString; postgres.js (>= 3.4.4) is equally supported. drizzle.config.ts: dialect 'postgresql', out './drizzle', dbCredentials.url from DATABASE_URL; CI runs `drizzle-kit generate` (commit SQL + journal) and `drizzle-kit migrate --config` per environment; applied migrations are tracked in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations. Migrations run from CI against the Neon branch directly (not through Hyperdrive). Recommendation: postgres.js, `max: 5` per isolate, `ctx.waitUntil(sql.end())` (unverified from memory: this cleanup idiom appears in Cloudflare's postgres.js example).

findings.topic: D1 comparison
findings.detail: Pricing matches DO SQLite: 25B rows read/mo then $0.001/M; 50M rows written/mo then $1.00/M; 5 GB then $0.75/GB-mo; scale-to-zero, no egress. Limits: 10 GB per database (Paid, cannot be increased), 500 MB Free; 50,000 databases; 100 columns per table; 100 KB max statement; Time Travel 30 days. Read replication via Sessions API (withSession('first-primary'|'first-unconstrained'|bookmark), getBookmark()) in six regions; announced public beta 2025-04-10 and no GA changelog found as of this run. Drizzle works with D1 (migrations_pattern for nested layout). Export: `wrangler d1 export` produces SQL dumps but blocks other requests while running, skips virtual tables, and int64 precision loss applies. Migration risk if starting on D1: SQLite dialect (no timestamptz, enums, arrays, jsonb operators, partial/GIN indexes, RETURNING quirks), Drizzle schema files are dialect-specific so all table definitions and dialect-dependent queries must be rewritten; export is a blocking full dump (downtime or dual-write); 10 GB hard cap with status_events/timeline and BTS history is reachable within the first year at 100k flights/month; no connection pooling needed is the only ergonomic win. Verdict: Neon via Hyperdrive.

findings.topic: Queues
findings.detail: Pricing: Paid 1M operations/mo included then $0.40/M; Free 10k ops/day; one operation per 64 KB written, read or deleted (a message costs ~3 ops end to end). Limits: 128 KB message; 100 messages or 256 KB per sendBatch; consumer batch 1-100 (default 10), max_batch_timeout 0-60 s (default 5); max_retries default 3, max 100; delaySeconds up to 24 h; retention configurable to 14 days (24 h Free); 5,000 msg/s per queue; 250 concurrent push-consumer invocations, autoscaled (retry()/retryAll() do not count as failures; uncaught exceptions do); consumer wall time 15 min; 10,000 queues; 25 GB backlog. DLQ configured with dead_letter_queue on the consumer; messages exceeding max_retries go to DLQ (else deleted); DLQ without consumer retains 4 days; DLQ needs its own consumer. Explicit msg.ack()/msg.retry({delaySeconds}) plus ackAll/retryAll. Push consumers are the default; pull consumers are HTTP-based for non-Workers environments.

findings.topic: Workflows
findings.detail: Billing for steps and storage started 2026-08-10. Paid: requests 10M/mo then $0.30/M (shared Workers pool), CPU 30M ms then $0.02/M, storage 1 GB-mo then $0.20/GB-mo, steps 500k/mo then $0.80 per additional 100k. Free: 100k req/day, 3,000 steps/day, 1 GB-mo. Retries and rollback handlers do not count as steps; sleep steps do not count toward the step cap; idle/sleeping instances incur no CPU. Limits: 10,000 steps/instance default (to 25,000 Paid); 1 MiB per step result and per event payload; 1 GB persisted state per instance (Paid); 50,000 concurrently running instances (waiting instances excluded); sleep up to 365 days; 10,000 retries per step; completed-instance retention 30 days Paid, but as of 2026-09-10 new Workflows on Paid default to 7-day retention. API: step.do(name, {retries:{limit,delay,backoff}}, fn), step.sleep, step.sleepUntil, step.waitForEvent({type,timeout}), NonRetryableError, env.WF.create({id, params}), createBatch up to 100, .subscribe() event streaming (2026-09-15), delete instances via API (2026-09-17).

findings.topic: KV
findings.detail: Paid: 10M reads/mo then $0.50/M; 1M writes/mo then $5/M; 1M deletes/mo then $5/M; 1M lists/mo then $5/M; 1 GB then $0.50/GB-mo; misses are billed. Free: 100k reads/day, 1k writes/day, 1 GB. Eventually consistent: immediate at the writing colo, up to 60 s or more elsewhere; cacheTtl default 60 s; unsuitable for keys updated tens of times per second (use DOs). Fit: METAR/TAF/board caches with expirationTtl; not for anything a FlightTracker must read-after-write.

findings.topic: R2
findings.detail: Standard: $0.015/GB-month; Class A $4.50/M; Class B $0.36/M; egress free. Free tier: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A, 10M Class B per month. Infrequent Access: $0.01/GB-mo, $9/M A, $0.90/M B, $0.01/GB retrieval, 30-day minimum. Share-card images and GDPR export bundles at 100k flights/month will stay inside or near the free tier.

findings.topic: Workers Analytics Engine
findings.detail: Currently not billed; published future pricing: 10M data points/mo included then $0.25/M; 1M read queries/mo included then $1.00/M. Limits: max 250 writeDataPoint calls per invocation; up to 20 blobs, 20 doubles, 1 index (index <= 96 bytes, blobs <= 16 KB total) per point; retention 3 months; high volumes are sampled and queries must weight by _sample_interval. SQL API: POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account_id>/analytics_engine/sql with Bearer token holding Account Analytics Read; SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY/aggregates. Binding: analytics_engine_datasets [{binding, dataset}]. Implication for 'provider queries per day as a first-class metric': AE is the right hot store, but 90-day retention and sampling mean a nightly cron must roll up per-provider daily counts into a Postgres table for durable, exact billing reconciliation.

findings.topic: Workers Paid plan, Cron, platform limits
findings.detail: Workers Paid: $5/mo minimum; 10M requests/mo then $0.30/M; 30M CPU-ms/mo then $0.02/M CPU-ms; no duration charge; Free: 100k req/day, 10 ms CPU/invocation. Cron Triggers: 5 per account (Free) / 250 (Paid); Paid CPU 30 s for sub-hourly schedules and 15 min for >= 1 h schedules; per-env `triggers.crons`; local test via /cdn-cgi/local/scheduled?cron=... . Limits: 100 (Free) / 500 (Paid) Workers per account; 64 MiB uncompressed bundle; 50 (Free) / 10,000 (Paid) subrequests per invocation; 6 simultaneous outgoing connections; 64 (Free) / 128 (Paid) vars+secrets per Worker at 5 KB each; HTTP CPU 30 s default up to 5 min; Cron/DO/Queue invocations capped at 15 min wall clock.

findings.topic: Rate Limiting binding
findings.detail: GA since 2025-09-19 (changelog). Config: {"ratelimits":[{"name":"PUBLIC_RL","namespace_id":"1001","simple":{"limit":100,"period":60}}]}; period must be 10 or 60 s; await env.PUBLIC_RL.limit({key}) returns {success}. Counters are per Cloudflare location (not global), intentionally permissive and eventually consistent; bindings sharing a namespace_id share counters across Workers; requires Wrangler >= 4.36.0. No separate line item on the Workers pricing page (treated as included; explicit 'free' statement not found, so partially unverified). Use it for per-IP / per-token abuse throttling on public API, share pages and the MCP endpoint; do NOT use it for free-tier quota accounting or provider budgets (those belong in Postgres or a DO).

findings.topic: Cloudflare Access for admin routes
findings.detail: Zero Trust Free plan covers up to 50 users; pay-as-you-go $7/user/month beyond (third-party pricing summaries; Cloudflare's own pricing page did not render numbers during this run). Self-hosted Access apps require an active Cloudflare zone (full or partial setup) or a Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostname; apps can be scoped to paths (e.g. api.taxiway.app/admin) using app-path wildcards; workers.dev hostnames can also be protected. Workers should independently verify the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header (cookie CF_Authorization for browsers) with jose jwtVerify + createRemoteJWKSet against https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs, checking issuer and the application AUD tag (POLICY_AUD, TEAM_DOMAIN vars).

findings.topic: Email Routing to Worker (forward-to-address import)
findings.detail: Email Routing is free on every plan; requires the domain's DNS on Cloudflare (it manages MX/SPF); inbound message size limit 25 MiB (rejected above); 200 routing rules per domain; 200 verified destination addresses per account. Worker `email(message, env, ctx)` handler receives ForwardableEmailMessage with from, to, headers, raw (ReadableStream), rawSize, forward(), reply() (DMARC-validated), setReject(); parse MIME with postal-mime. Email handlers count against normal CPU limits (Paid recommended). Emails sent from Workers show as 'dropped' in the routing summary even when delivered. Design note: the email handler should only enqueue {r2Key or inline <=128 KB, sender, recipient-token} to IMPORT_QUEUE / start a Workflow; do not run LLM extraction inside the email handler.

findings.topic: Cloudflare Email Service sending (magic links)
findings.detail: Status: Beta, Workers Paid only. Pricing: 3,000 emails/account/month included, then $0.35 per 1,000; sends to verified destination addresses are free and unmetered. Limits: 50 recipients per message; 5 MiB message (25 MiB to verified addresses); 30 domains per zone for routing+sending; new accounts start on a 'conservative daily quota' that scales with deliverability and account standing (number not published); before a sending domain is onboarded you can only send to verified addresses. Binding: "send_email":[{"name":"EMAIL"}] with optional destination_address / allowed_destination_addresses. Risk for Phase 0: an undisclosed daily cap on a beta product is a bad dependency for auth-critical magic links; keep a provider-agnostic MailSender interface with a Resend/Postmark adapter fallback (unverified pricing for those, not researched here).

findings.topic: Observability: Workers Logs, Traces, OTel export, Logpush, Sentry
findings.detail: Workers Logs: observability.enabled=true (+head_sampling_rate, invocation_logs); Paid 20M events/mo included then $0.60/M, 7-day retention; Free 200k/day, 3 days; auto 1% sampling after 5B/day. Workers Traces: open beta, observability.traces.enabled, follows OTel, each span is one observability event from the same 20M pool; billing starts 2026-10-01; as of 2026-09-17 traces automatically include RPC session spans into Durable Objects. OTel export (beta, Workers Paid only): observability.{traces,logs}.destinations=[names created in dashboard], head_sampling_rate, persist:false to skip Cloudflare storage; free during beta, docs state $0.05/M events beyond 10M included from 2026-10-01 for export; destinations include Honeycomb, Grafana Cloud, Axiom, Sentry, any OTLP endpoint. Workers Logpush: Paid, $0.05/M requests after 10M/mo, Cloudflare now recommends OTel export over Logpush for new integrations. Sentry: @sentry/cloudflare 10.75.0; Sentry.withSentry(optionsFn, handler) or Vite plugin autoInstrumentation; @sentry/hono/cloudflare middleware `sentry(app, (env)=>({dsn:env.SENTRY_DSN}))`; Sentry.instrumentDurableObjectWithSentry(optionsFn, Class) (>= 9.16.0) captures DO errors and creates spans for storage get/put/delete/list; requires nodejs_compat (AsyncLocalStorage) and compatibility_date >= 2024-09-23; distributed tracing across RPC needs explicit propagation config.

findings.topic: Hono on Workers
findings.detail: hono 4.13.8 on npm (published mid-September 2026 per registry timestamp 1789457493894 ms). Companion packages: @hono/zod-openapi 1.6.3 (peer zod ^4.0.0, hono >= 4.10.0) providing OpenAPIHono + createRoute with RPC (hc) compatibility; @hono/zod-validator 0.9.1 (peer zod ^3.25 || ^4, hono >= 4.11.2) for zValidator('json'|'query'|'param', schema); Standard Schema validators (Valibot etc.) also work. RPC: export type AppType = typeof app; hc<AppType>(baseUrl) infers input/output; both tsconfigs need strict:true and matching hono versions; large apps slow the IDE, so split into route modules mounted with app.route() and pre-compile the client types (emit .d.ts in packages/shared via TypeScript project references) for the mobile app. Auth middleware: standard app.use('/v1/*', mw) with c.set('user'); Sentry Hono middleware goes first. Router: default SmartRouter (RegExpRouter + TrieRouter) is fine on Workers (unverified from memory: docs list RegExpRouter as fastest; default is SmartRouter).

findings.topic: Wrangler environments, secrets, CI/CD
findings.detail: wrangler 4.135.0. Environments via top-level `env.<name>` in wrangler.jsonc, deployed with `wrangler deploy --env staging`; inheritable keys (name, main, compatibility_date, routes, triggers, build, workers_dev) can be set once; ALL bindings (vars, kv_namespaces, r2_buckets, durable_objects, queues, d1, hyperdrive, services, analytics_engine_datasets, ratelimits, send_email) are non-inheritable and must be redeclared in every env; `wrangler types` emits types for bindings across all envs. Secrets: `wrangler secret put KEY --env staging`; `wrangler deploy --secrets-file` bulk (up to 100); local `.dev.vars` / `.dev.vars.<env>` (only the env-specific file loads when present); account-level Secrets Store binding is beta. Workers Builds: GitHub/GitLab integration; Free 3,000 build-min/mo (1 concurrent), Paid 6,000 (6 concurrent) then $0.005/min; 20-min build timeout; monorepo via root directory + watch paths per Worker; environment targeting by creating one Worker per env with deploy command `wrangler deploy --env <env>` and non-production branch command `wrangler versions upload --env <env>`; preview URLs use <version-or-alias>-<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev (--preview-alias); CRITICAL: preview URLs are not generated for Workers that use Durable Objects, Containers or Sandbox. workers.dev is treated as a hobby/free website tier; production should run on a custom domain (custom domain needed anyway for Access and Email Routing). nodejs_compat is default for compatibility_date >= 2026-08-04.

findings.topic: Phase 0 wrangler.jsonc binding list (proposed, derived from verified config shapes)
findings.detail: apps/api/wrangler.jsonc: name 'taxiway-api'; main 'src/index.ts'; compatibility_date '2026-09-01' (>= 2026-08-04 so nodejs_compat is implicit; still list compatibility_flags ['nodejs_compat'] for clarity); workers_dev false in prod, routes on api.<domain>; placement {mode:'smart'} (optional, evaluate with Neon region); exports: FlightTracker, AirportState, UserInbox, ProviderBudget each {type:'durable-object', storage:'sqlite'}; findings.topic: Phase 0 DO class list and storage layout (proposed)
findings.detail: 1) FlightTracker, name = `${operatingCarrierICAO}:${flightNumber}:${schedDepDateLocalYYYYMMDD}:${originIATA}` (idFromName; also stored in Postgres flight_instances.do_name as the registry). SQLite tables: meta(key TEXT PK, value TEXT) holding state json {phase, refresh_tier, next_refresh_at, last_provider, alerts_active, budget_used_today, cost_units_total, init_done}; snapshot(id INTEGER PK, fetched_at, provider, payload JSON) keep last N; status_events(id INTEGER PK, ts, field, old_value, new_value, source) = the timeline; subscribers(user_id TEXT PK, subscribed_at, notify_prefs JSON); provider_calls(id, ts, provider, endpoint, ok, latency_ms, cost_units) mirrored to Analytics Engine. Alarm = next refresh per cadence tier; alarm() is idempotent (recompute tier from clock, no-op if a provider push already refreshed within tier interval); after 2h post-arrival: write final snapshot to Postgres, deleteAll(), deleteAlarm(), mark registry row 'archived'. RPC: subscribe(userId, prefs), unsubscribe(userId), getState(), applyProviderEvent(event), forceRefresh(reason), getCostLedger(). 2) AirportState, name = IATA; tables: weather(kind 'metar'|'taf', fetched_at, raw, parsed JSON), nas_status(fetched_at, payload), delay_index(computed_at, score, reasons JSON); alarm every 15 min while active_flights>0 else none; also seeds KV CACHE for cheap public reads. 3) UserInbox, name = user_id (uuid); tables: devices(token PK, platform, app_version, updated_at), prefs(key, value) incl. quiet hours, pending_notifications(id, flight_key, type, payload, not_before, coalesce_key), delivered(id, delivered_at, channel, result); alarm used for quiet-hours release and coalescing bursts; NOTIFY_QUEUE consumer calls USER_INBOX.enqueue(). 4) ProviderBudget, name = `${provider}:${utcDate}` (sharded per provider per day so it is never a global singleton): counters(bucket TEXT PK, count, cost_units), reserve(n) RPC returns allow/deny against the day budget; FlightTracker also keeps a per-flight cap locally so most calls never hit ProviderBudget (call it only when per-flight usage crosses thresholds, or on every call if peak < ~200 rps). Optional Phase 1: ShareLink DO keyed by share token for live share pages with view counters.

findings.topic: Recommended test layout (proposed)
findings.detail: Vitest 4.1 with two projects via vitest.workspace / projects: (a) apps/api/test/unit/** runs in plain node environment for provider adapters (AeroDataBox real adapter with recorded fixtures via msw or undici MockAgent, AeroAPI mocked adapter, codeshare resolver, cadence calculator, delay-risk heuristics) and packages/shared schemas; (b) apps/api/test/workers/** runs under @cloudflare/vitest-plugin with wrangler.configPath. Workers-project files: flight-tracker.lifecycle.test.ts (create stub via env.FLIGHT_TRACKER.getByName, runInDurableObject to seed state and assert SQL rows, loop `await runDurableObjectAlarm(stub)` with a stubbed provider and injected clock to walk tiers daily→hourly→10min→2min→archive, assert provider call counts equal the documented per-flight budget, assert alarm idempotency by invoking alarm twice); provider-budget.test.ts; user-inbox.quiet-hours.test.ts; queues/notify-consumer.test.ts using getQueueResult; http/routes.test.ts using SELF.fetch or exports.default.fetch with Hono app and a fake Access JWT; hyperdrive: use miniflare.hyperdrives with a localConnectionString injected from globalSetup pointing at a Postgres service container in GitHub Actions (or a Neon ephemeral branch when secrets are available); apply drizzle migrations in globalSetup. CI (GitHub Actions, not Workers Builds, because DO Workers get no preview URLs): lint+typecheck → unit → workers tests (postgres:16 service) → drizzle-kit migrate against staging Neon branch → wrangler deploy --env staging on main; production deploy on tag with `wrangler versions upload --env production` then `wrangler versions deploy` for gradual rollout (versions/gradual rollout behaviour with DOs unverified in this run).

cloudflare-backend.recommendation: Database: Neon (Launch plan, one always-on-ish 0.25-1 CU compute, expect ~$20-80/mo compute at 10k-100k flights) accessed through two Hyperdrive configs (DB uncached for user/flight state, DB_CACHED for reference data like airports/airlines/BTS aggregates) with Drizzle + postgres.js. Reject D1 for the reasons in findings: 10 GB uncapped-growth risk from status_events and BTS history, SQLite dialect lock-in that forces a Drizzle schema and query rewrite, blocking export, and read replication still in beta. Coordination: SQLite-backed Durable Objects declared with the new `exports` field (not the deprecated migrations array), FlightTracker keyed by operating carrier + number + local departure date + origin via getByName, with an idempotent alarm handler that recomputes the refresh tier from an injectable clock and a per-flight query budget enforced inside the DO, backed by a sharded ProviderBudget DO per provider per UTC day for the global guard; Postgres holds the flight_instances registry because DOs cannot be enumerated. Cost attribution: every provider call writes one Analytics Engine data point (index = provider, blobs = endpoint/flight_key/result, doubles = latency/cost_units) and a row in the DO's provider_calls table; a nightly cron rolls AE into a Postgres provider_daily_usage table because AE retention is 3 months and results are sampled. Async work: Queues for notification fan-out, provider webhook ingestion and any high-volume idempotent unit of work (cheap at $0.40/M ops, 128 KB messages, DLQ); Workflows for email-account sync, CSV import and GDPR export/deletion because they are multi-step, need per-step retries and durable intermediate state, and their volume (steps priced at $0.80/100k after 500k) stays in the low tens of dollars even at 10k syncs/day. Framework: Hono 4.13 with @hono/zod-openapi 1.6 (Zod 4) for validated OpenAPI routes and an hc client type compiled into packages/shared for the mobile app; Sentry via @sentry/hono/cloudflare middleware plus instrumentDurableObjectWithSentry; Workers Logs + Traces with head sampling and OTel export to the SVP's preferred backend (Honeycomb/Grafana) with persist:false to avoid paying twice once billing starts 2026-10-01. CI/CD: GitHub Actions running wrangler (Workers Builds cannot produce preview URLs for DO Workers), three Workers environments (dev local, staging, production) each mapped to its own Neon branch, secrets per env with `wrangler secret put --env`, custom domains from day one because Access and Email Routing need a Cloudflare zone. Admin surface behind Cloudflare Access (free to 50 users) with jose JWT verification in the Worker. Magic-link email: abstract behind a MailSender interface; Cloudflare Email Service is beta with an undisclosed ramping daily quota, so ship with a second adapter (Resend or Postmark) and decide in Phase 1 which is primary.
risks: Workers Builds does not generate preview URLs for Workers that export Durable Objects; PR-level preview environments for the API must come from a dedicated staging env or ephemeral `wrangler deploy --env pr-<n>` Workers via GitHub Actions (each needs its own DO namespaces and Neon branch).

DO lifecycle via `exports` cannot be rolled back to a version deployed before the change and cannot be rolled out gradually; class renames/deletes are control-plane atomic and deletes are permanent. Treat DO class names as API and rename rarely.

Alarms are at-least-once with up to 6 retries; a non-idempotent alarm() can double-query providers and double-bill. Cadence logic must be idempotent and checkpoint provider results before any await on non-storage I/O.
Gradual Worker rollouts mean a new API version can call an old FlightTracker for minutes; RPC method signatures must stay backward compatible across deploys.

Hyperdrive query cache is not invalidated on writes (60 s max_age default, 15 s SWR); using a cached config for user-facing reads causes stale flight state after a write. Keep the default config caching-disabled and opt in per query path.

Hyperdrive holds idle origin connections for 10 minutes and Neon resets scale-to-zero on connection activity; production Neon compute will effectively be always-on, so cost-model it as such (and disable scale-to-zero on Launch to avoid cold-start latency spikes).
Analytics Engine is not yet billed and retains only 3 months with sampling at volume; treat it as a hot metrics store, not the system of record for provider cost accounting.
Rate-limit binding counters are per-colo and permissive; it cannot enforce global free-tier quotas or provider budgets.
Cloudflare Email Service is beta, Workers Paid only, 3,000 emails/mo included, and new accounts start on an undisclosed conservative daily quota; auth-critical magic links need a fallback sender.

Workers Traces and OTel export move to paid on 2026-10-01 from the same 20M-event pool as Workers Logs; with head_sampling_rate=1 and DO RPC spans auto-included, event volume per API request will be several spans plus logs. Set sampling before launch.
Workflows default retention on Workers Paid dropped to 7 days on 2026-09-10; audit/GDPR evidence must be persisted to Postgres, not inferred from Workflow instance history.
@hono/zod-openapi 1.6.x requires Zod 4; the mobile app and shared package must standardize on Zod 4 to share schemas.

The vitest integration package was renamed (@cloudflare/vitest-plugin, Vitest 4.1+); older tutorials and AI-generated snippets reference @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers and defineWorkersConfig and will not work unchanged.

Vitest fake timers do not affect DO alarms or KV TTLs; lifecycle tests must drive alarms explicitly with runDurableObjectAlarm and pass an injected clock, otherwise cadence tests become wall-clock dependent.
DO SQLite int64 precision loss beyond 2^53 affects any provider IDs stored as integers; store IDs as TEXT.
Email Routing requires the product domain's DNS on Cloudflare; if the domain is registered elsewhere, nameservers must move before forward-to-address import can work.
open_decisions_for_owner: Neon region and Workers Smart Placement: pick the Neon region (likely AWS us-east-1) and decide whether to pass locationHint 'enam' when creating FlightTracker/UserInbox DOs so DO→Hyperdrive writes stay single-digit ms; trade-off is higher read latency for EU/APAC users on DO-served endpoints versus cheaper, faster persistence.
Neon plan: Launch (max 16 CU autoscale, 7-day PITR, 10 branches) vs Scale (30-day PITR, 25 branches, $0.222/CU-hr); Launch is sufficient for Phase 0-3 unless 30-day PITR is a compliance requirement.

Magic-link sender for launch: Cloudflare Email Service (beta, cheapest, single-vendor) vs Resend/Postmark (mature deliverability, extra vendor); recommendation is to implement both adapters in Phase 0 and choose primary in Phase 1 based on the Cloudflare quota ramp observed on the staging account.

Provider budget enforcement granularity: per-flight cap inside FlightTracker only (zero extra hops, allows day-level overshoot) vs also a sharded ProviderBudget DO per provider per day (one RPC hop per provider call, hard daily cutoff). Recommend both, with FlightTracker calling ProviderBudget only when its local counter crosses tier thresholds.

Observability backend for OTel export (Honeycomb, Grafana Cloud, Axiom, or Sentry drains) and the head_sampling_rate for traces once billing starts 2026-10-01; whether to keep persist:true (pay Cloudflare) in addition to the external destination.

CI/CD: GitHub Actions + wrangler (full control, PR ephemeral envs possible, no preview URLs limitation) vs Workers Builds (zero-maintenance, but no preview URLs for DO Workers and environment targeting requires one Worker per env). Recommend GitHub Actions.

Whether the API Worker also serves public share pages and the MCP endpoint, or those become separate Workers (separate rate-limit namespaces, separate Access/WAF posture, separate blast radius) bound via service bindings to the same DO namespaces.
Cloudflare Access for admin: use Zero Trust Free (50 users) with the product zone, and whether admin routes live on a separate hostname (admin.<domain>) to simplify Access app scoping.
Retention policy for status_events and BTS history in Postgres (drives storage cost at $0.35/GB-mo) and whether archived FlightTracker snapshots go to Postgres, R2 (cheaper, $0.015/GB-mo), or both.
alternatives_rejected: D1 as the primary database: 10 GB non-negotiable cap, SQLite dialect lock-in under Drizzle, blocking export, read replication still in public beta since April 2025; migration cost later would exceed the pooling convenience now.
Key-value-backed Durable Objects: Cloudflare recommends SQLite for all new namespaces; KV backend has 128 KiB value cap and 50 GB per-account cap.

Cloudflare Workflows for notification fan-out: step pricing ($0.80/100k after 500k) and 1 MiB step results are wrong-shaped for millions of small idempotent pushes; Queues at $0.40/M ops with DLQ fits.
Queues for email sync/CSV import: multi-step jobs with partial progress and per-step retries would need hand-rolled state in Postgres; Workflows provide this natively.
Workers Builds as the sole CI: no preview URLs for DO Workers and per-environment Workers required; GitHub Actions with wrangler is more flexible.
A single global ProviderBudget or rate-limiter DO: explicitly an anti-pattern in Cloudflare's rules (hot singleton); shard per provider per day.
Using the rate-limit binding for free-tier quotas: per-colo, permissive, eventually consistent by design.

Neon pooled (PgBouncer) connection string behind Hyperdrive: Neon's own guide uses the direct string since Hyperdrive already pools in transaction mode; double pooling adds a hop and prepared-statement complications.
Workers Logpush for logs: Cloudflare itself now recommends OTel export for new integrations.
workers.dev hostnames for production: treated as hobby tier, and Access/Email Routing need a Cloudflare zone anyway.

flight-data-providers.summary: Verified September 2026 pricing and API shapes for all provider classes Taxiway needs. FlightAware AeroAPI v4 is per-result-set (15 records = 1 set): GET /flights/{ident} is $0.005, /flights/{id}/position $0.010, /track $0.012, /airports/{id}/flights $0.020, /schedules $0.020, push-alert delivery $0.020 each with free alert management; Standard tier ($100/mo minimum, explicitly allows B2C, 5 result sets/sec, alerts + 500k historical sets/mo) is sufficient for Taxiway, Premium ($1,000/mo, 100/s) only for Foresight predictions and B2B. Live /flights/{ident} covers 10 days back to 2 days forward; /history/* covers 2011 to 15 days ago at roughly 4x the live price. Gate, terminal, baggage_claim, codeshares and inbound_fa_flight_id all exist in the spec, but inbound_fa_flight_id is computed at request time and usually appears only once the inbound aircraft is on the ground, and gate/baggage coverage depends on carrier+airport feeds. AeroDataBox (direct plans $19/40k units, $99/400k, $499/4M; RapidAPI/API.Market from free 400 units) prices by tier: flight status by number and FIDS are TIER 2 (2 units), aircraft and airport lookups TIER 1; it returns codeshareStatus, gates, terminals, baggageBelt, revised/predicted/runway times and aircraft reg, but live updates exist only 1-2 days ahead and coverage is uneven outside US/EU/AU. Community ADS-B is the only free position source: adsb.fi (1 req/s, personal non-commercial only), airplanes.live (educational/non-commercial only), adsb.lol (ODbL, "available to everyone", dynamic rate limits, API keys coming); OpenSky requires a written commercial license, and Flightradar24's commercial API is $9/$99/$900 per month on credits (6 credits per light position record). Weather (aviationweather.gov 100 req/min with per-minute cache files, NWS with mandatory User-Agent, Open-Meteo free tier non-commercial, $29/$99 commercial), FAA NAS status (public XML at nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information), BTS on-time PREZIP monthly ZIPs (~30-60 MB, ~600k rows, 2-3 month lag) and public-domain OurAirports plus MIT mwgg/Airports for IANA timezones round out the stack. The single most important architectural constraint discovered: AeroAPI Standard's 5 result-sets/sec cap means a 2-minute airborne polling cadence saturates at roughly 600 concurrently airborne tracked flights, so airborne state must be alert-driven with ADS-B positions, not AeroAPI polling.

findings.topic: 1. AeroAPI v4 tiers, minimums, rate limits, entitlement
findings.detail: Three tiers (all usage-billed per result set, 1 set = 15 records): Personal = free $5/mo credit ($10 for ADS-B feeders), personal/academic use only, 10 result sets/minute, no alerts, no history. Standard = $100/mo minimum, permitted for 'business or business-to-consumer purposes', 5 result sets/second, adds flight alerting, historical data (500,000 result sets/month), email support. Premium = $1,000/mo minimum, adds all B2B use, Foresight predictions, Aireon space-based ADS-B, 99.5% uptime SLA, phone support, 100 result sets/second. Volume discounts on Standard/Premium: 30% off at $1,000-$2,000/mo usage scaling to 94% off above $64,000/mo. Implication: Taxiway (B2C) fits Standard; Premium is needed only for Foresight (delay predictions) or if the 5/s rate cap is hit.
