findings.topic: 1. AeroAPI v4 identifiers and time windows
findings.detail: GET /flights/{ident}: ident may be a designator (e.g. UAL123 or UA123), registration, or fa_flight_id; ident_type param disambiguates (designator|registration|fa_flight_id); start/end ISO8601; 'Specified start date must be no further than 10 days in the past and 2 days in the future'; default window ~11 days past to ~2 days future; max_pages (default 1) is an upper bound; cursor pagination. fa_flight_id description: 'Unique identifier assigned by FlightAware for this specific flight. If the flight is diverted, the new leg of the flight will have a duplicate fa_flight_id.' ident = operator code + flight number (commercial) or registration (GA); ident_icao and ident_iata also returned. /history/* endpoints cover 2011-01-01 to 15 days ago (history/flights/{ident} max 7-day span; history airport/operator boards max 24h span). Position search covers ~last 24h. Recommendation: FlightTracker DO natural key = operating carrier ICAO + flight number + scheduled departure date (origin local) + origin ICAO; store fa_flight_id as a provider external id learned on first fetch (needed for /position, /track, /route and useful for alerts) but do not make it the primary key because it is unknown before first lookup, provider-specific, and duplicated across diversion legs. Query by ident with a tight start/end so a single flight returns 1 result set ($0.005); an unbounded ident query returns up to 15 flights per page and can bill multiple sets.

findings.topic: 1. AeroAPI v4 field availability (gates, baggage, inbound aircraft, codeshares, registration)
findings.detail: Spec-confirmed fields on the Flight object: inbound_fa_flight_id ('previous flight of the aircraft serving this flight'), codeshares (ICAO list) and codeshares_iata, registration ('when known'), aircraft_type (ICAO, IATA fallback), progress_percent, scheduled/estimated/actual _out/_off/_on/_in, departure_delay, arrival_delay, filed_ete, status, blocked, diverted, cancelled, position_only, route_distance, foresight_predictions_available, origin/destination {code, code_icao, code_iata, timezone, name, city}. gate_origin, gate_destination, terminal_origin, terminal_destination, baggage_claim appear in the OpenAPI document (search-indexed) and FlightAware engineering confirms gate/codeshare/baggage/terminal in one call; the WebFetch excerpt of the yml was truncated before those schemas so treat exact descriptions as unverified from memory. Operational caveats from FlightAware staff: inbound_fa_flight_id is computed at request time (requires matching registration, matching gate at the turnaround airport, and plausible timing) and typically populates only once the inbound aircraft is already on the ground; gate and baggage availability 'depends heavily on the specific carrier and airport combination'. Workaround for 'inbound aircraft leg': query /flights/{registration}?ident_type=registration once registration is known (returns recent + upcoming flights for that tail, 1 result set).

findings.topic: 1. AeroAPI v4 push alerts (webhook)
findings.detail: Setup: PUT /alerts/endpoint {url} sets the account-wide default delivery URL (required before any POST /alerts); POST /alerts body: ident, origin, destination, aircraft_type, start, end, max_weekly, eta, events {arrival, cancelled, departure, diverted, filed, hold_end, hold_start, in, off, on, out}, impending_arrival [minutes...], impending_departure [minutes...], target_url (per-alert override). 'departure' and 'arrival' are bundled events (departure bundles filed + OFF + up to 5 per-departure changes such as gate/time changes; arrival bundles en-route changes + taxi stop). Delivery: AeroAPI POSTs JSON {long_description, short_description, summary, event_code (e.g. 'offblock'), alert_id, flight {fa_flight_id, ident, registration, atc_ident, aircraft_type, origin, destination, route, position_only, blocked, cancelled, diverted, route_distance, filed_ete, scheduled/estimated/actual_*...}}. Cost: $0.020 per delivered alert; management is free. max_weekly defaults 1,000 (Standard) / 4,000 (Premium) per alert config. impending_departure is capped at 60 minutes before departure (users requested 120). FlightAware provides a push-notification test page and 24h delivery success/failure log. Sample webhook receivers in flightaware/aeroapps (BSD-3). Community threads show occasional missed deliveries; design for polling fallback.

findings.topic: 1. AeroAPI v4 positions, track, boards, delays, schedules
findings.detail: GET /flights/{id}/position returns last_position {fa_flight_id, altitude, altitude_change, groundspeed, heading, latitude, longitude, timestamp, update_type} where update_type enum: P=projected, O=oceanic, Z=radar, A=ADS-B, M=multilateration, D=datalink, X=surface/near-surface, S=space-based. GET /flights/{id}/track returns positions[] with include_estimated_positions and include_surface_positions flags ($0.012). GET /airports/{id}/flights (+ /arrivals, /departures, /scheduled_arrivals, /scheduled_departures, /to/{dest_id} with connection=nonstop|onestop) params airline, type (Airline|GeneralAviation), start, end; response rows include ident, fa_flight_id, operator, operator_iata, flight_number, registration, atc_ident, inbound_fa_flight_id, codeshares. GET /airports/{id}/delays returns color-coded (red/yellow/green) delay categories with reasons (delay_secs/category fields unverified from memory). GET /schedules/{date_start}/{date_end} ($0.020/set) params origin, destination, airline, flight_number, include_codeshares, include_regional; returns scheduled rows (ident, aircraft_type, origin, destination, scheduled_out/off/on/in; actual_ident/actual_ident_iata for operating carrier resolution: unverified from memory). Rate limit note: at 5 result sets/s (Standard) a 2-minute cadence supports at most ~600 simultaneously airborne tracked flights (5/s x 120 s); beyond that you need Premium (100/s) or alert-driven updates.

findings.topic: 2. AeroDataBox pricing tiers (2026, USD)
findings.detail: Direct (aerodatabox.com, billing via portal): Starter $19/mo = 40,000 units, 5 req/s; Growth $99/mo = 400,000 units, 10 req/s; Scale $499/mo = 4,000,000 units, 20 req/s; Custom = contact. Extra units on Starter/Growth via ADS-B feeding, custom overage on Scale. API.Market: Basic free 7-day trial 400 units 1 req/s; Pro $7.50/5,000 (1 req/s); Pro 2 $15/15,000 (2 req/s); Ultra $37.50/50,000 (3 req/s); Ultra 2 $75/150,000 (4 req/s); Mega $187.50/500,000 (5 req/s), Mega overage $0.00037/unit. RapidAPI: Basic free 400 units 1 req/s; Pro $8/5,000 (2 req/s); Ultra $40/50,000 (4 req/s); Mega $200/500,000 (8 req/s), overage $0.0004/unit. Unit cost by endpoint tier: TIER 1 = 1 unit, TIER 2 = 2 units, TIER 3 = 6 units, FREE = 0 (a TIER 4 exists per docs; cost not stated on pricing page). Effective cost of a TIER 2 flight-status call: Growth $0.000495, Scale $0.00025, RapidAPI Basic free (200 calls/mo). withFlightPlan=true doubles the TIER 2 charge when a plan is returned (US airspace only).

findings.topic: 2. AeroDataBox endpoints, tiers, and fields
findings.detail: From the API.Market OpenAPI spec: GET /flights/{searchBy}/{searchParam} (nearest flight) TIER 2; /flights/{searchBy}/{searchParam}/{dateLocal} TIER 2; /flights/{searchBy}/{searchParam}/{dateFromLocal}/{dateToLocal} TIER 3; /flights/{searchBy}/{searchParam}/dates TIER 2 (searchBy: number|callsign|reg|icao24; params withAircraftImage, withLocation, dateLocalRole=Both|Departure|Arrival). FIDS: /flights/airports/{codeType}/{code}/{fromLocal}/{toLocal} TIER 2 (max 12-hour window) and relative /flights/airports/{codeType}/{code}?offsetMinutes=-120&durationMinutes=720 TIER 2; params direction=Arrival|Departure|Both, withLeg, withCancelled, withCodeshared, withCargo, withPrivate, withLocation. Aircraft: /aircrafts/{searchBy}/{searchParam} (id|reg|icao24) TIER 1, /registrations and /all TIER 1, /airlines/{airlineCode}/aircrafts TIER 3, /aircrafts/reg/{reg}/image/beta TIER 2, /aircrafts/search/term TIER 2. Airports: /airports/{codeType}/{code} TIER 1 (timeZone with withTime), /runways TIER 1, /airports/search/location|ip|term TIER 2. Delays: airport delay endpoints return per-direction median delay, cancelled count, delay index and validity window, plus delayPercentiles (p5-p95) and historical delays (path /airports/{codeType}/{code}/delays is from memory, unverified). Webhooks: POST /subscriptions/webhook/{subjectType}/{subjectId} (subjectType FlightByNumber | FlightByAirportIcao), GET/DELETE /subscriptions/webhook/{id}, GET /subscriptions/webhook, /subscriptions/balance (FREE tier) and /subscriptions/balance/refill TIER 1; notifications cover flights from 6h ago to 72h ahead. Flight object: number, callSign, status, codeshareStatus (IsOperator = operated by the airline owning the number, IsCodeshared = operated by another carrier; Unknown), isCargo, departure/arrival {airport {icao, iata, name, timeZone}, scheduledTime {utc, local}, revisedTime, predictedTime, runwayTime, terminal, gate, checkInDesk, baggageBelt, quality[]}, aircraft {reg, modeS, model, image}, airline {name, iata, icao}, greatCircleDistance, location (with withLocation). Status enum values (Unknown, Expected, EnRoute, CheckIn, Boarding, GateClosed, Departed, Delayed, Approaching, Arrived, Canceled, Diverted, CanceledUncertain) partially confirmed via SDK docs. No stable per-flight id: key on number + date + origin. Codeshare handling: query the marketing number and read codeshareStatus; with withCodeshared=false FIDS returns operating flights only.

findings.topic: 2. AeroDataBox freshness and regional coverage caveats
findings.detail: Three data layers: schedules (static; refreshed 'once in 2 weeks' per airport; up to 365 days ahead plan-dependent), live updates (revised/actual times, status, gates, terminals, check-in desks, baggage belts, registration; 'nearly real-time up to once in a few hours'; live data typically only 1-2 days forward), ADS-B layer (callsign, reg, Mode-S, runway times; 'a few seconds up to half an hour'). Live status coverage 80%+ in US, Western Europe, Canada, Australia, parts of East Asia; 0% in Afghanistan, Yemen, Ukraine, parts of Africa and Central Asia. Coverage is asymmetric (a flight can have full departure detail but schedule-only arrival). Older product page states live updates exist 'for only a few hundred airports mostly located in Europe' (stale but indicative). Implication: beyond ~48h AeroDataBox returns schedule-only data, so far-out daily polls are wasted units; poll it daily only for schedule-change detection.

findings.topic: 3. Community ADS-B feeds: adsb.fi
findings.detail: Base https://opendata.adsb.fi/api/ ; endpoints /v2/hex/{hex}, /v2/icao/{hex}, /v2/callsign/{callsign}, /v2/registration/{reg}, /v2/sqk/{squawk}, /v2/mil, /v3/lat/{lat}/lon/{lon}/dist/{dist} (max 250 NM; v2 geo endpoint deprecated); feeder-only /v2/snapshot (all aircraft, twice per minute, 1 req/30s). Public rate limit 1 request/second; 4xx/429 responses trigger temporary IP bans. Format: ADSBExchange v2 / readsb aircraft.json compatible JSON (hex, flight, r, t, lat, lon, alt_baro, gs, track, seen, rssi...). Terms: 'for personal, non-commercial use only', no license/sell/rent/lease, must cite adsb.fi with a link; commercial or higher-rate needs require contacting them. Not usable for Taxiway without a written agreement.

findings.topic: 3. Community ADS-B feeds: airplanes.live and adsb.lol
findings.detail: airplanes.live: endpoints (v2, ADSBExchange-compatible JSON) /v2/hex/[hex] (up to 1000 comma-separated), /v2/callsign/[cs], /v2/reg/[reg], /v2/type/[type], /v2/squawk/[sq], /v2/mil, /v2/ladd, /v2/pia, /v2/point/[lat]/[lon]/[radius] (max 250 NM); rate limited to 1 request/second; no API key for basic access. Terms per api-docs: 'educational and non-commercial purposes only'; commercial applications and high-volume requests not permitted; a 2026 forum report shows non-feeder access being cut with an 'API Key invalid' error. adsb.lol: https://api.adsb.lol, v2 endpoints /v2/hex, /v2/callsign, /v2/reg, /v2/point/{lat}/{lon}/{radius}, /v2/closest, /v2/mil, /v2/type, plus POST /api/0/routeset (callsign -> plausible route, used by tar1090) and feeder-only RE-API; rate limits 'dynamic based on environment load'; 'in the future you will require an API key which you can obtain by feeding adsb.lol'; data licensed ODbL 1.0 and 'available to everyone' (no explicit non-commercial clause, but ODbL attribution and share-alike-for-derivative-database obligations apply). Coverage caveat for all three: terrestrial receivers only, so no oceanic/remote coverage (positions stale over the Atlantic/Pacific); MLAT for non-ADS-B aircraft. Practical position lookup: key by ICAO hex (from registration via aircraft DB) and fall back to callsign (ICAO operator + flight number, which may differ from the marketing number).

findings.topic: 3. Registration -> ICAO hex mapping sources and OpenSky
findings.detail: OpenSky aircraft database CSV: https://opensky-network.org/datasets/metadata/aircraftDatabase.csv (also s3.opensky-network.org/data-samples/metadata/aircraftDatabase.csv); columns icao24, registration, manufacturericao, manufacturername, model, typecode, serialnumber, linenumber, icaoaircrafttype, operator, operatorcallsign, operatoricao, operatoriata, owner, testreg, registered, reguntil, status, built, firstflightdate, seatconfiguration, engines, modes, adsb, acars, notes, categoryDescription; OpenSky states it is 'not up to date' and updated irregularly. Mictronics DB (basis of tar1090-db, used by readsb/tar1090 everywhere): exports at https://www.mictronics.de/aircraft-database/export.php (JSON indexedDB format, CSV variants), fields hex, registration, ICAO type code, operator flags; licensed Open Data Commons Attribution (ODC-By); mirrored as github.com/wiedehopf/tar1090-db (update.sh pulls nightly). adsbdb.com (api.adsbdb.com): free JSON lookups aircraft by Mode-S or registration, callsign -> route (origin/destination), airline by ICAO/IATA, Mode-S <-> N-number conversion; sources PlaneBase + third-party route data with 'restricted redistribution'; rate limits and license not documented (avoid as a bulk source, fine for ad-hoc fallback). Note: US N-numbers map deterministically to hex (A00001 = N1 scheme) and the FAA registry (releasable aircraft database) is public domain; non-US requires a DB. OpenSky REST API: OAuth2 client-credentials (30-min tokens), /states/all (400 credits/day anonymous, 4,000 registered, 8,000 active feeders; 1-4 credits per call by bbox size), /flights/aircraft|arrival|departure (2-day window), /tracks (30 days); terms: any commercial/for-profit use and any operational integration 'into a live product, service, or automated system' requires a written license from OpenSky. Not suitable for Taxiway without a license.

findings.topic: 3. Commercial position alternatives: FlightAware and Flightradar24 API
findings.detail: FlightAware: /flights/{id}/position $0.010/set (single last position incl. update_type P/O/Z/A/M/D/X/S so projected/estimated positions are flagged), /track $0.012 (full polyline), Aireon space-based ADS-B (oceanic coverage) only on Premium. Flightradar24 commercial API (fr24api.flightradar24.com, launched 2024/25): plans Explorer $9/mo 30,000 credits 10 req/min; Essential $99/mo 450,000 credits 30 req/min; Advanced $900/mo 4,050,000 credits 200 req/min; promo doubles monthly credits for purchases/renewals by 2026-12-31. Credits charged per returned entity: live flight-positions light = 6 credits per flight returned (60 for 10 flights); empty responses cost 1 credit; flight-positions full, flight-tracks, flight-summary (light/full) and historic positions have their own per-record prices (exact values unverified; docs page did not render). Endpoints: live/flight-positions/{light|full} (filters by flight number, registration, callsign, bbox, airline, route), flight-tracks, flight-summary/{light|full} (departure/takeoff/arrival/landing times, reg, type), historic positions, airports, airlines, usage; sandbox available. At 6 credits/position and 90 positions per 3h flight (2-min cadence) that is 540 credits/flight, i.e. Essential covers ~830 flights/mo, Advanced ~7,500/mo (~$0.12/flight), comparable to AeroAPI /position at $0.90/flight only if polling is sparse.

findings.topic: 4. Weather: aviationweather.gov, NWS, Open-Meteo
findings.detail: aviationweather.gov Data API: https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/{metar|taf|airport|pirep|isigmet|gairmet|cwa|stationinfo}; params ids (comma list), format=json|xml|geojson|csv|raw, hours, bbox, taf=true on metar; up to 30 days history; 'All requests are rate limited to 100 requests per minute', most endpoints max 400 entries, abusers get blocked; custom User-Agent recommended. Bulk cache files (gzip) at https://aviationweather.gov/data/cache/ (metars.cache.csv.gz, metars.cache.xml.gz, tafs.cache.xml.gz, stations.cache.*): METARs/SIGMETs/PIREPs regenerated about once per minute, TAFs every 10 minutes, stations daily; NWS 'strongly recommends' the cache files over large custom queries. Recommendation: Cron Trigger pulls metars.cache.csv.gz every 5 min and tafs every 15 min into KV keyed by ICAO (global coverage, ~1 request each) rather than per-airport API calls. NWS api.weather.gov: mandatory User-Agent header (identify app + contact), flow GET /points/{lat},{lon} -> forecastGridData / /gridpoints/{wfo}/{x},{y}/forecast (and /forecast/hourly), /alerts/active?point= or ?area=; US only; rate limits unspecified ('generous'), 429 with retry after ~5 s; cache /points results but re-check occasionally since grid/office can change. Open-Meteo: free tier non-commercial only, 600 calls/min, 5,000/hour, 10,000/day, 300,000/month; commercial plans Standard 1M calls/mo, Professional 5M calls/mo (adds historical/climate/ensemble), Enterprise >50M; prices shown only in Stripe checkout, third-party listings say Standard $29/mo and Professional $99/mo; data CC BY 4.0 (attribution required). Use Open-Meteo as global non-aviation fallback (e.g. 'when to leave' surface conditions) on a paid plan.

findings.topic: 5. FAA NAS status and Eurocontrol
findings.detail: FAA: GET https://nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information returns XML (not JSON) with root <AIRPORT_STATUS_INFORMATION><Update_Time> and <Delay_type Name=...> sections: Ground Stop Programs (<Ground_Stop_List><Program> with ARPT, Reason, End_Time), Ground Delay Programs (<Ground_Delay_List><Ground_Delay> with ARPT, Reason, Avg, Max), General Arrival/Departure Delay Info (<Arrival_Departure_Delay_List><Delay> with ARPT, Reason, Min, Max, Trend, Type attribute), Airport Closures (<Airport_Closure_List><Airport> with ARPT, Reason, Start, Reopen); a <Dtd_File> reference; no cache headers. US government work, no key, no documented rate contract; the older SOA endpoint https://soa.smext.faa.gov/asws/api/airport/status/{IATA} has been unreliable/unreachable (Home Assistant issues) so treat as deprecated. Etiquette: single Cron Trigger fetch every 2-5 minutes (third parties recommend 5-15 min), diff on Update_Time, store in AirportState DOs; never poll from clients. Only covers US airports; NAS 'delay index' for non-US airports must derive from AeroDataBox delay stats or own flight-status aggregates. Eurocontrol NM B2B: SOAP/REST web services for ANSPs, aircraft operators, airports, ground handlers, CFSPs and AMCs; requires an online service request, PKI client certificate (.p12) for PREOPS then OPS after validation tests; two certificates per organisation/location free, EUR 200 per extra; a consumer app is not an eligible user class, so stub the interface and plan on AeroDataBox/own-derived European delay indices.

findings.topic: 6. BTS On-Time Performance ingest
findings.detail: Download: https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_{YYYY}_{M}.zip (M unpadded), one ZIP per month, ~30-60 MB zipped, ~600k rows (June 2026 = 607,577 flights), CSV with ~110 columns. Release lag 2-3 months (June 2026 released 2026-09-14/15; May 2026 released 2026-08-13). Key fields: Year, Quarter, Month, DayofMonth, DayOfWeek, FlightDate; Reporting_Airline, DOT_ID_Reporting_Airline, IATA_CODE_Reporting_Airline, Tail_Number, Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline; Origin/Dest (+AirportID, AirportSeqID, CityMarketID, CityName, State, Wac); CRSDepTime, DepTime, DepDelay, DepDelayMinutes, DepDel15, DepartureDelayGroups, DepTimeBlk, TaxiOut, WheelsOff, WheelsOn, TaxiIn, CRSArrTime, ArrTime, ArrDelay, ArrDelayMinutes, ArrDel15, ArrivalDelayGroups, ArrTimeBlk; Cancelled, CancellationCode (A carrier, B weather, C NAS, D security), Diverted; CRSElapsedTime, ActualElapsedTime, AirTime, Flights, Distance, DistanceGroup; CarrierDelay, WeatherDelay, NASDelay, SecurityDelay, LateAircraftDelay (since June 2003); gate-return and Div1-5 diversion fields (since Oct 2008). Only US reporting carriers (large domestic carriers, ~1% revenue threshold), domestic flights only; no international/foreign carriers. Licensing: BTS/TranStats data are US federal government works (17 USC 105) freely downloadable; a specific TranStats license page was not found so mark 'unverified (from memory)' and note NTAD products separately use CC-BY-NC 4.0 which does not apply here. Ingest approach: monthly Cron Trigger (or manual) job runs outside Workers (GitHub Actions/Container) that streams the ZIP, uses DuckDB or Python to aggregate, and upserts aggregate tables into Neon: ontime_route_carrier_month (carrier, flight_number, origin, dest, month -> n, on_time_pct, mean/median dep and arr delay, p90, cancel_pct, divert_pct, delay-cause minute shares), ontime_airport_hourblock_month (origin/dest x DepTimeBlk), ontime_flight_number_recent (last 12 months for the specific number). Do not load raw rows (7M rows/yr) into Neon; keep raw parquet in R2 if needed. Be polite: sequential downloads, 1-2 s between files, cache ETag.

findings.topic: 7. Reference data: airports, timezones, airlines, aircraft types
findings.detail: Airports: OurAirports CSVs (airports.csv 12.7 MB, runways.csv, airport-frequencies.csv, countries.csv, regions.csv, navaids.csv) at https://ourairports.com/data/ mirrored nightly on github.com/davidmegginson/ourairports-data; public domain; airports.csv fields: id, ident, type (large_airport|medium_airport|small_airport|heliport|seaplane_base|balloonport|closed_airport), name, latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, continent, iso_country, iso_region, municipality, scheduled_service, gps_code, icao_code, iata_code, local_code, home_link, wikipedia_link, keywords; NO timezone field. Timezones: (a) mwgg/Airports airports.json (~28-29k airports keyed by ICAO with iata, name, city, state, country, elevation, lat, lon, tz IANA; MIT) is the simplest join; (b) compute from lat/lon with geo-tz (exact polygons, ~892 KB data, Node fs based so run at build/import time, not in Workers) or tz-lookup (72 KB, ~10% mismatch on inhabited points, browser/Worker safe); (c) providers also return airport timezone (AeroAPI origin.timezone, AeroDataBox airport.timeZone) which can backfill. Recommendation: build a canonical airports table at import time from OurAirports + mwgg tz, validated with geo-tz, store IANA tz in Postgres, and ship a trimmed subset (scheduled_service=yes, ~4-5k rows) to mobile. Airlines/operators: OpenFlights airlines.dat (5,888 rows, last updated 2012, ODbL/DbCL) is stale; use Open Travel Data (OPTD, CC-BY) via benct/iata-utils IATA->ICAO/name mapping, plus AeroAPI /operators ($0.002 per 15 operators, ~$0.15 to dump the whole list) to build and refresh a carriers table (icao, iata, name, callsign, country); Wikidata as tie-breaker. Aircraft types: ICAO Doc 8643 designators are sold by ICAO but community extracts exist (github.com/ColtJD45/icao-aircraft-designator-list CSV, gists mapping ICAO<->IATA type codes, doc8643.com ~2,700 types); OpenFlights planes.dat has only 173 rows; AeroAPI /aircraft/types/{type} is $0.100 so only for lazy backfill. Codeshare mapping: no open static dataset; resolve at runtime from AeroAPI codeshares/codeshares_iata (operating flight carries the marketing list) and AeroDataBox codeshareStatus; persist a codeshare_alias table (marketing carrier+number+date -> operating carrier+number) learned from lookups so repeat searches skip the provider. AeroAPI /schedules with include_codeshares supports bulk pre-resolution for popular routes.

findings.topic: 8. Expected provider queries per tracked flight under the mandated cadence
findings.detail: Assumptions: flight added 14 days out, 3h block time, tracked until landing+2h; cadence: daily >7d (7 calls), daily 7d->48h (5 calls; mandate is silent for this band), hourly 48h->3h (45), every 10 min 3h->boarding at T-30m (15), every 2 min boarding->landing 3.5h (105), every 10 min for 2h after landing (12) = ~189 status polls. Pure polling on AeroAPI: 189 x $0.005 = $0.95 status + positions from AeroAPI every 2 min airborne 90 x $0.010 = $0.90 => ~$1.85/flight; with ADS-B community positions => $0.95. Alert-driven design (recommended): POST /alerts at T-48h (free), ~6-10 deliveries (filed, departure bundle, off, on, in, arrival bundle, gate/time changes) x $0.020 = $0.12-0.20; polling reduced to daily far-out (12), hourly 48h->3h (45), 10-min 3h->departure (15), 10-min airborne for ETA/gate refresh (18), 1 post-arrival (1) = ~91 x $0.005 = $0.46 => ~$0.60-0.66/flight list price on Standard, before 30%+ volume discounts above $1k/mo. Rate-limit check: Standard 5 result sets/s = 18,000/hour; 100k tracked flights/mo (~3.3k/day, ~137/hour departing) at ~91 calls each = ~12.5k calls/day average, fine, but the 2-min airborne cadence would break the 5/s cap once ~600 flights are airborne simultaneously, which is why positions must come from ADS-B and airborne status must be alert-driven. AeroDataBox: TIER 2 = 2 units/call; drop far-out polls (schedule-only) => ~170 calls = 340 units/flight; Growth ($99, 400k units) covers ~1,150 flights/mo, Scale ($499, 4M) ~11,700/mo (~$0.043/flight), 100k flights/mo = 34M units => Custom plan (~$4.3k at Scale unit rate). Infra-level estimate (provider only, list price): 1k flights/mo: AeroAPI ~$650 (or $100 minimum if lightly used) + AeroDataBox Growth $99; 10k: AeroAPI ~$6.5k list, ~$4.5k after 30% tier, + AeroDataBox Scale $499; 100k: AeroAPI ~$65k list, materially less after the 60-94% high-volume tiers (negotiate), or shift status polling to AeroDataBox Custom (~$5k) and keep AeroAPI for alerts+gates only (~$0.20-0.30/flight => $20-30k). Dedup factor: these are per operating-flight-instance costs; per-user cost falls with sharing (Flighty-style users track 2-4 flights/mo each, and popular flights are tracked by tens of users).

findings.topic: 8. Per-provider matrix: cost, quota, freshness, fields, exclusives
findings.detail: AeroAPI (Standard): $0.005/status set, $0.010/position, $0.020/alert delivery, $0.020/board, 5 sets/s, 10d back/2d fwd live, history 15d+ at 4x; freshness seconds (ADS-B/MLAT/radar/datalink, projected positions flagged); fields: sched/est/actual out/off/on/in, gates, terminals, baggage_claim, registration, aircraft_type, codeshares, inbound_fa_flight_id, progress_percent, route_distance, delays, boards, schedules, operators, airport delays, Foresight (Premium only). EXCLUSIVE or best: push alerts with hold detection, baggage claim, inbound aircraft link, blocked/position_only flags, oceanic/Aireon (Premium), historical tracks. AeroDataBox: $0.0002-0.001/status call, 5-20 req/s, live window ~1-2 days, schedules 365d fwd/back; freshness minutes-to-hours; fields: scheduled/revised/predicted/runway times, terminal, gate, checkInDesk, baggageBelt, codeshareStatus, isCargo, aircraft reg + modeS, airline iata/icao, FIDS (12h windows), aircraft by reg/icao24 (TIER 1), airport info with timezone, delay index + percentiles incl. history, webhooks (6h back/72h fwd). EXCLUSIVE or best: check-in desk, Mode-S hex directly on the flight object (solves reg->hex), airport delay percentiles and historical delay index for non-US airports, ultra-cheap dev/free tier. Community ADS-B (adsb.lol): $0, 'dynamic' rate limit, ~1-30 s freshness, fields: hex, flight (callsign), r, t, lat, lon, alt_baro, gs, track, baro_rate, squawk, seen; EXCLUSIVE: free positions; no ETA/gates; no oceanic; ODbL. FR24 API: $9-900/mo credits, 6 credits/light position; positions + summary + tracks; commercial-licensed alternative for positions. aviationweather.gov: $0, 100 req/min, METAR 1-min/TAF 10-min cache, global. NWS: $0, US only, User-Agent required, hourly/12h forecasts + alerts. Open-Meteo: $0 non-commercial/300k mo, $29-99 commercial, global surface forecast. FAA NAS: $0, XML, US ground stops/GDP/closures/delay trends. BTS: $0, monthly ZIP, US domestic history (on-time %, delay causes). Reference: OurAirports (PD), mwgg/Airports (MIT, tz), Mictronics/tar1090-db (ODC-By, hex<->reg<->type), OPTD/iata-utils (CC-BY airlines), Doc 8643 extracts (types).

flight-data-providers.recommendation: Primary-per-field-group for Phase 0/1: (1) Flight status, times, gates, terminals, baggage claim, codeshares, registration, inbound aircraft: FlightAware AeroAPI Standard ($100/mo min) as primary in production, driven by push alerts (PUT /alerts/endpoint once; POST /alerts per FlightTracker at T-48h with events departure, arrival, cancelled, diverted, filed, out/off/on/in, hold_start/hold_end, impending_departure [30,60], impending_arrival [15,30]) plus sparse GET /flights/{ident} polls; AeroDataBox as secondary/fallback and as the dev-mode live provider. Why: AeroAPI is the only provider with hold detection, baggage claim, inbound linkage and webhook alerts at $0.02/delivery, and its Standard tier explicitly licenses B2C; AeroDataBox has a 1-2 day live horizon and uneven non-US/EU coverage, so it cannot be primary for status but is 10-20x cheaper per call for schedule refresh and FIDS. (2) Live positions: community ADS-B via adsb.lol (ODbL, no non-commercial clause) as the AircraftPositionProvider default, resolving registration -> ICAO hex from a locally imported Mictronics/tar1090-db table (ODC-By) with AeroDataBox aircraft.modeS as a runtime backfill; degrade gracefully to AeroAPI /flights/{id}/position ($0.010) only when ADS-B returns nothing for 10+ minutes and the flight is not oceanic; keep FR24 API as a swappable commercial adapter. Do not use adsb.fi or airplanes.live (both non-commercial) or OpenSky (written license required) in production; keep adapters behind config for local dev only. (3) Airport boards: AeroDataBox FIDS (TIER 2, 12h window, ~$0.0005/call) primary; AeroAPI /airports/{id}/flights ($0.020) fallback. Boards are user-initiated and cached in KV for 5-10 min per airport+direction. (4) Weather: Cron-ingest aviationweather.gov cache files (METAR every 5 min, TAF every 15 min) into KV; NWS gridpoint forecasts for US airports (User-Agent 'Taxiway/x.y (ops@domain)'); Open-Meteo Standard plan for non-US surface forecasts. (5) Airport delay index: FAA NAS XML polled every 2-5 min by one Cron Trigger into AirportState DOs (US); AeroDataBox airport delay index for non-US; Eurocontrol stubbed (consumer apps are not an eligible user class). (6) Historical on-time: BTS PREZIP monthly batch aggregated off-Workers into Postgres aggregate tables. (7) Reference data: OurAirports (PD) + mwgg/Airports tz (MIT) validated with geo-tz at import; OPTD/iata-utils + AeroAPI /operators for carriers; Doc 8643 community CSV for aircraft types. FlightTracker key: operating carrier ICAO + flight number + scheduled departure date (origin local) + origin ICAO, with fa_flight_id stored as a provider external id (not the PK: unknown before first fetch, provider-specific, duplicated across diversion legs); marketing numbers map to this key via a learned codeshare_alias table. Dev-mode setup: AeroDataBox real adapter on the RapidAPI/API.Market free tier (400 units = 200 status calls/mo, 1 req/s) or Starter $19 for the team, AeroAPI mocked from recorded fixtures of the OpenAPI schemas (including alert webhook payloads replayed into the Worker), ADS-B adapter pointed at adsb.lol with a fixture mode, and the budget guard configured with the price table above so cost attribution logs are exercised from day one. Cadence amendment to argue in the Phase 0 plan: keep the mandated cadence as the polling ceiling but let provider alerts collapse the 2-minute airborne cadence to 10 minutes for status (positions still every 2 min from ADS-B); this both cuts AeroAPI cost from ~$1.85 to ~$0.60 per flight and keeps the 5 result-sets/s Standard cap from becoming the scaling bottleneck at ~600 concurrent airborne flights.
alternatives_rejected: FlightAware AeroAPI Premium ($1,000/mo min) at Phase 0: only needed for Foresight delay predictions, Aireon oceanic ADS-B and the 100/s rate cap; revisit when concurrent airborne tracked flights approach ~600 or when the ML delay-risk phase wants Foresight as a feature input.

AeroDataBox as the primary production status provider: live updates limited to ~1-2 days ahead, schedule refresh only every ~2 weeks, no inbound-aircraft link, no hold detection, 0% live coverage in several regions; keep as secondary/dev.
adsb.fi and airplanes.live as production position feeds: both state personal/educational non-commercial use only; airplanes.live has already started rejecting non-feeders.
OpenSky Network REST API for positions or aircraft metadata at runtime: commercial and any operational integration require a written license; the aircraft DB is explicitly 'not up to date'.

Flightradar24 API as the Phase 0 position provider: viable and commercially licensed, but at 6 credits per light position it costs ~$0.12/flight on the $900 plan and adds a second paid vendor before product-market fit; kept as a swappable adapter.
FAA SOA ASWS endpoint (soa.smext.faa.gov/asws): reported unreachable/unreliable; the nasstatus.faa.gov XML feed is the working public source.
Loading raw BTS rows into Neon: ~7M rows/year with ~110 columns is needless storage and query cost for a feature that only needs monthly aggregates per route/carrier/hour-block.
OpenFlights as the airline/route reference: airlines.dat last updated 2012 and routes.dat frozen in 2014 under ODbL; use OPTD (CC-BY) plus AeroAPI /operators instead.
Per-airport aviationweather.gov API calls: 100 req/min cap and NWS guidance both push toward the once-per-minute gzip cache files ingested by a single Cron Trigger.
risks: AeroAPI Standard rate cap (5 result sets/s) is a hard scaling ceiling: any design that polls per-flight every 2 minutes while airborne saturates at ~600 concurrent flights; mitigate with alert-driven updates, ADS-B positions, and a global token bucket inside a rate-limiter DO in front of the adapter.

AeroAPI push-alert delivery is not guaranteed (community reports of missed deliveries); the FlightTracker alarm schedule must remain the source of truth with alerts as accelerators, and a reconciliation poll must run at key milestones (scheduled departure +15 min, scheduled arrival +15 min).

inbound_fa_flight_id typically appears only once the inbound aircraft has landed, so the 'inbound aircraft leg' feature needs the registration-based /flights/{reg} query (extra $0.005-0.010 per flight) and will still be blank for many international/regional carriers.
Gate, terminal and baggage-claim coverage is carrier+airport dependent on both providers; the UI must treat these as optional and the delay-risk heuristics must not assume them.

Community ADS-B terms are shifting (adsb.lol plans mandatory API keys tied to feeding; airplanes.live already gating non-feeders); budget for either running feeders or paying FR24/AeroAPI for positions, and keep the AircraftPositionProvider interface strictly swappable.

adsb.lol data is ODbL: storing position history in Postgres could make the flight track table a 'derivative database' with share-alike obligations; keep positions ephemeral (DO memory/KV with short TTL) or obtain clarity before persisting tracks.

AeroDataBox unit accounting surprises: withFlightPlan doubles TIER 2 charges, date-range status lookups are TIER 3 (6 units), and FIDS windows cap at 12 hours; enforce parameter allowlists in the adapter.
Open-Meteo free tier is non-commercial; using it in a paid app without the Standard plan violates terms.

BTS license text for TranStats was not located (public-domain status inferred from US government work status); confirm before shipping the 'historical on-time' feature, and note BTS covers only US domestic reporting carriers so the feature is US-centric.
NWS API is US-only and rate limits are unspecified; a global forecast path (Open-Meteo paid) is required for non-US 'when to leave'.
FAA nasstatus feed is XML with no documented SLA or cache headers; parse defensively and alert on schema drift.

Historical AeroAPI data (>15 days old) costs 4-10x live prices and only 500k sets/month on Standard; logbook backfill for imported CSVs should use BTS aggregates and stored snapshots rather than /history/* at scale.
open_decisions_for_owner: Adopt alert-driven airborne cadence (status every 10 min via AeroAPI, positions every 2 min via ADS-B) instead of the literal 2-minute AeroAPI polling mandate; this changes cost from ~$1.85 to ~$0.60 per tracked flight and avoids the Standard rate cap.

Whether to run 2-4 Taxiway-operated ADS-B feeders (cheap SDR hardware) to secure adsb.lol/airplanes.live API-key access and AeroAPI Personal feeder credits, versus paying FR24 API or AeroAPI positions.
Whether ODbL share-alike exposure from adsb.lol is acceptable if flight tracks are persisted (share images, logbook replay), or positions stay ephemeral.
Commit to AeroAPI Standard from Phase 0 ($100/mo) versus mocked-only until Phase 1; recorded fixtures require at least one real key to capture.
Which AeroDataBox channel to buy: direct Starter/Growth (5-10 req/s, ADS-B feeding overage) vs RapidAPI/API.Market Mega (5-8 req/s, defined overage price) given the 5 req/s dev+prod combined need.
Non-US airport delay index source: AeroDataBox delay index (paid, uneven coverage) vs self-derived from tracked-flight status aggregates only.
Whether Premium/Foresight is the intended input for the ML delay-risk phase, which would set a $1,000/mo floor earlier than otherwise needed.
Handling of the 7-day to 48-hour polling band (mandate is silent): daily vs every 6 hours; affects ~5-20 calls per flight.
Confirm BTS TranStats reuse terms and whether the historical on-time feature launches US-only.

auth-billing.summary: Better Auth (v1.7.5, released 2026-09-14) is the right auth core for Taxiway: it runs on Cloudflare Workers behind Hono (official Hono integration, nodejs_compat/AsyncLocalStorage flag), has a first-party Drizzle adapter for Postgres (peer drizzle-orm ^0.45.2, pg ^8), and ships the exact plugin set the product needs as first-party code: anonymous (with onLinkAccount for the local-only-to-real-account upgrade), magic-link (hashed token storage, 5-min default expiry), Apple and Google social providers with native idToken sign-in (so expo-apple-authentication and the Google native SDK work without a browser round trip), an Expo client that persists the session cookie in expo-secure-store, database-backed rate limiting with cf-connecting-ip support, user deletion hooks, and an optional api-key plugin. Alternatives are weaker for this shape: Lucia was deprecated in March 2025; Auth.js has no Expo/React Native support; Clerk is a hosted user store ($25/mo Pro, 50k MRU free) that conflicts with Neon-as-source-of-truth and automated GDPR deletion; Supabase Auth is priced per MAU and is designed to sit on Supabase Postgres; hand-rolling means re-implementing Apple client-secret rotation, PKCE, token verification and account linking. Session transport on mobile should be the Better Auth Expo cookie-in-SecureStore model (not the bearer plugin), with sliding sessions (expiresIn 30d, updateAge 1d) and a short compact cookieCache to keep Neon reads off the hot path; a devices table (push tokens, Live Activity push-to-start tokens) is our own and is linked from session. For magic-link email, Cloudflare Email Service is still Beta, requires Workers Paid, gives 3,000 emails/mo then $0.35 per 1,000, but starts new accounts on a ramping daily quota, so Phase 0 should ship an EmailSender interface with Resend (3,000/mo free, 100/day cap; $20/mo for 50k) as the default and Cloudflare Email as a second adapter. RevenueCat is free to $2,500 MTR then 1%; react-native-purchases 10.10.0 (2026-09-17) needs an Expo dev build (no Expo Go); use users.id as app_user_id from first launch (anonymous server user included) so RevenueCat aliasing only happens on the anonymous-to-existing-account path; webhooks carry an Authorization header you choose plus optional HMAC (X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature t=,v1=), retry 5 times over ~2.5h, and must be deduplicated on event.id. Phase 0 should create billing_events, subscriptions and entitlements tables so Phase 5 is purely additive. Account deletion must be in-app (Apple rule since 2022-06-30) and should be a queued, hard-delete pipeline: revoke Apple/Google tokens, DELETE the RevenueCat customer, unsubscribe every FlightTracker DO, wipe the UserInbox DO, delete R2 objects, then delete the user row with FK cascade, keeping only anonymized billing_events and a deletion_log. api_tokens (hashed, scoped, revocable) and share_links (random opaque token, expiry, revocation, per-IP limits) are the two Phase 0 primitives that make the Phase 6 MCP endpoint and Phase 5 share pages additive. Admin surfaces sit behind Cloudflare Access with @hono/cloudflare-access 0.4.0 validating the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion JWT against the team JWKS with a mandatory aud check; service tokens show up as common_name with empty email.

findings.topic: Better Auth current version and release cadence
findings.detail: Latest stable is v1.7.5 (2026-09-14); the 1.6 line is still receiving patches (v1.6.33 same day). Five releases landed between 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-14. 1.7.x notes relevant to Workers: fixed async-context loss in Cloudflare Workers bundles (1.7.2); origin resolved from Host for dynamic baseURL (1.7.0); Drizzle Relations v2 entry point (1.7.0); schema validation at init on by default (1.7.3); Expo SecureStore switched to async access to stop iOS Keychain-locked crashes (1.7.0) and multibyte session fix (1.7.4); api-key plugin atomic state transitions (1.7.0); session cleanup on user deletion also purges secondary storage (1.6.26). npm peerDeps: pg ^8.0.0, drizzle-orm ^0.45.2 || >=1.0.0-rc.1 <2.0.0, drizzle-kit >=0.31.4. Pin an exact version in Phase 0 and upgrade deliberately; the cadence is high.

findings.topic: Better Auth on Cloudflare Workers + Hono
findings.detail: Official Hono integration: app.all('/api/auth/*', c => auth.handler(c.req.raw)); session middleware via auth.api.getSession({ headers: c.req.raw.headers }); CORS must be registered before the auth route with credentials:true and explicit origins that also appear in trustedOrigins. Workers require compatibility_flags ['nodejs_compat'] (or 'nodejs_als') for AsyncLocalStorage. Community package better-auth-cloudflare v0.3.1 (peer better-auth ^1.5.0) wires KV as secondaryStorage, Hyperdrive Postgres via Drizzle, autoDetectIpAddress from CF headers, and recommends per-request auth instance creation; its README warns KV is eventually consistent (60s+ propagation) and that with Better Auth 1.7 verification and rate-limit state must stay in the database because KV is not atomic. Hyperdrive docs: node-postgres >= 8.16.3 (recommended) or postgres.js >= 3.4.5, nodejs_compat flag with compatibility_date 2026-09-19 or later, create the client per request, Drizzle supported over pg; limit pool size (postgres.js max: 5).

findings.topic: Better Auth Drizzle adapter
findings.detail: drizzleAdapter(db, { provider: 'pg', schema, usePlural, schemaName }) from @better-auth/drizzle-adapter (relations-v2 entry point available; no migration needed to switch). `npx auth@latest generate` emits the Drizzle schema for core tables plus enabled plugins. Core tables: user(id, name, email unique, emailVerified, image, createdAt, updatedAt), session(id, userId, token unique, expiresAt, ipAddress, userAgent, createdAt, updatedAt), account(id, userId, providerId, accountId, accessToken, refreshToken, idToken, scope, expiresAt, password, createdAt, updatedAt; identity = providerId+accountId), verification(id, identifier, value, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt). advanced.database.generateId accepts false | 'serial' | 'uuid' | fn. Provider OAuth tokens in account are NOT encrypted by default; encrypt in databaseHooks.account.create.before.

findings.topic: Better Auth anonymous plugin (local-only mode upgrade path)
findings.detail: anonymous() adds user.isAnonymous boolean and endpoints POST /sign-in/anonymous and POST /delete-anonymous-user. Options: emailDomainName (default placeholder email {id}@anonymous.placeholder.invalid), generateRandomEmail, generateName, onLinkAccount({ anonymousUser, newUser }) called when an anonymous session then signs in/up via another method (email, social, magic link; PR #9548 fixed a case where it was not called on email-verification sign-in, so pin >= the fixed release), disableDeleteAnonymousUser (default false: anonymous user row is deleted after link). Calling signIn.anonymous() while already anonymous returns an error. Design: use onLinkAccount to re-key user_flights, devices, preferences, api_tokens to newUser.id in one transaction and to enqueue a DO re-subscribe job; set disableDeleteAnonymousUser:true and delete the anonymous row from a queue job only after row counts reach zero, so a failed migration cannot cascade-delete the user's data.

findings.topic: Better Auth Expo client and session transport
findings.detail: @better-auth/expo v1.7.5 (peer better-auth ^1.7.5; optional peers expo-secure-store >=12.5.0, expo-linking >=7, expo-web-browser >=14, expo-network >=8.0.7, expo-constants >=17). Server: plugins:[expo()], trustedOrigins:['taxiway://','taxiway://*'] (exp:// wildcards only in dev). Client: expoClient({ scheme, storage: SecureStore, storagePrefix }). The session cookie from Set-Cookie is persisted in SecureStore and replayed; for your own API calls attach `Cookie: await authClient.getCookie()` with credentials:'omit'. Requires Expo SDK 55+ (RN 0.83+), New Architecture, Metro package exports (default since SDK 53). Expo web supported with the same config (real cookies). Native Apple/Google: obtain provider idToken client-side, call authClient.signIn.social({ provider, idToken:{ token, nonce, accessToken } }); no redirect. Bearer plugin exists (issues token in set-auth-token header, client sends Authorization: Bearer) but docs say use cautiously and only for APIs that cannot use cookies; not needed for the Expo path. Session defaults: expiresIn 7d, updateAge 1d (sliding), freshAge 1d; cookieCache { enabled, maxAge, strategy:'compact'|'jwt'|'jwe' } avoids a DB read per request; listSessions/revokeSession/revokeOtherSessions APIs; with secondaryStorage sessions go to KV unless storeSessionInDatabase:true. Current Expo: SDK 57 stable (2026-06-30), SDK 58 beta (2026-09-15).

findings.topic: Sign in with Apple via Better Auth
findings.detail: socialProviders.apple needs clientId (Services ID, e.g. com.taxiway.web.si, used for web), clientSecret (ES256 JWT signed with the .p8 key: iss=Team ID, sub=client id, aud=https://appleid.apple.com, exp <= 6 months / 15,777,000 s; generate with jose and rotate), and appBundleIdentifier (iOS bundle id) so idToken audience validation accepts native tokens. Apple emits email/name only on first authorization. HTTPS required (no localhost) and https://appleid.apple.com must be in trustedOrigins. expo-apple-authentication (iOS/tvOS only; ios.usesAppleSignIn:true) signInAsync({ requestedScopes:[FULL_NAME, EMAIL], nonce, state }) returns user (stable id), identityToken, authorizationCode, email, fullName (first sign-in only); getCredentialStateAsync(user) reports AUTHORIZED/REVOKED/NOT_FOUND/TRANSFERRED. Apple token revocation for account deletion: POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke with client_id, client_secret, token (refresh_token or access_token from /auth/token), token_type_hint; 200 with empty body. To be able to revoke later you must exchange the authorizationCode for a refresh_token at sign-in and store it (encrypted) in accounts.refresh_token.

findings.topic: Google sign-in via Better Auth
findings.detail: socialProviders.google supports clientId as an array [web, iOS, Android]; the array widens idToken verification but the auth-code (web) flow uses only the first entry with a single clientSecret. Native: const { idToken, accessToken } = await GoogleSignin.signIn(); authClient.signIn.social({ provider:'google', idToken:{ token, accessToken } }). accessType:'offline' + prompt:'select_account consent' only if refresh tokens are needed (they are not for login; Gmail sync in Phase 3 should use a separate email_connections table and its own consent). @react-native-google-signin/google-signin: free 'Original' module (Android + iOS only, built on the deprecated legacy Android Google Sign-In SDK, public npm) returns idToken only when webClientId is configured; paid 'Universal Sign In' module (Android, iOS, web, macOS; modern Credential Manager; private npm registry; Expo SDK >= 52.0.40; may be free for EAS customers) is the maintained path. Alternative: expo-auth-session browser PKCE flow (free, no native SDK, worse UX).

findings.topic: Better Auth magic link, rate limiting, deletion hooks
findings.detail: magicLink({ sendMagicLink({ email, url, token, metadata }, ctx), expiresIn (default 300 s), disableSignUp, generateToken, storeToken: 'plain'|'hashed'|custom }); client signIn.magicLink({ email, callbackURL, newUserCallbackURL, errorCallbackURL }); verification via GET /magic-link/verify?token=; tokens live in the verification table (secondary storage with getAndDelete gives atomic single use). Rate limit: default window 60 s / max 100, on in production; storage 'memory' (useless on Workers) | 'database' (rateLimit table via migrate) | 'secondary-storage' | customStorage.consume(); customRules per path e.g. '/sign-in/email': { window:10, max:3 }; advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders:['cf-connecting-ip']; X-Retry-After header on 429. user.deleteUser { enabled, sendDeleteAccountVerification, beforeDelete (throw APIError to block), afterDelete }. accountLinking { enabled (default true), trustedProviders, allowDifferentEmails, updateUserInfoOnLink, disableImplicitLinking }. Admin plugin (optional) adds user.role/banned/banReason/banExpires and session.impersonatedBy with adminRoles/adminUserIds. Multi-session plugin is browser-cookie oriented (multiple accounts per browser, maximumSessions 5) and is not needed for a consumer mobile app.

findings.topic: Better Auth api-key plugin (evaluated for MCP tokens)
findings.detail: Reference page: apikey table with id, key (hashed by default; disableKeyHashing exists with a security warning), configId, referenceId (owner), name, start (display prefix chars), expiresAt, permissions (JSON Record<string,string[]>), metadata, remaining/refill counters, rateLimit* fields, createdAt/updatedAt. Defaults: header x-api-key (customAPIKeyGetter available), defaultKeyLength 64, startingCharacters shouldStore true / charactersLength 6, enableSessionForAPIKeys false, keyExpiration defaultExpiresIn/min/max, permissions.defaultPermissions. Verification via POST /api-key/verify; /api-key/delete checks ownership. Hash algorithm is not stated on the page. Usable, but the schema is plugin-owned and geared to quota/refill; a 9-column api_tokens table under our control is simpler to reason about for the MCP threat model.

findings.topic: Alternatives: Lucia, Auth.js, Clerk, Supabase Auth
findings.detail: Lucia: deprecated March 2025; site (updated July 2026) now offers a single-file auth_session.ts and the Auth Book, not a library. Auth.js: integrations are Next/Astro/Express/Fastify/Nuxt/Qwik/Remix/SolidStart/SvelteKit plus a community Hono middleware; no Expo/React Native client. Clerk: Free 50,000 MRU per app (raised 2026-02-05; MRU = users who return 24h after signup), Pro $25/mo ($20 annual) with 50k MRU then $0.02/user; add-ons $100/mo each; Billing 0.7% of volume; @clerk/expo with expo-secure-store token cache, native Apple/Google SSO and email code/link, but native components need a dev build and enabling the Native API bypasses browser CAPTCHA. Clerk owns the user store, so deletion/export must fan out to a second system and anonymous/guest sessions are not a documented primitive. Supabase Auth: 50k MAU free, Pro $25/mo with 100k MAU then $0.00325/MAU, anonymous sign-ins included; it is designed around Supabase Postgres, not Neon+Hyperdrive.

findings.topic: Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending)
findings.detail: Status: Email Sending is Beta for outbound transactional email; Email Routing (inbound) is GA. Requires Workers Paid plan for arbitrary recipients; Workers Free can only send to verified destination addresses. Pricing: 3,000 outbound emails/month included per account, then $0.35 per 1,000; rejected/suppressed sends do not count. Limits: 50 recipients per message, 5 MiB message (25 MiB to verified destinations), 16 KB custom headers, 30 domains per zone; new accounts start on a conservative daily quota that scales with sending behaviour and deliverability. Domain must be a zone on Cloudflare DNS; onboarding auto-creates MX (bounces), SPF, DKIM and DMARC records (5-15 min propagation). Binding: wrangler send_email:[{ name:'EMAIL', remote:true }]; env.EMAIL.send({ from, to, subject, text, html }) returns { messageId }; also REST /accounts/{id}/email/sending/send and SMTP smtps://smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465. Inbound Email Routing handler email() is the natural home for the forward-to-address import in Phase 3.

findings.topic: Resend and Postmark pricing
findings.detail: Resend: Free 3,000 emails/month with a 100/day cap; Pro $20/mo for 50,000 or $35/mo for 100,000, 10 domains, 30-day retention, 5 webhook endpoints; Scale from $90/mo (100k) to $1,150/mo (2.5M), 1,000 domains, 10 webhooks. Plain HTTPS REST, works from Workers. Postmark: 100 emails/month free forever; Basic $15/mo for 10,000 (+$1.80/1k), Pro $16.50/mo (+$1.30/1k), Platform $18/mo (+$1.20/1k); dedicated IP from $50/mo at 300k+/month. Both are Workers-compatible via fetch. Magic-link volume estimate: at 100k MAU with ~1 magic-link login/user/month you are at ~100k emails/month, i.e. Resend Pro $35, Postmark ~$135, Cloudflare ~$34.

findings.topic: RevenueCat SDK for Expo / React Native
findings.detail: react-native-purchases 10.10.0 published 2026-09-17 (npm latest); peer react >=16.6.3, react-native >=0.73.0, optional react-native-web. Expo: install with `npx expo install react-native-purchases react-native-purchases-ui`; Expo Go is not supported for real purchases (only a Preview API Mode), a development build with expo-dev-client via EAS is required; no config plugin needed. Bundle id / application id must match RevenueCat and store config. Web: only RevenueCat Billing (Stripe) works; getProducts/purchaseProduct/restorePurchases are unsupported on web, so the web app should show subscription management via a Stripe-backed RevenueCat Billing paywall or defer web purchases.

findings.topic: RevenueCat pricing
findings.detail: Free up to $2,500 monthly tracked revenue (MTR); above that Pro is 1% of tracked revenue with no minimum stated; all features (SDKs, webhooks, REST API, paywalls, experiments, charts, integrations) included on both. Enterprise is custom. The 1% is on gross tracked revenue before store commission, so effective take on net revenue is higher (roughly 1.18% at 15% Apple SBP tier).

findings.topic: RevenueCat customer identity and app_user_id strategy
findings.detail: Without a custom id the SDK mints $RCAnonymousID:<random> (cached on device, regenerated on reinstall). Custom App User ID: Purchases.configure({ apiKey, appUserID }) at launch or Purchases.logIn(id) later; logOut() mints a fresh anonymous id. Rules: unique, non-guessable (UUIDs recommended), max 100 chars, no '/', not blocked words (null, anonymous, guest), never email/IDFA/PII. logIn from an anonymous id aliases it into the custom id if the custom id does not already exist; if both exist, merge follows the project Restore Behavior: 'Transfer to new App User ID' (default; purchases move, only one customer has access at a time, TRANSFER webhook fires), 'Transfer if there are no active subscriptions', or 'Keep with original App User ID' (blocks transfers and throws on restore from another id; on iOS this can strand a new subscription because the Apple receipt is per Apple Account). Webhooks show one original_app_user_id and the rest in aliases[]; look users up by both. Recommendation: configure with appUserID = users.id from first launch (the anonymous Better Auth user already has a stable UUID), so RevenueCat never sees $RCAnonymousID and aliasing only occurs on anonymous-to-existing-account merge, where you call Purchases.logIn(existingUserId) after onLinkAccount succeeds.

findings.topic: RevenueCat webhooks
findings.detail: Configure at Integrations > Webhooks with an HTTPS URL and an optional Authorization header value of your choosing that RevenueCat sends verbatim on every POST (compare with constant-time equality). Optional HMAC signing: header X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix_ts>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex> computed over the raw body bytes combined with the timestamp using the integration signing secret; verify on raw bytes before JSON.parse, constant-time compare, reject if |now - t| > 5 min. Respond 200 within 60 s; non-200 is retried 5 times at 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 minutes; at-least-once delivery, dedupe on event.id; ordering not guaranteed; can be scoped to one app or all apps in a project. Payload common fields: api_version, event.id, event.type, event_timestamp_ms, app_id, app_user_id, original_app_user_id, aliases[], product_id, entitlement_ids[], period_type (TRIAL|INTRO|NORMAL|PROMOTIONAL|PREPAID), purchased_at_ms, expiration_at_ms, environment (SANDBOX|PRODUCTION), store, price (USD), currency, transaction_id, original_transaction_id, subscriber_attributes. Event types: TEST, INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, CANCELLATION, UNCANCELLATION, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE, SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED, EXPIRATION, BILLING_ISSUE, PRODUCT_CHANGE, SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED, REFUND_REVERSED, INVOICE_ISSUANCE, TRANSFER, SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS (deprecated), TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT, VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION, EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT, PURCHASE_REDEEMED, PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED, PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED. RevenueCat's own guidance: after a webhook, call the REST API for the current customer state rather than reconstructing it from event deltas.

findings.topic: RevenueCat REST API v2
findings.detail: Base https://api.revenuecat.com/v2, Authorization: Bearer <v2 secret key> (v1 keys do not work). GET /projects/{project_id}/customers/{customer_id}?expand=active_entitlements returns the customer with active entitlements in one call; subscription endpoints exist per customer. Rate limits: customer information 480 req/min, charts/metrics 25/min, project config 60/min, with Retry-After on 429. DELETE /projects/{project_id}/customers/{customer_id} erases all customer data and is documented as sufficient for GDPR erasure; it does not cancel Apple/Google/Stripe subscriptions (Google can be cancelled via API first; Apple cannot; Stripe must be cancelled in Stripe). Promotional entitlement grants are still documented on the v1 path POST /v1/subscribers/{app_user_id}/entitlements/{entitlement_id}/promotional (secret key, fixed duration enum); confirm whether a v2 equivalent exists before Phase 5.

findings.topic: RevenueCat sandbox testing
findings.detail: Three tiers: RevenueCat Test Store (auto-provisioned per project, no platform accounts, use first), then platform sandboxes, then production. Apple: sandbox testers in App Store Connect > Users and Access; StoreKit Configuration file in Xcode linked to a duplicated scheme, products must also exist in RevenueCat, upload the StoreKit test public certificate to RevenueCat (Project > Apps > StoreKit testing framework); sandbox renewals are compressed (1 month = 5 min, 1 year = 1 h, max 12 renewals/day; TestFlight renews once per 24 h since Dec 2024). Google: add license testers under Play Console Settings > License testing, publish a signed build to a closed testing track, tester must open the opt-in URL or products will not load, device must have exactly one license-tester Google account and a PIN; sandbox renewals every 5 min (weekly/monthly) or 30 min (annual), max 6 renewals. Dashboard has a 'View Sandbox Data' toggle; webhook events carry environment=SANDBOX so the backend must key entitlements by environment and ignore sandbox in production unless the user is flagged as a tester.

findings.topic: Apple in-app account deletion requirement
findings.detail: Since 2022-06-30 any App Store app that supports account creation must offer in-app account deletion that removes the entire account record and associated personal data (deactivation alone is insufficient); data you are legally required to retain may be kept; the option must be offered to all users regardless of jurisdiction. Sign in with Apple users: revoke tokens via POST /auth/revoke. Subscriptions: tell users billing continues through Apple, require or strongly guide them to cancel first (showManageSubscriptions / https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions), optionally allow scheduling deletion for subscription end but always offer immediate deletion. Apple also sends Sign in with Apple server-to-server notifications (consent-revoked, account-delete, email-disabled/enabled) as a JWT with an events claim to an endpoint registered under the App ID; handle consent-revoked by unlinking the Apple account and account-delete by triggering the same deletion pipeline (event detail from memory, unverified beyond the doc title).

findings.topic: Cloudflare Access for admin routes
findings.detail: Access injects the JWT in header Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion (and cookie CF_Authorization for browsers). Validate RS256 signature against https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs (match kid in public_certs; keys rotate every 6 weeks with a 7-day overlap), iss = https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com, exp, and aud = the application's AUD tag. Service tokens (CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret headers, secret shown once, duration in hours e.g. 8760h) are exchanged by Access into a JWT whose common_name claim carries the token name and whose email is empty. @hono/cloudflare-access v0.4.0 (peer hono >=4): import { cloudflareAccess } from '@hono/cloudflare-access'; app.use('/admin/*', cloudflareAccess('team-name', ['<aud>'])) exposes c.get('accessPayload') (email, common_name, ...); aud is optional for backwards compatibility but omitting it enables cross-application token replay inside the same account (documented as a real vulnerability class), so pass it. Returns 401 on missing/invalid/expired tokens or wrong aud, 500 if the team does not exist. Current Hono is 4.13.8.

findings.topic: Phase 0 auth tables (proposed, Drizzle pg, snake_case via usePlural + column mapping)
findings.detail: users: id uuid PK (advanced.database.generateId:'uuid'), name text, email citext/text unique, email_verified bool not null default false, image text, is_anonymous bool not null default false, role text not null default 'user', locale text, time_zone text, plan text not null default 'free' (denormalized cache from entitlements), deletion_requested_at timestamptz, deleted_at timestamptz, created_at/updated_at timestamptz. sessions: id uuid PK, user_id uuid FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, token text unique, expires_at timestamptz, ip_address text, user_agent text, device_id uuid FK devices ON DELETE SET NULL (custom additionalField), impersonated_by uuid null, created_at/updated_at; auth-billing.recommendation: 1. Auth core: Better Auth 1.7.5 (pinned) on Hono in the API Worker, Drizzle adapter (provider 'pg') over node-postgres via Hyperdrive to Neon, one auth instance built per request from env bindings. Plugins: anonymous, magicLink (storeToken 'hashed', expiresIn 600), expo, socialProviders apple (Services ID for web, appBundleIdentifier for iOS, ES256 client secret generated from a Workers secret .p8 and cached) and google (clientId array [web, iOS, Android]). Rate limiting storage 'database' with cf-connecting-ip and custom rules for /sign-in/magic-link and /sign-in/anonymous, backed by an edge WAF rate-limit rule on /api/auth/*. Do not add the bearer, multi-session, admin or api-key plugins in Phase 0; each is additive later. Why: it is the only option that is first-party on Workers, first-party with Drizzle/Postgres, first-party on Expo, and first-party for anonymous-to-real-account linking, while keeping the user table in Neon so GDPR deletion and DO subscriber cleanup are one transaction plus one queue job. 2. Sessions on mobile: use the Expo plugin's cookie-in-SecureStore transport (not bearer); session.expiresIn 30 days, updateAge 1 day (sliding), cookieCache enabled with strategy 'compact' and maxAge 300 s so the hot path (every flight read) does not hit Neon; sessions stay in Postgres (no KV secondary storage in Phase 0 because KV is eventually consistent and cannot serve verification/rate-limit atomically). Add device_id as an additionalField on session so a device row can be linked at registration; devices table is ours (push tokens, Live Activity push-to-start token, install_id). Refresh is implicit via sliding expiry; there is no separate refresh token, which is fine because the cookie is in Keychain/Keystore, and revocation is a DB row delete. 3. Local-only mode: implement as a server-side anonymous user created lazily (first time the app needs a FlightTracker subscription or push), because push and the shared-flight architecture require a subscriber identity; the client must work before that call completes. Upgrade path: onLinkAccount re-keys all user-owned rows to newUser.id in one transaction, enqueues a DO re-subscribe job (per user_flight: FlightTracker.resubscribe(old,new)), then Purchases.logIn(newUser.id); set disableDeleteAnonymousUser:true and delete the anonymous row from the queue job after verifying zero remaining rows. Pick RevenueCat restore behavior 'Transfer to new App User ID'. 4. Native sign-in: expo-apple-authentication with a server-generated nonce, exchange authorizationCode server-side to obtain and encrypt the Apple refresh_token for later revocation; Google via the maintained Universal Sign In module if EAS makes it free, else the free Original module with webClientId (accept the legacy-SDK risk) or expo-auth-session as the zero-native fallback. 5. Email: EmailSender interface in packages/shared with two adapters; default Resend in Phase 0 (deliverability track record, 3,000/mo free, trivial from Workers), Cloudflare Email Service adapter behind a flag to switch once it exits Beta and the account's daily quota has ramped (it is cheapest at scale: $0.35/1k after 3,000 and inbound routing is what Phase 3 forward-to-address needs anyway). 6. RevenueCat: app_user_id = users.id from first launch; webhook Worker route verifies both the Authorization header and the HMAC signature on raw bytes with a 5-minute tolerance, inserts billing_events by event.id (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), returns 200, and processes from a Queue by calling GET /v2/projects/{p}/customers/{id}?expand=active_entitlements and upserting entitlements; the API authorizes free-tier limits from the entitlements table, never from the client. Create billing_events, subscriptions, entitlements in Phase 0 so Phase 5 only adds the paywall and the webhook route. 7. Deletion/export: in-app delete triggers Better Auth deleteUser with beforeDelete that sets deletion_requested_at and enqueues the pipeline (Apple /auth/revoke, Google revoke, email-sync token revoke, RevenueCat DELETE customer, per-flight DO unsubscribe, UserInbox DO deleteAll, R2 prefix delete, then hard delete with FK cascade); retain only anonymized billing_events (user_id SET NULL) for financial records and a PII-free deletion_log. Export is a queued job to R2 with a 24-hour signed URL. Warn about active subscriptions before deletion and deep-link to store subscription management. 8. Tokens: api_tokens (SHA-256 hash, scopes[], expires_at, revoked_at, last_used) is the Phase 0 primitive for the Phase 6 MCP endpoint (Authorization: Bearer twy_..., 401 on revoked, per-token and per-IP limits); share_links is a separate table with an opaque random token, expiry, revocation and view counting; both are created in Phase 0 migrations even if unused. 9. Admin: separate admin hostname routed to the same Worker, protected by Cloudflare Access; @hono/cloudflare-access with team name and AUD tag from vars, service tokens for CI/cron scripts identified by common_name; no application-level admin roles in Phase 0.
alternatives_rejected: Clerk: fastest to demo and 50k MRU free, but a hosted user store outside Neon makes the anonymous-to-account merge, DO subscriber re-keying, and automated GDPR deletion two-system problems; $25/mo Pro plus $100/mo add-ons; native Expo API bypasses CAPTCHA; guest/anonymous sessions are not a documented primitive.
Supabase Auth: MAU-priced ($0.00325/MAU above 100k on Pro) and built to run on Supabase Postgres; using it standalone against Neon+Hyperdrive is unsupported territory.
Auth.js: no Expo/React Native client and only a community Hono middleware.
Lucia: deprecated March 2025, now a copy-paste file; fine as reading material for a hand-rolled design, not as a dependency.

Hand-rolled auth: you would reimplement Apple ES256 client secrets, idToken verification for three Google client ids, magic-link token hashing, account linking, and rate limiting; Better Auth is boring enough and the schema is plain Drizzle tables you own.
Better Auth bearer plugin for mobile: the docs discourage it outside cookie-less APIs; the Expo plugin already stores the cookie in SecureStore, and bearer would add a second transport to secure.

KV as Better Auth secondaryStorage in Phase 0: KV's eventual consistency delays revocation by 60s+ and cannot host verification/rate-limit atomically; cookieCache gives most of the read reduction with none of the semantics risk.

Better Auth api-key plugin for MCP tokens: workable, but its plugin-owned schema (configId/referenceId, refill counters) and x-api-key convention are more than the MCP endpoint needs; a small owned api_tokens table is easier to threat-model.
Cloudflare Email Service as the Phase 0 default: still Beta, Workers Paid required, and a ramping daily quota on new accounts is the wrong risk profile for an auth-critical email path.
Postmark as default: best deliverability reputation but 100 emails/month free and $15/10k is 4x Resend at the volumes Phase 0-2 will see; keep as a swap-in adapter.

Using $RCAnonymousID and Purchases.logIn on every account upgrade: forces RevenueCat aliasing on the common path and produces webhooks keyed by anonymous ids; using users.id from first launch avoids it.
risks: Better Auth release velocity (5 releases in 5 days, 1.6 and 1.7 lines in parallel) and history of Workers/Expo-specific regressions (async context loss, SecureStore crashes, multibyte cookie bug); pin exact versions, run the Miniflare integration tests on upgrade, and keep the auth surface small.

onLinkAccount edge cases: PR #9548 shows it was previously skipped on some email-verification sign-in paths; test the anonymous-to-magic-link, anonymous-to-Apple, and anonymous-to-existing-account merges explicitly, including the duplicate user_flights unique-constraint case.

Anonymous account abuse: every anonymous user can subscribe to FlightTracker DOs and consume provider budget; rate-limit /sign-in/anonymous per IP and install_id, cap flights per anonymous user, and plan App Attest / Play Integrity attestation before public launch.

Apple private email relay and first-sign-in-only email/name: if the first Apple sign-in fails after Apple returns the credential you never get the email again; persist it before any other work and store the Apple refresh_token or deletion-time revocation will be impossible.
Free @react-native-google-signin Original module is built on the deprecated legacy Android SDK; Google may break it, and the maintained Universal module is paid unless EAS covers it.
Cloudflare Email Sending is Beta with an undocumented starting daily quota; do not make it the only path for magic links until GA.
RevenueCat webhooks are at-least-once, unordered, and retried for ~2.5 hours; without event.id idempotency and refresh-from-API you will corrupt entitlement state on TRANSFER and PRODUCT_CHANGE.

RevenueCat customer deletion does not cancel Apple subscriptions; deleting an account with an active Apple subscription leaves the user paying with no product, which Apple review guidelines expect you to warn about.
Cloudflare Access without aud validation accepts JWTs minted for any other Access app in the account; the Hono middleware makes aud optional, so enforce it in config review.
OAuth tokens in the account table are plaintext by default; the encryption hook must exist before the first real Apple/Google sign-in or a later backfill is needed.
open_decisions_for_owner: Local-only mode semantics: truly offline (no server identity until upgrade, so no push and no shared FlightTracker subscription) versus a server-side anonymous user created on first flight add (recommended). This determines whether the free tier can deliver push at all without sign-in.
Google native sign-in module: pay for Universal Sign In (or confirm EAS entitlement), accept the free legacy-SDK module, or use expo-auth-session browser PKCE on all platforms.
Email provider default for magic links: Resend (recommended for Phase 0) vs Postmark vs Cloudflare Email Service now (accept Beta and quota ramp for lower cost and single-vendor simplicity).

Session lifetime: 30-day sliding sessions with 5-minute cookie cache (recommended) versus Better Auth's 7-day default; and whether revocation latency of up to 5 minutes from cookieCache is acceptable.
Deletion timing: immediate hard delete on request (recommended, queue completes within minutes) versus a 7-14 day grace window with undo; both satisfy Apple as long as immediate is offered.
RevenueCat restore behavior: 'Transfer to new App User ID' (recommended for a consumer app) versus 'Transfer if no active subscriptions'.
Whether to adopt the Better Auth api-key plugin for MCP tokens or the owned api_tokens table (recommended).
Whether to add the Better Auth admin plugin (roles, bans, impersonation) in Phase 0 or rely solely on Cloudflare Access plus service tokens (recommended for Phase 0).
Whether web purchases are in scope (requires RevenueCat Billing via Stripe) or the web app only reads entitlement state.
Postgres id strategy: uuid v4 via Better Auth generateId 'uuid' versus DB-generated uuid v7 (generateId:false) for index locality on high-write tables.

cost-model.summary: Provider cost dominates at every scale (78-91% of monthly spend); infrastructure on Cloudflare is nearly free until 100k flights/month. The mandated cadence, read literally (hourly from 7 days out), yields 308 status polls per flight for a 3h flight added 14 days out; relaxing 7d-48h to every 6h gives 208, and daily gives 193. Two verified facts reshape the design: (1) FlightAware AeroAPI GET /flights/{ident} only returns departures up to ~2 days in the future, so every pre-48h refresh on AeroAPI must use /schedules at $0.020/result set (4x the $0.005 status poll), which makes AeroDataBox the only sane pre-48h source; (2) AeroAPI Push Alert Delivery costs $0.020 per delivered alert, so an alert is worth 4 status polls, and the winning pattern is alerts + a sparse confirmation poll inside 48h (about 30 polls + ~8 alerts = $0.31 list per flight) rather than 2-minute polling (about $0.90-1.45 list). With AeroAPI's published marginal volume discounts (30% to 94%), the hybrid model costs about $310 / $2,240 / $8,550 per month in AeroAPI fees at 1k / 10k / 100k flights, and all-in monthly totals are roughly $400 / $2,460 / $10,240, i.e. $0.40 / $0.25 / $0.10 per tracked flight. Cloudflare DO + Workers + Queues + KV come to under $2 at 10k and about $170 at 100k; Neon, Sentry, EAS and RevenueCat are the next tier of fixed-ish cost. ADS-B community position APIs are free but adsb.fi and airplanes.live explicitly forbid commercial use and adsb.fi enforces 1 req/s; position polling must be batched (multi-hex per request) in a single poller DO, and a commercial position source is an open decision before 10k. Budget guard numbers are given as per-flight lifetime/day caps in billable-event units and a global daily list-price cap with 70/90/100% thresholds.

findings.topic: Cadence derivation: status polls per tracked flight (no alerts)
findings.detail: Windows relative to scheduled departure D, flight duration F=180 min, boarding = D-40 min, tracking stops at arrival+120 min. Formula: N_status = W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 + W5 + W6 where W1 = max(0, lead_days-7) daily polls; W2 = (min(lead_days,7)*24 - 48)/interval_h polls for the 7d..48h window (interval_h is the open assumption: brief says 'daily beyond 7 days' and 'hourly within 48h', the 7d..48h gap is unspecified; ASSUMPTION A = hourly, ASSUMPTION B = every 6h, C = daily); W3 = 45 hourly polls (48h..3h); W4 = 140/10 = 14 polls (3h..boarding, every 10 min); W5 = (40 + F)/2 = 220/2 = 110 polls (boarding through landing, every 2 min); W6 = 120/10 = 12 polls (landing..arrival+2h, ASSUMPTION every 10 min to capture gate-in and baggage claim). Results: 14-day lead: A = 7+120+45+14+110+12 = 308; B = 7+20+45+14+110+12 = 208; C = 7+5+45+14+110+12 = 193. 3-day lead: A = 0+24+45+14+110+12 = 205; B = 0+4+45+14+110+12 = 185. 30-day lead: A = 23+120+45+14+110+12 = 324; B = 23+20+45+14+110+12 = 224. Observation: W5 (in-flight 2-min polling) is 53% of the B total; W2-hourly is the other big lump and buys nothing (schedule/aircraft data beyond 48h changes at most daily). Recommendation: adopt C (daily) for 7d..48h and 5-min status polls during cruise (position comes from ADS-B), giving 7+5+45+14+ (60/2=30 boarding-to-off + 150/5=30 cruise-to-landing) + 12 = 143 polls without alerts.
