findings.topic: Row volume and storage estimate per tracked flight (input to the cost model)
findings.detail: Per tracked flight in Postgres: flight_instances 1 row (~1.2 KB with indexes), flight_designators 1-4 rows, flight_events ~30-60 rows (~250 B each, ~12 KB), provider_calls ~40-80 rows (~300 B each, ~20 KB; the count matches the refresh-cadence budget of ~60 status polls plus alert callbacks when AeroAPI alerts are used, more if AeroDataBox polling only), delay_predictions ~6-10 rows (~1 KB each with features), flight_tracks 1 row (~10 KB), delay_outcomes 1 row, plus per subscriber ~8 notifications and ~10 deliveries (~2 KB). Roughly 50 KB per flight before retention; at 1k/10k/100k flights per month that is ~50 MB/500 MB/5 GB per month of inserts, with 90-day retention on the append tables giving a steady state of roughly 0.15/1.5/15 GB (well inside Neon's smaller plans; the exact plan pricing belongs to the infra-cost agent). DO: ~600-900 rows written per flight (positions dominate; each index write counts), so 100k flights/month is ~80M rows written, ~$30/month over the 50M included at $1/M; reads are negligible because subscriber reads hit KV. KV: the snapshot pattern makes reads scale with subscribers x polling, not with flights.

schema-design.recommendation: Adopt the schema as laid out: Postgres (Neon PG18, Drizzle pg-core) as the system of record with ~52 tables; FlightTracker DO SQLite as the only home for positions, the event outbox, subscriber list and budget counters; KV for provider-derived caches and the read fan-out snapshot; R2 for blobs with prefix lifecycle rules; Analytics Engine for audit/analytics and the dashboard copy of provider cost. Pin drizzle-orm 0.45.2 + drizzle-kit 0.31.10 (`latest`) for Phase 0 and restrict usage to APIs that are identical in 1.0-rc (core query builder with explicit joins, `check`, `index/uniqueIndex`, `sql` defaults, `generatedAlwaysAs(sql)`, `$onUpdate`); avoid the v0 relational query builder and `.enableRLS()` so the v1 upgrade is mechanical. Use PG18's native `uuidv7()` as the column default and app-generated UUIDv7 for offline/DO-born rows. Use `text + check` for every enumeration, timestamptz for every instant with a single origin-local `date` for the flight natural key, tombstones only on sync entities, denormalised `user_id` ownership enforced in a repository layer (no RLS yet because of Hyperdrive connection pooling), no partitioning (BRIN + retention crons), and one envelope-encryption format for all secret columns. Make the FlightTracker DO the single writer of `flight_instances` and `flight_events` via an outbox so at-least-once alarms cannot double-write, and publish the flight snapshot to KV so 500 subscribers never touch the DO. Keep positions out of Postgres entirely; persist a <=200-point sample per flight at finish. The technical why in one line: every choice minimises coordination on the hot path (DO-local writes, KV reads, client-generated ids) and keeps the parts that are painful to change (keys, time model, PK type, secret format) fixed from day one, while leaving the parts that will churn (status vocabularies, retention, partitioning, RLS) cheap to change.
risks: Drizzle 1.0 is at rc.4 with no GA; staying on 0.45 defers a known migration (relations v2, migrations folder v3, withRLS) that will land during a later phase; going to rc now risks API churn and doc mismatch.

Stored generated `flight_key` with a unique index: Drizzle docs warn against generated columns inside constraint builders; Postgres allows a unique index on a stored generated column but this must be proven with `drizzle-kit generate` in Phase 0, with the fallback being an app-computed `flight_key` column plus a check constraint that it equals the concatenation.

Hyperdrive + postgres.js `prepare: true` is the documented fast path but a community issue reports intermittent failures with lazily-created Drizzle clients on Workers; the client must be constructed per request and integration tests must run against real Hyperdrive, not only local pg.

KV eventual consistency (up to 60 s) on `flight:snapshot` means two devices can briefly see different states; acceptable for status, but the mobile client must treat the DO/WebSocket path as authoritative for gate changes if you later add live sockets.
At-least-once DO alarms and Queue redelivery require the outbox + dedupe keys to be implemented exactly as designed; skipping `notif_dedupe`/`sent` tables produces duplicate pushes on retries.

Retention crons deleting millions of rows on Neon can bloat without partitioning; batch deletes by uuidv7 range (time-ordered ids make `where id < uuidv7(now() - interval '90 days')` cheap) and run `VACUUM` expectations into the ops runbook.

PNR/confirmation codes and OAuth refresh tokens are encrypted with app-managed keys in Workers Secrets Store; key rotation needs `key_version` handling from day one or rotation becomes a full re-encrypt outage.

Gmail `gmail.readonly` is a Restricted scope requiring Google's CASA security assessment before public launch; the schema stores the granted scopes so a downgrade path (labels-only heuristics) is possible, but the product timeline depends on that review.
Microsoft Graph minimum scope (Mail.Read) and the KV 60 s minimum expirationTtl were not confirmed live in this run (marked unverified from memory).
alternatives_rejected: ULID or bigint identity primary keys: ULID has no native PG type and doubles index size; bigint needs a server round-trip and breaks offline-first client-generated ids.
AeroAPI fa_flight_id as the flight natural key: provider lock-in and unavailable when AeroDataBox is the source; kept as an attribute instead.
IATA airline code in the natural key: IATA 2-letter codes have controlled duplicates; ICAO 3-letter is unique and is what AeroAPI's ident_icao already provides.
pgEnum for statuses and event types: ADD VALUE/rename/drop semantics and drizzle-kit handling make vocabulary churn painful; text + check chosen.
Declarative partitioning of append tables in Phase 0: no Drizzle support, custom DDL forever, and volumes at 100k flights/month do not need it.
Row-Level Security in Phase 0: Hyperdrive connection pooling makes per-request session variables leak-prone; repository-layer enforcement chosen with RLS reserved for later.
Storing ADS-B positions in Postgres: ~600+ rows per flight of pure write amplification with no query need beyond the live map; DO ring buffer plus end-of-flight sample chosen.
A per-view Postgres write for share-link analytics: turns a public page into a DB write amplifier; Analytics Engine chosen.
Using KV for rate limiting or idempotency: 1 write/sec per key and eventual consistency make it wrong for both; Rate Limiting binding or DO chosen.
Reusing Gmail OAuth tokens for Google Calendar: different consent scopes and revocation semantics; separate calendar_connections rows chosen.
Logbook as a SQL view over flight_instances + subscriptions: instances are archived and imported history has no instance; materialised logbook_entries table chosen.

D1 as the primary database: not argued here because the schema needs timestamptz, jsonb, partial/BRIN indexes, arrays and generated columns that SQLite lacks or emulates poorly, and Hyperdrive+Neon is the mandated default.

Storing the whole notification preference matrix as one boolean column per event type: rigid and forces a migration per new event; jsonb map validated by the shared zod schema chosen, with quiet-hours as explicit columns.
open_decisions_for_owner: Drizzle major version for Phase 0: pin 0.45.2 (stable, documented) and accept a later v0->v1 migration, or start on 1.0.0-rc.4 (relations v2, migrations v3) and accept rc churn; recommendation is 0.45 with the API-restriction rule above.
Account deletion grace window (immediate hard delete vs 7-14 day pending state); the schema supports both via account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for.
Whether confirmation codes (PNR) are stored at all; the schema encrypts them, but not storing them removes a credential class from the threat model at the cost of the check-in deep-link convenience.

Retention windows: proposed 90 days for flight_events, provider_calls, notifications; 30 days for airport_delay_snapshots, import_rows, email_extractions.extracted; 7 days for exports. Confirm whether the visible status timeline must outlive 90 days (would move it to R2 archive per flight).
Full-resolution ADS-B track retention in R2 (365 days, Pro replay feature) vs sample-only in Postgres; affects R2 cost and privacy posture.
Free-tier limits that the usage_counters table enforces: active tracked flights, connected email accounts, imports per month, NL questions per month, share links; numbers are product decisions.

Whether to cap the per-flight and per-day provider budgets in provider_budget_config as hard stops (flight goes stale) or fallback-to-secondary-provider; this changes what the FlightTracker does when AeroAPI spend is exceeded.
Whether the public share page and ICS feed live on a separate hostname (cookie isolation, simpler rate limiting) since share_links and ics_feed_tokens are designed for a token-in-URL model.
Watcher role subscriptions ('meet me', family tracking) are excluded from logbook and stats by design; confirm that is the product intent.

security-privacy.summary: Phase 0 should ship five security primitives that every later phase builds on: (1) an application-layer envelope-encryption module (AES-256-GCM per-user DEK wrapped by a versioned KEK held as a Workers Secret, with a KeyProvider interface so the KEK can move to Secrets Store once it leaves Beta); (2) a generic `api_tokens` table (SHA-256 hash + display prefix + scopes + expiry + revocation) plus an `audit_log` table, which is exactly what share links (Phase 5) and the per-user MCP endpoint (Phase 6) need; (3) a Hono middleware chain with the GA `ratelimit` binding for per-IP (unauthenticated routes) and per-user/per-token (authenticated routes) limits, with a one-rule WAF backstop and DO-based quotas only for expensive per-user operations; (4) a first-party analytics path (mobile -> our API -> Workers Analytics Engine, no third-party analytics SDK) plus Sentry configured with PII off on both mobile and Workers; (5) Cloudflare Access on a separate admin Worker with service tokens and `ctx.access` identity. The single biggest schedule risk is not code: `gmail.readonly` and `gmail.metadata` are both Google restricted scopes, restricted-scope verification is quoted at ~6 weeks plus a CASA assessment (AL1 $540–1,800 / 1–3 weeks; AL2 ~$4,500 / 2–4 weeks; annual re-validation), and unverified apps are capped at 100 users, so the Google Cloud project, consent screen, privacy policy, demo video and lab engagement must start in Phase 0 for Phase 3 to land. Microsoft has an analogous gate: multi-tenant apps registered after Nov 2020 that are not publisher-verified are blocked from user consent under risk-based step-up consent, and publisher verification needs a verified Partner Center account. Cloudflare still has no native GitHub OIDC federation, so CI uses a scoped, per-environment API token in GitHub Environments. App Attest / Play Integrity should be deferred (reserve columns and a header slot only); the real cost-abuse control is the per-flight and per-day provider budget guard in the FlightTracker DO plus free-tier limits. LLM extraction of email must run on a zero-data-retention path; note that Anthropic's Covered Models (Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1) require 30-day retention even under ZDR, so use a non-covered model or OpenAI ZDR (sales-approved) for the extraction step.

findings.topic: 1. Where the KEK lives: Workers Secrets vs Secrets Store (status Sep 2026)
findings.detail: Cloudflare Secrets Store launched in Beta on 2025-04-09 and is still described as Beta as of Sep 2026 (no GA changelog entry found; latest entries: 2025-05-27 limit raised to 100 secrets/account; 2025-08-25 AI Gateway BYOK integration). Binding shape: `secrets_store_secrets: [{binding, store_id, secret_name}]`, accessed asynchronously via `await env.BINDING.get()`; requires Secrets Store Admin/Deployer roles; secrets are NOT available in `wrangler dev` local mode. Per-Worker secrets (GA, synchronous `env.X` string): 64/Worker on Free, 128/Worker on Paid, 5 KB each. Recommendation: Phase 0 uses a Worker Secret `TOKEN_KEK_V1` (32 random bytes base64) behind a `KeyProvider` interface (`getKek(version): Promise<CryptoKey>`), so moving to Secrets Store later is a one-file change and gets you scoped roles + audit logging when it reaches GA.

findings.topic: 1. Envelope encryption scheme and column layout (recommendation)
findings.detail: WebCrypto in Workers supports AES-GCM, AES-KW, HKDF, HMAC, SHA-256 and `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual` (verified). Scheme: per-user 256-bit DEK generated with `crypto.getRandomValues`, wrapped with the KEK using AES-KW (`wrapKey`/`unwrapKey`, KEK imported non-extractable); tokens encrypted with the user's DEK using AES-256-GCM, 96-bit random IV per encryption, 128-bit tag (WebCrypto appends tag to ciphertext), and AAD = `oauth_connections:<row_id>:refresh_token` to bind ciphertext to its row and prevent ciphertext-swap attacks. Why per-user DEK rather than single KEK: (a) KEK rotation re-wraps one small `user_keys` row per user instead of re-encrypting every token, (b) GDPR/account deletion becomes crypto-shredding (delete the DEK row and all that user's ciphertext is unrecoverable, including in Neon PITR/backups), (c) blast radius of one DEK leak is one user. Tables: `user_keys(user_id PK, wrapped_dek bytea, wrap_alg text default 'A256KW', kek_version smallint, created_at, rotated_at)`; `oauth_connections(id uuid PK, user_id FK, provider enum('google','microsoft'), provider_account_id text, email_hint text, scopes text[], refresh_token_ct bytea, refresh_token_iv bytea /*12 bytes*/, access_token_ct bytea null, access_token_iv bytea null, access_token_expires_at timestamptz null, enc_alg text default 'A256GCM', dek_version smallint default 1, status enum('active','revoked','error'), last_sync_at, created_at, revoked_at, UNIQUE(user_id, provider, provider_account_id))`. Rotation runbook: add `TOKEN_KEK_V2` secret -> deploy code that reads both -> Cron Trigger job re-wraps `user_keys` in batches, bumping `kek_version` -> when count(kek_version=1)=0 delete V1 secret. Never log plaintext; never return tokens to the client; access tokens are optional to persist (Gmail/Graph access tokens live ~1h) but if cached, use the same scheme. Neon disk encryption is defence-in-depth only; app-layer encryption is what protects against SQL injection, console access, and backup exfiltration.

findings.topic: 2. Share-link and MCP token primitives (Phase 0 tables/middleware)
findings.detail: `api_tokens(id uuid PK, user_id FK, kind enum('mcp','share','service'), token_hash bytea UNIQUE /*sha256 of full secret*/, token_prefix text /*first 12 chars for display+support lookup*/, name text, scopes text[], resource_id uuid null /*flight_id for share links*/, expires_at timestamptz, revoked_at timestamptz null, last_used_at timestamptz null, use_count int default 0, created_at)`. Token format: `twy_<kind>_<base64url(32 random bytes)>` = 256 bits entropy (share links can use 20 bytes/160 bits to keep URLs short; both make enumeration infeasible even at 1e9 req/day). Lookup is by hash (unique index), so the prefix is for humans, not the index. Constant-time compare is unnecessary once you compare hashes via the DB, but use `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual` anywhere a raw secret is compared in code. `audit_log(id bigint PK, ts, actor_type enum('user','token','service','admin','system'), actor_id text, token_id uuid null, action text, target_type text, target_id text, request_id text, metadata jsonb, ip_hash text null /*sha256(ip+daily salt)*/)`. Hono middleware in Phase 0: `requestId` -> `auth()` that resolves a principal `{type:'session'|'token'|'access_service'|'anonymous', userId, tokenId, scopes}` from session JWT, `twy_` bearer token, or Cloudflare Access identity -> `requireScope('flights:read')` -> `rateLimit(...)`. Add `packages/shared/publicProjection.ts` with `toSharedFlightView(flight)` and a unit test that asserts the DTO key set is exactly an allow-list (no passenger name, PNR, seat, email, notes). MCP spec 2026-07-28 says servers MUST validate inputs, implement access control, rate limit tool invocations and sanitize outputs; clients SHOULD prompt for confirmation on sensitive ops and treat tool annotations as untrusted unless from trusted servers.

findings.topic: 2. Share-link threat model (Phase 5, designed now)
findings.detail: Threats: enumeration (mitigated by >=160-bit token + per-IP 404 rate limit); referrer leakage (serve `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`); over-sharing (projection DTO only; 'meet me' mode is a separate opt-in scope `share:meet` that adds terminal/arrival-door details); stale caching leaking post-revocation (cache rendered HTML in Cache API/KV keyed by sha256(token), TTL <=60s while airborne, 300s otherwise, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` to browsers, explicit purge on revoke; never put the token in cache keys in plaintext logs); OG image in R2 named by a second random id, not the share token; expiry default = scheduled arrival + 24h, max 7 days, owner revocation sets `revoked_at` and purges cache; abuse/scraping: ratelimit binding key=IP 60/60s on `/s/*` plus WAF rule; the page is Workers-served HTML with zero client-side provider calls (architecture mandate) so the share page can never leak provider credentials. Log views to `audit_log` with ip_hash only (privacy). The Hono handler must return identical 404 for unknown, expired and revoked tokens (no oracle).

findings.topic: 2. MCP endpoint threat model (Phase 6, designed now)
findings.detail: MCP 2026-07-28 (final 2026-07-28, RC 2026-05-21): authorization is OPTIONAL for implementations, but when an HTTP server supports it the server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server that MUST publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), MUST validate token audience (RFC 8707), MUST NOT accept or pass through any other tokens, and clients MUST send `resource`; Client ID Metadata Documents are preferred and Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated; the protocol is now stateless (no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no initialize handshake). Tools may return `resultType: 'input_required'` with an `elicitation/create` request, which is the spec-native confirmation primitive. Recommendation: Phase 6 supports two auth paths on the same `api_tokens` primitive: (a) user-minted PAT `twy_mcp_...` (scopes default `flights:read`; `flights:write` must be explicitly ticked; 90-day default expiry; one-tap revoke; shown once) for clients that accept a static bearer header; (b) OAuth 2.1 via `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` (stores access/refresh tokens, codes and client secrets only by hash in KV, PKCE S256 mandatory for public clients, configurable TTLs). Tool design: every tool is scoped to the authenticated user only (no user_id params), read tools set `annotations.readOnlyHint=true`; `add_flight` is two-step: `propose_flight(...)` returns a `proposal_id` and a human-readable summary, `confirm_flight(proposal_id)` requires `flights:write` and a proposal <10 min old (idempotent, `destructiveHint=false`), optionally via `input_required` elicitation for clients that support it. Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs embed third-party text (provider remarks, gate strings, airline names, itinerary notes from email); sanitize (strip control chars, cap length, no markdown links to user-controlled URLs) and never include instructions in output. Rate limit tool calls per token (60/60s) and per user; `audit_log` every call with tool name and args hash; 403 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="flights:write"` per spec for step-up.

findings.topic: 3. Rate limiting options on Workers
findings.detail: Workers `ratelimit` binding is GA since 2025-09-19 (Wrangler >=4.36.0). Config: `ratelimits: [{name, namespace_id: '1001', simple: {limit, period}}]`; `period` must be 10 or 60 seconds; `await env.LIMITER.limit({key})` returns `{success}`; counters are per Cloudflare location, eventually consistent, 'intentionally not an accurate accounting system'; docs advise against IP keys because of mobile NAT and proxies. No price is listed on the binding or GA pages (treat as included; unverified). WAF rate-limiting rules: Free 1 rule / 10s window / 10s timeout / IP only; Pro 2 rules / 1 min; Business 5 rules / 10 min with custom expressions; Enterprise 100 rules with header/cookie/JSON-field/JA4 characteristics. DO-based token bucket: exact and global but costs a DO request per check; Cloudflare's own example exists. Recommendation (Hono order): `requestId` -> `cors` -> `ipLimiter` (binding, namespace 1001, key=`cf-connecting-ip`, 120/10s, applied ONLY to unauthenticated routes: `/auth/*`, `/s/*`, `/v1/public/*`, webhook receivers) -> `auth()` -> `principalLimiter` (binding, namespace 1002, key=user_id 600/60s; namespace 1003 key=token_id 60/60s for `twy_mcp_`) -> handler. Expensive per-user operations (email sync trigger, GDPR export, in-app NL questions) get exact daily quotas enforced inside the existing `UserInbox` DO (no extra DO class), since those are business quotas, not abuse controls. Add one WAF rule on the API zone (Free plan: e.g. 300 req/10s per IP -> block) as a pre-Worker backstop that also protects your Workers request bill. Return 429 with `Retry-After` and draft `RateLimit-*` headers. Webhooks from providers (AeroAPI push, RevenueCat) are exempt from per-IP limits but require HMAC/secret verification.

findings.topic: 4. App Store privacy labels / privacy manifest implications
findings.detail: Apple's definition of 'collect' = transmitted off-device and accessible longer than needed to service the request; auth tokens and IPs discarded immediately need no disclosure. Taxiway's expected label: Contact Info (email address; linked; App Functionality), Identifiers (User ID; linked), User Content ('Emails or Text Messages' once email sync ships; linked; App Functionality), Purchases (purchase history via RevenueCat; linked), Usage Data (product interaction; NOT linked if analytics carry no user id), Diagnostics (crash + performance via Sentry; not linked if sendDefaultPii off), Location: avoid 'collecting' by computing 'when to leave' from a user-entered origin or on-device geocoding rather than sending device coordinates to the API (if coordinates are sent and coarsened immediately, disclose as Coarse Location). Tracking = No; set `NSPrivacyTracking=false`, no `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains`. Privacy manifests (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) with `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` and `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` required-reason declarations are enforced since spring 2024 and third-party SDKs must ship manifests/signatures; all third-party SDK data must be disclosed. Account deletion must be initiable in-app (since 2022-06-30), must delete the whole record (deactivation insufficient), and Sign in with Apple apps must call the Apple token-revocation REST API on deletion.

findings.topic: 4. Google Play Data Safety implications
findings.detail: Data Safety categories relevant to Taxiway: Personal info (email, user IDs), Messages (Emails, once sync ships), App activity, App info & performance (crash logs), Financial (purchase history), Location if transmitted. 'Collection' includes data sent via SDKs/webviews; 'sharing' excludes transfers to service providers (so Cloudflare/Neon/Sentry as processors are not 'sharing'). Must declare encryption in transit and a deletion-request mechanism. Play account-deletion policy (enforced after 2024-05-31): apps with account creation must provide an in-app deletion path AND a web link to request deletion, declared in the Data Safety form; retention exceptions only for security/fraud/regulatory reasons and must be disclosed in the privacy policy. Implication: the GDPR/CCPA automated deletion endpoint in Phase 0 should also back a public web deletion-request page.

findings.topic: 4. Product analytics choice: Workers Analytics Engine vs PostHog vs Aptabase
findings.detail: Workers Analytics Engine: Free 100,000 data points/day and 10,000 read queries/day; Paid 10M points/month and 1M queries/month included, then $0.25 per additional 1M points and $1.00 per 1M queries; currently not billed at all; limits: 250 data points per invocation, 1 index (<=96 B), 20 blobs (<=16 KB total), 20 doubles, 3-month retention, SQL API (needs your own Grafana/dashboards; no funnels/retention UI). PostHog: officially unsupported self-hosting (no CVEs/tagged releases, 'assume all risk', consider only under ~300k events/mo), Cloud is recommended and gives 1M events/month free then ~$0.00005/event. Aptabase: privacy-first mobile analytics, free 20k events/mo, $10/200k, $20/1M, $75/5M, $140/10M; self-hostable; states it does not sell end-user data. Recommendation: Phase 0 = no third-party analytics SDK in the app; mobile batches events to `POST /v1/events` (validated allow-list of event names + typed props, max 50/batch), the Worker writes to Analytics Engine with index=event_name and blobs=[platform, app_version, cf.country, cohort_bucket] and NO user id (use a daily-salted hash only if DAU is needed, so Usage Data stays 'not linked'). Provider-query counts also go to Analytics Engine as a separate dataset (index=provider). Revisit Aptabase (privacy-compatible) or PostHog Cloud in Phase 4+ if product needs funnels; the API-side event schema makes that a sink swap, not an app change.

findings.topic: 4. Sentry scrubbing configuration
findings.detail: Mobile (`@sentry/react-native`): set `sendDefaultPii: false` (controls automatic user context), implement `beforeSend` to delete `event.user.email`/ip and any `twy_`/`cfast_`/`sk-` patterns in message/extra, `beforeBreadcrumb` to drop `http` breadcrumbs carrying query strings/fragments (SDKs attach them by default) and any `console` breadcrumbs, disable Session Replay or keep default full masking, and never `setUser({email})`; only `setUser({id})`. Workers (`@sentry/cloudflare`, Vite plugin with `autoInstrumentation: true` wraps the Worker, Durable Objects and Agents classes): by default the SDK sends IP, user id, HTTP bodies and query params; configure `dataCollection: { userInfo: false, cookies: false, httpBodies: [] }`; the SDK also auto-filters keys matching a built-in denylist (`auth`, `password`) to `[Filtered]`. Add server-side Sentry data-scrubbing rules with a regex for `twy_[a-z]+_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{27,}` and email addresses as a backstop, and a unit test that the API's error middleware never puts request bodies or headers into the Sentry event.

findings.topic: 5. Gmail scopes and restricted-scope verification (CASA) timeline and cost
findings.detail: Both `gmail.readonly` ('view your email messages and settings') and `gmail.metadata` ('labels and headers, but not the email body') are classified RESTRICTED; `gmail.metadata` cannot return bodies, so it is insufficient for itinerary extraction (airline confirmation bodies carry the PNR/segments; subjects alone are unreliable). Google's FAQ estimates: brand verification 2–3 business days, sensitive scopes 10 business days, restricted scopes ~6 weeks plus security assessment; unverified apps using sensitive/restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users, after which Google sign-in is disabled for new users; restricted verification requires privacy policy, homepage, demo video and the assessment. CASA (App Defense Alliance, ASVS-based) moved from Tiers to Assurance Levels: AL1 'developer tested, lab reviewed' ~$540–1,800 (TAC Security has a Google-negotiated rate), 1–3 weeks; AL2 'lab tested' ~$4,500, 2–4 weeks; Google assigns the level based on data sensitivity and user volume; revalidation every 12 months; named labs: TAC Security, Leviathan, DEKRA, Bishop Fox. Realistic critical path: ~2–3 months from a stable staging deployment to a Letter of Validation; ADHD note: the assessed artifact is the running app + backend, so the assessment cannot start before Phase 3 has a testable build, but the consent screen, brand verification, privacy policy, domain verification and lab contract can all be done in Phase 0–1. Workspace API User Data & Developer Policy (Limited Use): user data may only power prominent user-facing features; no ads/resale; humans may not read data without documented affirmative consent; and data may not be used to 'create, train, or improve' an AI/ML model beyond that specific user's personalized model. LLM extraction as a user-facing feature is permitted; provider training on the content is not, and 'no human review' must hold on the LLM vendor side too.

findings.topic: 5. Microsoft Graph Mail.Read consent and publisher verification
findings.detail: Delegated `Mail.Read` does not require admin consent; `Mail.ReadBasic` excludes body, attachments and extensions (insufficient, same reasoning as gmail.metadata). Since November 2020, when risk-based step-up consent is enabled (default in many tenants), users cannot consent to newly registered multi-tenant apps that are NOT publisher verified and request permissions beyond sign-in/profile; the consent screen shows an 'unverified publisher' warning. Publisher verification is free but requires a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (formerly MPN) partner global account, an app registered in a work/school tenant with a publisher domain (not *.onmicrosoft.com), the CPP account email domain matching that domain, and an MFA-authenticated Application Administrator. Personal Outlook.com accounts do not go through tenant consent policies, but Microsoft 365 work accounts (a large share of travel itineraries) do. Start Partner Center enrollment in Phase 0; it is bureaucratic, not technical.

findings.topic: 5. Email-sync storage/retention design and zero-data-retention LLM providers
findings.detail: Design constraints that satisfy Google Limited Use, Apple/Play labels and GDPR minimisation: (1) raw MIME/body is fetched inside the Queue consumer, passed to the extractor in memory, and never written to Postgres, R2, KV, DO storage or logs (enforce with a lint rule/test that `email_messages` has no body column and that the consumer never calls `writeDataPoint` or logger with the body); (2) persist only `email_messages(id, connection_id, provider_message_id, message_id_hash /*sha256 of RFC 5322 Message-ID*/, received_at, subject_hash null, parse_status enum('pending','parsed','ignored','failed'), itinerary_id null, processed_at)` plus `itineraries(...)` holding the strict-JSON extracted segments and a `source` enum; (3) retention: `email_messages` rows kept 90 days after `processed_at` for dedupe then purged by Cron; on disconnect: call Google's token revoke endpoint (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`; unverified URL from memory), delete `oauth_connections` row, and cascade-delete `email_messages`; Microsoft has no refresh-token revoke API for the app side (unverified, from memory), so delete locally and instruct the user; (4) LLM extraction via an `LlmExtractor` interface with a zod schema and `strict` JSON output. Provider retention facts: OpenAI API default retains abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days; ZDR requires OpenAI approval via sales and then applies to `/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, embeddings, etc., with `store` forced false. Anthropic: ZDR is per-organization, requested via sales; BUT Covered Models (Claude Fable 5, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5, Mythos 5.1) require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR unless expressly authorised; a ZDR org can enable a 30-day-retention workspace for them. Consequence: run itinerary extraction on a non-covered, small model under ZDR (or OpenAI ZDR), and keep the model choice a config value. Workers AI keeps data on Cloudflare but its retention/training terms were not verified in this run.

findings.topic: 6. Sign in with Apple: token verification, private relay, server-to-server events
findings.detail: Verify the identity token against JWKS `https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys`; check `iss=https://appleid.apple.com`, `aud`=bundle id/services id, `exp`, and `nonce`; `sub` is the stable user id (persist it, not the email); claims `email`, `email_verified`, `is_private_email` (true => `@privaterelay.appleid.com` address), `real_user_status` (likely_real/unknown/unsupported; useful as a fraud signal). Private relay addresses only accept mail from sender domains/addresses registered in the Apple Developer 'Sign in with Apple for Email Communication' config with SPF/DKIM passing (page did not load; from memory: verified). Register a server-to-server notification endpoint and handle JWT-signed events `email-disabled`, `email-enabled`, `consent-revoked`, `account-delete` (the JWT carries an `events` claim with `type` and `sub`): on `consent-revoked`/`account-delete` treat as sign-out and start the deletion flow; on `email-disabled` stop sending to the relay. Account deletion must call Apple's revoke-tokens REST endpoint. Schema: `auth_identities(user_id, provider enum('apple','google','magic_link','anonymous'), provider_subject text, email text null, email_is_relay bool, created_at, UNIQUE(provider, provider_subject))`; email is nullable because Apple only returns it on first authorization.

findings.topic: 6. Google Sign-In verification
findings.detail: Verify the ID token signature locally against `https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs` (JWK; honour Cache-Control for refresh), check `aud` is one of your client IDs (iOS, Android, web each have their own), `iss` in {`accounts.google.com`, `https://accounts.google.com`}, `exp`, and use `email_verified`; Google recommends a client library or a general JWT library (jose works in Workers) over hand-rolled checks; the `tokeninfo` endpoint is for debugging only. Use `sub` as the stable identifier.

findings.topic: 6. App Attest / Play Integrity: defer, but reserve the slots
findings.detail: App Attest (iOS 14+, Secure Enclave devices only, no simulator): generateKey -> attestKey (Apple-signed cert chain validated server-side against Apple's App Attest root) -> per-request generateAssertion; Apple guidance is risk-based use, not every request, and attestation is rate limited. Play Integrity: standard requests (low latency, cached, warm-up) vs classic (nonce, seconds, sparse use); default quota 10,000 requests/day (raise via Play Console); verdicts `appRecognitionVerdict=PLAY_RECOGNIZED`, `appLicensingVerdict=LICENSED`, `deviceIntegrity` labels; server must decrypt+verify the token; Google explicitly recommends telemetry-first then tiered enforcement (allow / limit / challenge / deny) and no verdict caching. Recommendation: NOT in Phase 0. Rationale: the economically motivated abuse in this product is provider-query cost and free-tier evasion; both are already bounded by the shared FlightTracker (one provider call per refresh regardless of subscriber count), the per-flight/per-day budget guard, and free-tier limits keyed to authenticated users. Attestation adds two native modules and server verification code without changing that bound. Make it additive now by: (1) `devices(id, user_id, platform, push_token_ct, attestation enum('none','app_attest','play_integrity') default 'none', attest_key_id text null, attested_at null, last_seen_at)`; (2) an `X-Taxiway-Attestation` header slot read by a no-op `attestation()` middleware that records presence into `audit_log`; (3) revisit when anonymous mode + push become abuse targets (Phase 2/4).

findings.topic: 7. CI to Cloudflare: no native GitHub OIDC; token scoping
findings.detail: As of Sep 2026 Cloudflare's API does not support GitHub OIDC federation (wrangler-action issue #402 and workers-sdk discussion #11434 remain feature requests; the community `cf-oidc-token-broker` Worker exchanges a GitHub OIDC JWT for a 10-minute Cloudflare API token minted with an account-admin-equivalent master token, which just moves the secret). Cloudflare's documented path: a custom API token from the 'Edit Cloudflare Workers' template scoped to the single account, stored as a CI secret and passed to `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4` with `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`. Recommendation: two tokens (staging, production) stored as GitHub Environment secrets; production environment requires a reviewer and is restricted to the `main` branch; add the extra permissions the stack needs (Workers Scripts, Workers KV, Queues, Durable Objects, Hyperdrive, R2, Analytics Engine, Cron; the exact permission-group names were not enumerated in the doc, verify in the token UI); rotate quarterly (put the date in the runbook); never give CI `API Tokens:Edit`, `Secrets Store`, or zone-wide DNS. Alternative worth a spike: Cloudflare Workers Builds (Cloudflare-hosted CI from the GitHub app) removes the token entirely; monorepo support and Miniflare test stage maturity unverified in this run.

findings.topic: 7. EAS secrets and 'no provider keys in the app' enforcement
findings.detail: EAS environment variables have three visibilities: plain text (visible everywhere), sensitive (obfuscated in logs, readable via CLI), secret (readable only inside EAS build/workflow jobs, never on the website or CLI). Expo's own guidance: anything in client-side code is public. `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variables are inlined into the JS bundle (well-known Expo behaviour; the specific doc page was not fetched, unverified here). Enforcement recommendation for Phase 0 CI: (1) `packages/shared` exports `SECRET_PATTERNS` (AeroAPI key shape, AeroDataBox/RapidAPI key shape, `cfast_`, `twy_`, `sk-`, Neon connection strings `postgres://`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`); (2) a CI job runs `npx expo export --platform all` on `apps/mobile` and greps the output bundle for those patterns plus a literal list of provider hostnames (`aeroapi.flightaware.com`, `aerodatabox.p.rapidapi.com`); any hit fails the build (this also enforces the 'backend is the only component that talks to providers' mandate mechanically); (3) `gitleaks` on every PR; (4) provider credentials exist only as Workers secrets on `apps/api` (staging/prod), and `.dev.vars` is gitignored with a committed `.dev.vars.example`.

findings.topic: 7. Dependency policy: pnpm supply-chain settings, Renovate, audit
findings.detail: pnpm: `minimumReleaseAge` (minutes; added v10.16.0; default 0 before v11 and 1440 in v11) delays installing freshly published versions, transitive included; `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` allow-lists packages/patterns; `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` (v10.21.0, default off) fails install if a package loses provenance/trust level; `blockExoticSubdeps` (v10.26.0, default true) forbids git/tarball transitive deps; also `strictDepBuilds`, `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, and an explicit `onlyBuiltDependencies` allow-list so postinstall scripts cannot run unreviewed; since v11.5.3 env vars are not expanded in registry URLs. Renovate: `minimumReleaseAge` (e.g. '7 days') suppresses PRs for very new releases, `config:best-practices` preset, `lockFileMaintenance` on a schedule, `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` + `vulnerabilityAlerts` for malicious-package detection and fix PRs. Recommendation: pnpm >=11 with `minimumReleaseAge: 4320` (3 days), `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`, `onlyBuiltDependencies` allow-list; Renovate weekly grouped updates with `minimumReleaseAge: '7 days'` and immediate PRs for vulnerability alerts; `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` as a non-blocking CI report in Phase 0 (blocking from Phase 1 once the baseline is clean); GitHub Dependabot alerts enabled for the second opinion.

findings.topic: 8. Admin surface: Cloudflare Access on Workers, service tokens, seats
findings.detail: Cloudflare Access can now be enabled directly on a Worker (dashboard 'Protect this Worker behind Access', or API `POST /accounts/{id}/access/apps` with destination type `worker`/`preview_worker`; changelog 2026-08-14 and 2025-10-03); scope can be production URL, preview URLs, or all Workers. Authenticated requests expose `ctx.access.getIdentity()` (email, name, groups, device posture) with no manual JWT parsing; requests carrying valid service-token headers also produce a `ctx.access` object; `wrangler dev` supports an `access.dev` block (`aud`, simulated `identity`) for local tests. Service tokens: headers `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret`; new secrets since 2026-08-26 use `cfast_[40 alnum][8 checksum]` (scanner-friendly; legacy 64-hex still works); lifetime chosen at creation (e.g. 8760h), renewal extends, rotation issues a new secret with a 1h–30d grace window, expiry alert one week before. If you validate the JWT yourself (recommended defence-in-depth for any origin not exclusively reachable through Access): keys at `https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs`, match `kid`, verify `iss` and the application `aud` tag with `jose` `createRemoteJWKSet`/`jwtVerify`. Zero Trust Free plan covers 50 users (third-party sources; Cloudflare's own pricing page did not render), paid $7/user/month. Recommendation: put admin endpoints in a separate Worker `apps/api-admin` (Access apps attach per Worker, so mixing admin and public routes in one Worker is awkward), bound to the same Hyperdrive/DO namespaces via service bindings; Cron Triggers invoke the Worker directly and need no Access; use one service token per automation (BTS import runner, ops scripts) named in `audit_log.actor_id`; admin humans via Google Workspace IdP with a `taxiway-admins` group check on `ctx.access.getIdentity().groups`.

findings.topic: Phase 0 checklist: implemented vs documented-only
findings.detail: IMPLEMENTED in Phase 0: (a) `packages/shared/crypto`: envelope encryption module (`encryptForUser`, `decryptForUser`, `rotateKek`), KeyProvider with Workers-Secret backend, unit tests incl. AAD mismatch and IV uniqueness; (b) Drizzle schema for `users`, `auth_identities`, `user_keys`, `oauth_connections`, `api_tokens`, `audit_log`, `devices` (attestation columns nullable), `email_messages`, `itineraries`, `share_links` (view of api_tokens kind='share' or its own table with FK to api_tokens), `deletion_requests`, `export_jobs`; (c) Hono middleware: requestId, auth (session JWT + `twy_` PAT + Access identity), requireScope, rateLimit (ratelimit binding namespaces 1001–1004), attestation no-op, error handler with Sentry scrubbing; (d) Sign in with Apple + Google ID-token verification with jose, magic link, anonymous device accounts with upgrade/merge; (e) Apple server-to-server notification endpoint and Apple token-revocation call in the deletion flow; (f) GDPR export (R2, signed short-lived URL) and deletion (crypto-shred + cascade) endpoints plus a public web deletion-request page; (g) Sentry on mobile and Workers with PII off; (h) `/v1/events` -> Analytics Engine, and provider-cost logging to Analytics Engine (`provider`, `endpoint`, `flight_key`, `cost_units`); (i) CI: scoped CF tokens per environment, gitleaks, bundle-grep test, pnpm supply-chain settings, Renovate, `pnpm audit` report; (j) `apps/api-admin` Worker behind Access with one service token and `audit_log` writes; (k) WAF backstop rule + Referrer/robots headers on public routes. DOCUMENTED-ONLY in Phase 0: share-page threat model and caching rules (Phase 5), MCP threat model incl. OAuth provider choice and proposal/confirm tool semantics (Phase 6), email-sync data-flow diagram and retention policy, LLM provider ZDR selection, App Attest/Play Integrity rollout plan, KEK rotation runbook, incident response/secret-revocation runbook, App Store/Play privacy label drafts. OWNER TASKS started in Phase 0: Google Cloud project + OAuth consent screen (Testing) + brand verification + privacy policy/homepage/demo video plan + CASA lab quote; Microsoft Entra multi-tenant app + publisher domain + Partner Center (CPP) enrollment; Apple Developer email-relay sender domain registration; OpenAI/Anthropic ZDR request.

findings.topic: Threat-model document outline (docs/security/threat-model.md)
findings.detail: 1. Scope and assets (user identity, OAuth refresh tokens, itineraries/PNRs, push tokens, provider credentials, provider budget, share/MCP tokens, admin plane). 2. Trust boundaries diagram (mobile app -> API Worker -> DOs/Queues -> Neon/KV/R2; providers; LLM vendor; Apple/Google/Microsoft IdPs; Access). 3. Actors: anonymous internet, authenticated user, malicious user, compromised mobile build, share-link recipient, MCP client/LLM (prompt-injection channel), insider/admin, CI, provider. 4. STRIDE per boundary with controls and residual risk. 5. Data classification and storage matrix (what is encrypted at app layer, what is hashed, what is never stored, retention per table). 6. Auth & session design (token formats, lifetimes, revocation, Apple/Google verification, anonymous upgrade). 7. Secrets & key management (KEK location, rotation, who can read what, Secrets Store migration criteria). 8. Rate limiting & abuse (layers, keys, quotas, budget guard). 9. Share links (enumeration, leakage, caching, expiry, revocation, image assets). 10. MCP endpoint (OAuth/PAT, audience binding, scopes, tool semantics, injection handling, audit). 11. Email sync (scopes, verification status, data flow, no-body invariant, LLM vendor retention, human-access policy). 12. Admin plane (Access, service tokens, audit). 13. Privacy compliance mapping (App Store labels, Play Data Safety, GDPR/CCPA export+delete, Google Limited Use, Apple relay). 14. Supply chain & CI. 15. Logging/observability privacy rules (no PII in logs, ip_hash, token prefixes only). 16. Open risks and decisions, review cadence (re-run at each phase gate).

security-privacy.recommendation: Adopt per-user DEK envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM data, AES-KW wrapping, KEK as a Workers Secret behind a KeyProvider interface) rather than a single KEK: the marginal code is ~150 lines, and it buys cheap KEK rotation and crypto-shredding for automated GDPR deletion, which you have committed to. Keep the KEK in Workers Secrets for Phase 0 because Secrets Store is still Beta and unavailable in local dev; migrate when it reaches GA. Build one generic hashed `api_tokens` table plus `audit_log` now; share links and MCP tokens are then rows with different `kind`/`scopes`, not new infrastructure. For rate limiting, use the GA `ratelimit` binding as the primary mechanism (per-IP only on unauthenticated routes, per-user/per-token everywhere else), a single WAF rule as a pre-Worker backstop, and exact per-user quotas inside the existing UserInbox DO; do not build a DO token bucket for general traffic. For analytics, write from the backend to Workers Analytics Engine with no user identifier, which keeps Usage Data 'not linked' on both store labels and means zero third-party analytics SDKs in the binary; swap the sink later if product needs funnels. Defer App Attest/Play Integrity but reserve the schema columns and header slot. Treat email sync as a program-management risk more than an engineering one: kick off Google restricted-scope verification prerequisites, the CASA lab engagement, and Microsoft publisher verification in Phase 0, and pick a non-covered model under a ZDR agreement for extraction. Put admin endpoints in a separate Worker behind Cloudflare Access with service tokens, and still verify the Access JWT in code.
risks: Google restricted-scope verification (~6 weeks) plus CASA (1–4 weeks lab time, 2–3 months realistic) gates Phase 3; the 100-new-user cap applies until verified, so a public beta with email sync before the LOV is not possible.

Anthropic Covered Models (Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1) require 30-day retention even under ZDR; choosing one for extraction would conflict with the 'no raw bodies retained' promise unless the retention is disclosed. OpenAI ZDR also needs sales approval; neither is self-serve.

Secrets Store is still Beta and cannot be read in local dev; if chosen for the KEK now, Miniflare integration tests need a shim. Workers Secrets cap at 5 KB / 128 per Worker, which is fine for a KEK but not for a large key set.
The ratelimit binding is per-colo and approximate; it will not enforce global free-tier quotas. Anyone treating it as accounting will under-enforce limits for users hitting multiple PoPs.
No native Cloudflare OIDC for GitHub Actions: a long-lived API token lives in GitHub; mitigated by environment scoping and rotation, but it remains the highest-value CI secret.
Microsoft 365 tenants with risk-based step-up consent will block Taxiway's Outlook sync until publisher verification completes; Partner Center verification can stall on business-identity checks.

Apple private relay: transactional email (magic links, alerts) to relay addresses will be dropped unless the sending domain/addresses are registered and SPF/DKIM pass; magic-link login for relay users depends on this.
Analytics Engine retains data for only 3 months and has a 96-byte single index; product analytics needing retention curves or funnels will need an additional sink.
Envelope encryption relies on the KEK never appearing in logs or Sentry; a single `console.log(env)` leaks it. Enforce with a lint rule and Sentry scrubbing.
Free-plan WAF rate limiting is IP-only with a 10s window; mobile carrier NAT can cause false positives if the threshold is set too low.
alternatives_rejected: Single KEK encrypting every token directly (no per-user DEK): simpler, but KEK rotation means re-encrypting every ciphertext row and GDPR deletion cannot crypto-shred; rejected because deletion automation is a hard requirement.
Storing the KEK in Cloudflare Secrets Store in Phase 0: still Beta, async `get()`, unavailable in local dev; deferred behind the KeyProvider interface.
Postgres-side encryption (pgcrypto with the key in SQL): key would transit to Neon on every call and appear in query logs; rejected.
DO-based token bucket as the primary API rate limiter: adds a DO round-trip to every request and a cost per check; kept only for exact per-user quotas on expensive operations.

Third-party analytics SDKs in the mobile binary (PostHog RN, Aptabase, Firebase): adds privacy-manifest and label obligations and a network dependency; rejected for Phase 0 in favour of first-party events to Analytics Engine.
Self-hosted PostHog: officially unsupported by PostHog, no tagged releases/CVEs, ops burden; rejected.
App Attest / Play Integrity in Phase 0: two native modules plus server verification with no change to the provider-cost bound already enforced in the FlightTracker DO; deferred.
gmail.metadata / Mail.ReadBasic to avoid restricted-scope review: both exclude message bodies, and gmail.metadata is itself restricted, so it neither avoids review nor supports extraction; rejected.
Community OIDC token broker for Cloudflare deploys: relocates rather than removes a long-lived admin-equivalent token; rejected until Cloudflare ships native federation.
Mixing admin routes into the public API Worker behind path-based Access: Access-for-Workers attaches to the whole Worker, so a separate admin Worker is cleaner.
open_decisions_for_owner: LLM vendor for email extraction: OpenAI (ZDR via sales) vs Anthropic non-covered model (ZDR via sales) vs Workers AI (retention terms unverified). Decide by end of Phase 1 so the ZDR request is in flight before Phase 3.
Accept a 30-day-retention workspace for a Covered Model if extraction quality demands it, with disclosure in the privacy policy, or hard-require ZDR?
Budget approval for CASA (AL1 ~$540–1,800 or AL2 ~$4,500, annually) and which lab (TAC Security has a Google-negotiated rate).
Who owns Google brand verification, privacy policy, homepage, demo video, and Microsoft Partner Center enrollment (legal entity, domain, MFA admin)? These are non-engineering blockers.
Default MCP token scope: read-only only (safest) vs allowing write with two-step confirmation from day one.
Share link default expiry (arrival+24h proposed) and whether 'meet me' details are ever shareable without a login.
Use Cloudflare Workers Builds instead of GitHub Actions for deploys to eliminate the CI API token? Needs a spike on monorepo + Miniflare test support.
Analytics: is a daily-salted hashed user id acceptable (keeps labels 'not linked') or is per-user cohort analysis required (forces 'linked' disclosure and a different sink)?
Zero Trust plan: Free covers 50 seats; confirm the admin headcount and whether service tokens must be counted (unverified).
Whether 'when to leave' may send device coordinates to the API (forces Location disclosure on both stores) or must compute on-device from a user-chosen origin.

monorepo-ci.summary: Research as of 2026-09-19 for Taxiway Phase 0 tooling. The ecosystem has moved under us in three ways that a plan written from 2025 memory would get wrong: (1) Corepack is no longer shipped with Node 25+, so the pnpm pin must come from package.json `packageManager` + pnpm/action-setup, not corepack, and Node 24 LTS is the safe baseline; (2) @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers was renamed to @cloudflare/vitest-plugin (v1.1.13) and both only peer on Vitest ^4.1, while Vitest 5.0 shipped 2026-09-03, so Vitest must be pinned to 4.1.x in apps/api and packages/shared; (3) TypeScript 7.0 (Go compiler) is `latest` on npm but Expo SDK 57 expects ~6.0.3 and TS 7 breaks app.config.ts, so the repo pins TypeScript 6.0.x everywhere. Expo SDK 57 (expo 57.0.24, RN 0.86, React 19.2, Xcode 26.4+, iOS 16.4 min) officially supports pnpm isolated installs (since SDK 54) and configures Metro for monorepos automatically (since SDK 52), so pnpm 12 workspaces + Turborepo 2.11 is the boring, well-documented choice; Nx and Bun workspaces are not justified for a 3-package repo. Recommended layout: apps/mobile, apps/api, packages/shared, packages/db (kept separate from shared so the mobile bundle never depends on drizzle/pg), with TypeScript project references and one strict base. Lint: ESLint 9 flat config + Prettier (eslint-config-expo is what `npx expo lint` scaffolds); Biome 2.5 is viable but its React Native rules only landed in 2.4.13 as nursery. Tests: Vitest 4.1 + @cloudflare/vitest-plugin for shared/api (runDurableObjectAlarm, runInDurableObject exist), Jest 29 via jest-expo 57 + RNTL for mobile. CI: GitHub Actions as system of record with cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4 for deploys (staging on main, production on tag), Neon branch per PR for migration checks, EAS Build via expo/expo-github-action@v8 (free tier 15 iOS + 15 Android builds/month), EAS Update for OTA, e2e deferred (Maestro when needed). Two owner-facing gotchas: GitHub Environments (needed for env-scoped secrets + required reviewers) require GitHub Team/Pro on private repos, and bundle IDs / Android application IDs are immutable after first upload/publish so the domain and org decision must precede the first TestFlight build.

findings.topic: Runtime/toolchain versions as of 2026-09-19 (npm `latest`)
findings.detail: node: v26 is Current (released 2026-05-05), v24 'Krypton' is Active LTS, v22 is LTS/maintenance; use Node 24 for CI and .node-version. pnpm 12.4.2 (pnpm 12.0 released 2026-08-26, Rust rewrite, engines node>=18; breaking: unrecognized pnpm-workspace.yaml settings now error). turbo 2.11.2. typescript 7.0.2 (Go compiler; ships WITHOUT a stable programmatic API until 7.1, so typescript-eslint and framework tooling cannot use it). vitest 5.0.1 (5.0.0 released 2026-09-03; requires Node 22, Vite 6.4; clearMocks defaults true; output moves to .vitest/). wrangler 4.135.0 (miniflare 5.20260918.0-alpha, workerd 1.20260918.1). @biomejs/biome 2.5.14. hono 4.13.8. @hono/zod-openapi 1.6.3 (peer hono>=4.10, zod ^4). hono-openapi 1.3.3 (peer hono ^4.11.2). drizzle-orm 0.45.2, drizzle-kit 0.31.10. zod 4.6.5. expo 57.0.24 (devDep react-native 0.86.3). jest-expo 57.0.5 (babel-jest ^29.2.1 => Jest 29; peer @react-native/jest-preset ^0.86.3; react-test-renderer 19.2.3).

findings.topic: Corepack removed from Node 25+; how to pin pnpm
findings.detail: Node TSC voted to stop distributing Corepack; it ships with Node 14.19 up to but NOT including 25.0.0. Node 24 LTS still bundles it, but do not depend on it. Pin via package.json `"packageManager": "pnpm@12.4.2"` (and optionally `devEngines.packageManager`), and in CI use pnpm/action-setup@v4 which reads packageManager. Locally: `npm i -g pnpm@12` or `corepack enable` only on Node 24. Add `.node-version` = 24 (works with fnm/volta/asdf; .nvmrc duplicate optional).

findings.topic: Expo + pnpm monorepo compatibility (SDK 57)
findings.detail: Expo docs (updated 2026-09-03): first-class monorepo support for Bun, npm, pnpm, Yarn v1/Berry. SDK 52+: `expo/metro-config` configures Metro for monorepos automatically; delete legacy `watchFolders`, `resolver.nodeModulesPaths`, `extraNodeModules`, `disableHierarchicalLookup` from metro.config.js and run `npx expo start --clear`. SDK 54+: isolated (non-hoisted) pnpm installs officially supported; Expo Autolinking unified so 'the native code you link is from the same packages whose JS you bundle'. Fallback if a native module misbehaves under isolated installs: set `nodeLinker: hoisted` in pnpm-workspace.yaml. SDK 56 additionally made Expo compatible with global virtual stores (pnpm/Bun), saving ~300 MB per duplicate Expo install. Net: no `node-linker=hoisted` requirement any more; start isolated (pnpm default), keep hoisted as the documented escape hatch.

findings.topic: Expo SDK 57 facts
findings.detail: SDK 57 released 2026-06-30: React Native 0.86 (no intended breaking changes vs 0.85), React 19.2, Xcode 26.4+ required, iOS deployment target 16.4+, `expo prebuild` now clears and regenerates native dirs by default, opt-in iOS 27 scene lifecycle via `ios.enableSceneSupport` (expo-build-properties, expo@57.0.23+). Hermes V1 regressions fixed in 57.0.9 and 57.0.17 (pin >=57.0.17). SDK 56 (2026-05-21): expo-widgets stable, Live Activities/Widgets no longer need pre-rendering, TypeScript 6.0.3 expected. SDK 57 expects typescript ~6.0.3; TypeScript 7.0.2 breaks `app.config.ts` loading (expo/expo#47627, opened 2026-07-08, fix PR #47759 'needs review'; workaround app.config.js). Apple requires Xcode 26+ for App Store Connect uploads since 2026-04-28; default EAS image already uses Xcode 26.

findings.topic: Package manager + orchestration comparison
findings.detail: Turborepo 2.11: task graph + content-hash caching on top of pnpm workspaces, minimal config (turbo.json), Vercel remote cache optional (OIDC via vercel/setup-turborepo-remote-cache-action or TURBO_TOKEN/TURBO_TEAM) or actions/cache on `.turbo`. Nx: stronger for polyglot/large repos (affected graph, generators, distributed execution) but 'wants to own your workflow'; overkill for 4 packages. Bun workspaces: fast install, rudimentary task runner, and Expo/Metro + wrangler toolchains are Node-first; not worth the deviation. Cloudflare's own monorepo docs reference pnpm workspaces + Turborepo (`turbo deploy -F <worker>`). Turborepo has no React Native-specific guide (the /guides/frameworks/react-native URL 404s); Expo's own docs are sufficient because Metro handles workspace resolution itself.

findings.topic: Workers testing: package rename, Vitest pin, DO helpers, known issues
findings.detail: @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (0.22.0) is deprecated in favour of @cloudflare/vitest-plugin (1.1.13); docs now say 'Vitest 4.1 or later' and config is `plugins: [cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath: './wrangler.jsonc' } })]`. BOTH packages peer on vitest ^4.1.0 (+ @vitest/runner, @vitest/snapshot ^4.1.0); with vitest 5.0.x the pool fails before any test runs (workers-sdk#15618 opened 2026-09-12, status 'In Progress', PR #15500). Action: pin `vitest@~4.1` in the pnpm catalog. `cloudflare:test` exports: runInDurableObject(stub, cb), runDurableObjectAlarm(stub) => Promise<boolean> (runs and removes scheduled alarm immediately), listDurableObjectIds(ns), createExecutionContext(), waitOnExecutionContext(ctx), createScheduledController(), createMessageBatch(queueName, msgs), getQueueResult(batch, ctx), applyD1Migrations(). Known issues: no V8 coverage (use Istanbul); fake timers do not affect KV/R2/cache simulators; dynamic import() inside default export / DO handlers unsupported (static imports only); WebSockets in DOs need `--max-workers=1 --no-isolate`; DO alarms are not reset between test runs and do not respect isolated storage (community-reported; design FlightTracker tests to explicitly `deleteAlarm()` in setup); consume all fetch/R2 bodies; use `using` for RPC results.

findings.topic: Mobile test runner: Jest vs Vitest
findings.detail: Expo's official unit-testing guide and jest-expo (57.0.5, Jest 29 via babel-jest ^29) remain the supported path; RNTL is 'tested to work with Jest'. Vitest-for-RN exists (vitest-native plugin, RNTL discussion #1142) but is community-maintained and Expo does not document it. Recommendation: Jest 29 + jest-expo + @testing-library/react-native in apps/mobile; Vitest 4.1 in packages/* and apps/api. Two runners is acceptable because the shared pure logic (delay model, flight-key normaliser, zod schemas) lives in packages/shared and is tested once under Vitest.

findings.topic: Lint/format: ESLint+Prettier vs Biome (2026 state)
findings.detail: Expo official: `npx expo lint` scaffolds eslint.config.js (flat config, SDK 53+) extending eslint-config-expo; Prettier via eslint-plugin-prettier/recommended. Biome 2.5 (2026-06-05): 500 rules, GritQL plugins, type-aware linting; React Native rules landed in 2.4.13 as NURSERY: noReactNativeLiteralColors, noReactNativeRawText, useReactNativePlatformComponents, noReactNativeDeepImports; noInlineStyles (2.4.9, nursery). Biome discussion #6788 'Add react-native support' closed 2026-08-15 'we shipped the relevant rules'. Turborepo guide recommends running Biome as a root task (`//#format-and-lint`) because it is fast enough that cache misses do not matter. typescript-eslint cannot use TS 7.0 (no API); irrelevant while repo is pinned to TS 6.0.x. Boring choice for Phase 0: ESLint 9 flat + Prettier 3, single root eslint.config.js with per-directory blocks (eslint-config-expo for apps/mobile, typescript-eslint recommended-type-checked for apps/api + packages). Revisit Biome once its RN rules leave nursery.

findings.topic: Typed API client: Hono RPC (hc) vs OpenAPI codegen
findings.detail: Hono RPC: server `export type AppType = typeof routes`; client `hc<AppType>(baseUrl, { fetch, headers })` works in React Native (plain typed fetch wrapper), status-code-typed responses via `c.json(body, 200)`, InferRequestType/InferResponseType helpers. Hard requirements: `strict: true` in BOTH tsconfigs; handlers must use async/await (not .then chains). Documented perf problem: type instantiation slows tsserver as routes grow; mitigations are (1) compile API types ahead of time (tsc -b with declaration emit, client imports .d.ts), (2) TypeScript project references, (3) split into multiple sub-app clients. @hono/zod-openapi (1.6.3, zod ^4) also supports `hc` typing but forces `createRoute`/OpenAPIHono style everywhere; hono-openapi (1.3.3) is middleware-style and validator-agnostic. Version-skew caveat: hono resolved by @hono/zod-openapi and by hono/client must be the same instance or inference breaks (use pnpm catalog + single hono version). Recommendation: `hono` + `@hono/zod-validator` + `hc` for Phase 0; add hono-openapi later ONLY for the public/MCP surface that needs a spec.

findings.topic: Cloudflare deploy path: wrangler-action vs Workers Builds
findings.detail: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4 (defaults to Wrangler v4): inputs apiToken, accountId, environment, command, secrets (newline list of names), workingDirectory, packageManager (auto-detected from lockfile; npm/yarn/pnpm/bun), wranglerVersion. Workers Builds (git integration): GitHub/GitLab, Free plan 3,000 build-min/month + 1 concurrent build, Paid 6,000 min + 6 concurrent, $0.005/min overage, 20-min timeout; monorepo support via per-Worker root directory, build watch paths, custom deploy command (e.g. `turbo deploy -F api`), `--env` for Wrangler environments, preview URLs; dashboard Worker name must match wrangler config name. Wrangler environments: `env.staging`/`env.production` in wrangler.jsonc deploy Workers named `<name>-staging`/`<name>-production`; bindings, vars and secrets are NON-inheritable and must be repeated per env; secrets via `wrangler secret put KEY --env staging` or `.dev.vars.staging`; deploy via `wrangler deploy --env staging` or CLOUDFLARE_ENV. API token scopes for CI (account-level): Workers Scripts Edit, Workers KV Storage Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, Queues Edit, Hyperdrive Edit (+ Account Settings Read; D1 Edit only if D1 is used). Recommendation: GitHub Actions + wrangler-action, because the deploy job must run `drizzle-kit migrate` against Neon BEFORE `wrangler deploy` and be gated by a GitHub Environment; Workers Builds cannot express that ordering with environment-scoped secrets.

findings.topic: Cloudflare platform pricing relevant to environments
findings.detail: Workers Free: 100k req/day, 10 ms CPU/invocation; DO with SQLite storage available on Free (100k DO req/day, 13,000 GB-s/day, 5M rows read/day, 100k rows written/day); Hyperdrive 100k queries/day; Queues 10k ops/day. Workers Paid: $5/month minimum; 10M req/month (+$0.30/M), 30M CPU-ms (+$0.02/M); DO 1M req/month (+$0.15/M), 400k GB-s (+$12.50/M GB-s), SQLite 25B rows read (+$0.001/M), 50M rows written (+$1.00/M); KV 10M reads (+$0.50/M); R2 10 GB free then $0.015/GB-month; Queues 1M ops (+$0.40/M); Hyperdrive unlimited. DO SQLite billing started January 2026. Staging and production can live in one Paid account as separate `-staging`/`-production` Workers; Phase 0 dev can run on Free but Queues/Hyperdrive daily caps make Paid ($5) the practical floor.

findings.topic: Neon (Postgres) pricing, branching, local dev
findings.detail: Free: $0, 100 CU-hours/project/month, 0.5 GB storage/project, 100 projects, 10 branches/project, autosuspend after 5 min (cannot be disabled), no card. Launch: $0.106/CU-hour, $0.35/GB-month, 10 branches included then $1.50/branch-month, autoscale to 16 CU, no monthly minimum. Scale: $0.222/CU-hour, 25 branches included. GitHub Actions: neondatabase/create-branch-action@v6 (inputs project_id, api_key required; branch_name, parent_branch, expires_at, suspend_timeout optional; outputs db_url, db_url_pooled, branch_id), plus delete-branch, reset-branch and schema-diff actions; needs NEON_API_KEY secret + NEON_PROJECT_ID variable. Neon Local (docker image neondatabase/neon_local) is a local proxy that creates an ephemeral branch on container start (PARENT_BRANCH_ID) and deletes it on stop, or pins a branch (BRANCH_ID); apps connect to localhost:5432. Hyperdrive local dev: set `CLOUDFLARE_HYPERDRIVE_LOCAL_CONNECTION_STRING_<BINDING>` env var (recommended, keeps creds out of wrangler.jsonc) or `localConnectionString`; `wrangler dev` bypasses Hyperdrive pooling/caching; `--remote` hits production DB (avoid). Drizzle + Hyperdrive: `drizzle-orm/node-postgres` with `pg` Client/Pool per request, `nodejs_compat` flag, hyperdrive binding; drizzle-kit uses a DIRECT Neon URL from env (not Hyperdrive) for generate/migrate; `drizzle-kit check` validates migration-history consistency and is CI-safe.

findings.topic: EAS pricing, build/update/workflows, GitHub Actions integration
findings.detail:
EAS plans: Free $0 (15 Android + 15 iOS builds/month, low-priority queue, EAS Update 1,000 MAU, 60 min Workflows); Starter $19/month ($45 build credit, 3,000 MAU); Production $199/month ($225 credit, 50,000 MAU, high-priority queue, 2 concurrent builds); Enterprise custom ($1,000 credit, 1M MAU). Per-build: Android medium $1 / large $2; iOS medium $2 / large $4. Peak-time queues can exceed 90 min. GitHub Actions: expo/expo-github-action@v8 with `token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}` (personal or robot access token), `eas build --platform all --profile

--non-interactive --no-wait`; EAS Update PR previews via the action's `preview` sub-action running `eas update --auto` which posts a QR-code comment (needs `pull-requests: write`). EAS Submit lands iOS in TestFlight and Android on the eas.json submit-profile track (internal); promotion to public is manual in both consoles. EAS Workflows (.eas/workflows/*.yml) offer prebuilt build/submit/update/fingerprint/maestro/testflight jobs and a GitHub App trigger; usable later for e2e (maestro job) without Mac runners on GitHub.

findings.topic: Expo app variants, dev client, EAS env vars
findings.detail: Official pattern: app.config.ts/js reads `process.env.APP_VARIANT` ('development' | 'preview' | default production) and sets name, ios.bundleIdentifier and android.package with `.dev` / `.preview` suffixes so all three install side by side; eas.json build profiles set `env.APP_VARIANT` (development: developmentClient true + distribution internal; preview: distribution internal, optional ios.simulator; production: minimal). Warning from docs: changing identifiers makes EAS CLI prompt for a new Android keystore and new iOS provisioning profile per variant. EAS environment variables: named environments development/preview/production selected by `"environment"` in the build profile; visibility Plain text / Sensitive / Secret (secret = build-time only, never for client protection); EXPO_PUBLIC_* is the only prefix inlined into the JS bundle. Development builds (expo-dev-client) are required because Taxiway needs custom native modules (Live Activities/WidgetKit, Glance/Wear OS); Expo Go is irrelevant after Phase 0.

findings.topic: Identifier immutability (irreversible decisions)
findings.detail: Apple App Store Connect: 'You can't change [Bundle ID] after you upload a build'; SKU cannot be changed after the app record is created (earlier than bundle ID). Android: application ID must have >=2 dot-separated segments, each starting with a letter, chars [a-zA-Z0-9_]; 'once you publish your app, you should never change the application ID' (Play treats it as a different app; same signing cert required). Recommendation: same reverse-DNS ID on both platforms, derived from the owned domain, no platform token in it (e.g. domain taxiway.app => `app.taxiway.mobile`, dev `app.taxiway.mobile.dev`, preview `app.taxiway.mobile.preview`; if domain is taxiway.io => `io.taxiway.mobile`). Avoid `app.taxiway.ios.dev` from the brief: baking the platform into the ID buys nothing and complicates RevenueCat/Firebase/deep-link config. Reserve the production ID in App Store Connect + Play Console before Phase 0 ends but do not upload a build until the domain is final.

findings.topic: GitHub Environments and secrets
findings.detail: Environments give environment-scoped secrets/vars (only jobs that reference the environment see them), required reviewers (up to 6 people/teams, one approval suffices, optional prevent-self-review), wait timers, and deployment branch/tag rules (e.g. only `main` may deploy to staging, only `v*` tags to production). Constraint: on GitHub Free, environments are only available for PUBLIC repositories; private repos need GitHub Pro (personal) or Team (org). If the repo is private under a Free plan, fall back to repository secrets + branch protection and lose required-reviewer gating.

findings.topic: GitHub Actions building blocks
findings.detail: pnpm/action-setup@v4 (reads packageManager; `cache: true` optional); actions/setup-node@v6 with `cache: pnpm` (pnpm cache supported v6.10+ of setup-node lineage); actions/checkout@v5/v6; Turborepo remote cache via vercel/setup-turborepo-remote-cache-action@v1 (OIDC, needs id-token: write) or actions/cache@v4 on `.turbo` keyed by SHA; Turbo's own guide still shows older action majors (pnpm/action-setup@v3, setup-node@v4) so use the newer majors above.

findings.topic: E2E: Maestro vs Detox (defer)
findings.detail: Maestro: black-box, YAML flows, accessibility-layer driven, minimal native setup, first-class `maestro` job in EAS Workflows. Detox: gray-box, deeper sync, officially supports New Architecture for RN 0.77–0.84 (RN 0.86 support unverified; open issues on 0.81.x sync/deadlocks). Recommendation: no e2e in Phase 0; when added (Phase 2+), Maestro on EAS Workflows or a macOS GitHub runner against a simulator build from the preview profile.

findings.topic: Repo hygiene tooling
findings.detail: Renovate: `config:recommended` + `group:monorepos` groups sibling packages (e.g. all expo-*, all @cloudflare/*), schedule outside working hours, `automerge: true, automergeType: branch` for devDependencies and well-tested minor/patch; keep expo SDK bumps manual (SDK upgrades are coordinated via `npx expo install --fix`). Conventional Commits + commitlint (unverified specifics, from memory: @commitlint/config-conventional). MADR 4.0.0 (2024-09-17) ADR template sections: Context and Problem Statement; Decision Drivers; Considered Options; Decision Outcome; Consequences; Confirmation; Pros and Cons of the Options; More Information; YAML front matter status/date/decision-makers. Changesets: not needed (no published packages; apps version via app.json/EAS and wrangler deploys). CODEOWNERS: single owner in Phase 0; still add the file so review routing exists when contributors arrive.

findings.topic: Third-party accounts and costs for Phase 0
findings.detail: Apple Developer Program: US$99/year; organization enrollment needs a D-U-N-S number (free, ~5 business days via D&B), individual does not. Google Play Console: US$25 one-time; identity verification (government ID + card); organization accounts need D-U-N-S (up to 30 days); PERSONAL accounts created after 2023-11-13 must run a closed test with >=12 testers continuously opted in for 14 days (and, per 2026 practice, genuinely using the app) before production access. Sentry: Developer plan free (5,000 errors, unlimited projects, ONE user); Team $26/month billed annually (50k errors). RevenueCat: free up to $2,500 monthly tracked revenue, then 1% of MTR (can wait). Neon: free tier sufficient for Phase 0. Cloudflare: Workers Paid $5/month recommended. Expo/EAS: free tier (15+15 builds) sufficient for Phase 0 if builds are gated to tags/manual, not per-PR. GitHub: Team plan needed for environments on a private repo (price not verified here). AeroDataBox and FlightAware AeroAPI keys are covered by the provider research track.
